title: [ROCm] Fix cu_seqlens_q off-by-one in AITER FA speculative decode path
author: Bortlesboat
body:
In the speculative decode path of `AiterFlashAttentionImpl` (when `decode_max_query_len > 1`), `cu_seqlens_q` is sliced as `query_start_loc[:num_decodes]`, giving `num_decodes` elements. But `cu_seqlens_q` for `unified_attention` is a cumulative length array that needs `num_seqs + 1` entries (including the leading 0).

The correct pattern is already used in the fallback path 33 lines later (line 1228-1229), which correctly does `[:num_decodes + 1]`.

Also fixed `descale_shape` which computed `shape[0] - 1` on the wrong-length slice, producing `num_decodes - 1` instead of `num_decodes`. Simplified to use `num_decodes` directly, matching line 1232.

No duplicate PRs found.

Testing:
- `uvx pre-commit run ruff-format --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_aiter_fa.py` (passes locally)
- Previous CI failure only requested the matching `ruff format` whitespace change on this line; this follow-up commit applies that exact diff.

AI assistance was used for code search and CI log review; all changes reviewed by the human submitter.


**Reference:** The correct `cu_seqlens_q` slicing is confirmed by the upstream AITER `unified_attention` implementation:
https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/bc5ea32c19c604cda2f4781a97cb04d5fc494543/aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/attention/unified_attention.py#L426

title: [Bugfix] Fix extract_hidden_states crash with quantized KV cache dtype
author: yubofredwang
body:
## Purpose

When `kv_cache_dtype` is set to a quantized type (e.g. `fp8_e4m3`), `ExtractHiddenStatesModel` passes the global `cache_config` directly to `CacheOnlyAttentionLayer`, which only supports `auto`/`bfloat16`/`float16` and crashes with an AssertionError.

`CacheOnlyAttentionLayer` stores intermediate hidden states for the `extract_hidden_states` speculative decoding method — it does not store actual KV projections, so quantized cache dtypes are not applicable.

This fix creates a shallow copy of `cache_config` with `cache_dtype` reset to `"auto"` (resolves to the model's native dtype) before passing it to the hidden-states cache layer, while leaving the target model's KV cache quantization unchanged.

Tested locally

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Size arange_buffer to max_num_batched_tokens to prevent CUDA IMA
author: UranusSeven
body:
Hi from [novita.ai](https://novita.ai/) team 👋

## Purpose

Fix a CUDA illegal memory access (IMA) crash in the MLA indexer's decode flattening path when using data parallelism + speculative decoding (MTP).

### What changed

`arange_buffer` in `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` was allocated with size `max_num_seqs * next_n`, while the other flattening buffers (`expanded_seq_lens_buffer`, `expanded_block_table_buffer`) correctly use `max_num_batched_tokens`. During CUDAGraph dummy runs on idle DP groups, stale `query_start_loc` entries for padded requests inflate `actual_expanded` beyond `max_num_seqs * next_n`, causing a silent out-of-bounds GPU write.

### Why

1. `execute_dummy_batch` creates a 1-request dummy batch but `_build_attention_metadata` uses `num_reqs_padded` (CUDAGraph bucket size).
2. `query_start_loc` is only populated for the 1 real request; padded indices retain stale values from previous real batches.
3. `split_decodes_and_prefills` classifies all padded requests as decodes (since `max_query_len <= decode_threshold` with spec decode).
4. The flattening path computes `actual_expanded = sum(decode_lens)` over all padded requests, yielding values far exceeding the buffer size.
5. `self.arange_buffer[:actual_expanded]` writes out-of-bounds → CUDA IMA surfacing asynchronously at the next sync point.

## Test Plan

Tested with GLM-5-FP8 on 8× H200:
```bash
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5-FP8 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp \
  --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

## Test Result

- **Before fix**: Server crashes with CUDA IMA soon under load (1000 requests, avg 10K prompt tokens)
- **After fix**: Server ran 85+ minutes stable under the same benchmark load with zero errors

title: fix: clamp NaN/Inf in topk_softmax to prevent duplicate expert IDs
author: jhaotingc
body:
### Purpose
Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39244

Fix CUDA illegal memory access crash when serving MoE models (e.g., Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8) with FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE and CUDA graphs at high concurrency on H200.

CUDA graph replay pads the batch to the nearest capture size. Padded tokens have degenerate hidden states that produce NaN gating logits. The `topkGating` kernel's softmax outputs all-NaN, and the argmax loop picks expert 0 for every top-k slot (IEEE 754: `NaN > NaN` is false), producing duplicate expert IDs `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]`. These duplicates trigger an uninitialized-memory bug in FlashInfer's three-step MoE sort, causing `finalizeMoeRoutingKernel` to dereference wild pointers.

The fix clamps NaN/Inf values to 0 after softmax/sigmoid scoring in `topkGating`, before the argmax selection loop. With all-zero scores, argmax picks unique experts `[0,1,2,...,k-1]` via index tie-breaking. Zero performance overhead.

### Test Plan

- Kernel unit test: verify `topk_softmax` produces unique expert IDs for NaN/Inf/normal gating inputs
- Kernel microbenchmark: compare eager + CUDA graph replay latency for normal vs NaN inputs (batch 1-512, 128/256 experts)
- End-to-end: serve Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP=4, EP=4, CUDA graphs, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=1`) with 8 concurrent requests
- Full sweep: sglang benchmark conc 1-512, ISL=1600, OSL=600, REPEAT=5 on 4x H200

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py::test_fused_topk_nan_inf_clamp`


### Test Result

**Kernel correctness** (H200):

| Input | Before fix | After fix |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| normal | unique IDs | unique IDs (unchanged) |
| all_nan | `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]` (512/512 dup) | `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]` (0 dup) |
| all_inf | `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]` (512/512 dup) | `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]` (0 dup) |

**Kernel perf** (H200, CUDA graph replay, median of 1000 runs):

| Batch | Experts | normal (us) | all_nan (us) | diff |
|-------|---------|------------|-------------|------|
| 1 | 128 | 8.29 | 8.22 | -0.8% |
| 128 | 128 | 8.26 | 8.32 | +0.8% |
| 512 | 128 | 8.51 | 8.64 | +1.5% |
| 512 | 256 | 8.90 | 8.93 | +0.4% |

All within noise. Zero measurable overhead.

**End-to-end** (4x H200, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8):

| Test | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| 8 concurrent curl | 5/8 OK, 3/8 crash | 8/8 HTTP 200 |
| sweep conc 1-512 | crash at conc 16+ | all pass |


**unit test**

| State | Kernel | Test result |
|---|---|---|
| BEFORE  | partial fix | 60 failed, 12 passed |
| AFTER  — all three clamps active | full fix | **72 passed** |

## Summary

vLLM crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` when serving Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=1` and CUDA graphs enabled. The crash occurs at high concurrency (8+ requests) when the MoE batch size exceeds 256 tokens.

## Root Cause

CUDA graph replay pads the batch to the nearest capture size (e.g., 300 real tokens padded to 512). Padded tokens have stale/degenerate hidden states that produce **NaN gating logits** in the MoE router. The `topk_softmax` CUDA kernel then produces **duplicate expert IDs** for NaN inputs (e.g., `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]` for every padded token), because IEEE 754 `NaN > NaN` is always false, so the argmax never updates from expert 0, and the `-10000` zeroing of the winner also fails (`-10000 > NaN` is false).

These duplicate expert IDs trigger a latent bug in FlashInfer's `blockExpertPrefixSumKernel` (three-step MoE sort path, used when num_tokens > 256): it uses `break` after the first expert match, so duplicate expert slots leave `unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row` entries uninitialized. `finalizeMoeRoutingKernel` then reads garbage values as row indices, causing wild pointer dereferences.

### Chain of events

```
CUDA graph replay with padded tokens
  -> stale hidden states -> NaN gating logits
    -> topk_softmax produces [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] for padded tokens
      -> duplicate expert IDs enter cutlass_fused_moe (num_tokens > 256)
        -> blockExpertPrefixSumKernel skips duplicate slots (break)
          -> unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row has uninitialized entries
            -> finalizeMoeRoutingKernel reads garbage -> OOB -> CRASH
```

### Why it only happens with CUDA graphs

In eager mode, there are no padded tokens -- the batch contains only real tokens with valid hidden states, the router produces unique expert IDs, and the three-step sort works correctly. The crash requires:
1. Batch size > 256 (three-step sort path)
2. Duplicate expert IDs (from NaN gating on padded tokens)

Both conditions only occur together during CUDA graph replay at high concurrency.

## Fix

Clamp NaN/Inf values to 0 in `topk_softmax` after softmax/sigmoid scoring, before the argmax selection loop:

```cpp
// csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu, after line 443
#pragma unroll
for (int ii = 0; ii < VPT; ++ii) {
    if (isnan(row_chunk[ii]) || isinf(row_chunk[ii])) {
        row_chunk[ii] = 0.f;
    }
}
```

With all-zero scores, the argmax uses index tie-breaking to pick unique experts `[0,1,2,...,k-1]`, preventing duplicates. Normal (non-NaN) inputs are unaffected -- the clamp is a no-op.

### Why this is the right fix location

The `topk_softmax` kernel (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu:266`) is where the NaN propagates into duplicate expert IDs. Fixing it here:
- Prevents the bad input from reaching ANY downstream MoE kernel (FlashInfer, Triton, etc.)
- Zero performance overhead (see benchmarks below)
- Handles all NaN sources (CUDA graph padding, numerical overflow, any future degenerate input)

## Performance Impact

Benchmarked on H200, production MoE configs (128/256 experts, top_k=8). The fix adds `isnan`/`isinf` checks (single PTX predicate instructions) per element. The kernel is memory-bandwidth bound, so the extra comparisons are invisible:

### Eager mode (us, median of 1000 runs)

| Batch | Experts | normal | all_nan | diff |
|-------|---------|--------|---------|------|
| 1     | 128     | 10.94  | 10.91   | -0.3% |
| 8     | 128     | 10.72  | 10.72   | 0.0% |
| 32    | 128     | 10.72  | 10.75   | +0.3% |
| 128   | 128     | 10.72  | 10.66   | -0.6% |
| 256   | 128     | 10.78  | 10.72   | -0.6% |
| 512   | 128     | 10.66  | 10.69   | +0.3% |
| 512   | 256     | 10.72  | 10.72   | 0.0% |

### CUDA graph replay mode (us, median of 1000 runs)

| Batch | Experts | normal | all_nan | diff |
|-------|---------|--------|---------|------|
| 1     | 128     | 8.29   | 8.22    | -0.8% |
| 8     | 128     | 8.19   | 8.16    | -0.4% |
| 32    | 128     | 8.29   | 8.19    | -1.2% |
| 128   | 128     | 8.26   | 8.32    | +0.8% |
| 256   | 128     | 8.32   | 8.32    | 0.0% |
| 512   | 128     | 8.51   | 8.64    | +1.5% |
| 512   | 256     | 8.90   | 8.93    | +0.4% |

All differences are within noise (<2%). **Zero measurable overhead.**

## Verification

### Standalone (topk kernel)

Before fix:
```
all_nan: dup_tokens=512/512  topk_ids=[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]
all_inf: dup_tokens=512/512  topk_ids=[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]
```

After fix:
```
all_nan: dup_tokens=0/512  topk_ids=[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
all_inf: dup_tokens=0/512  topk_ids=[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix V1 dummy run writing NaN to KV cache null block
author: elvircrn
body:
## Summary

- V1's `_dummy_run` (used by idle DP ranks in DP+EP) calls `_get_slot_mappings`, which reads from a persistent `slot_mapping` buffer initialized with `torch.zeros`. The real-token region `[0:num_tokens_unpadded]` retains value **0**, mapping to block 0 offset 0 — the **null block**. The `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel sees `slot_idx=0 >= 0` and writes garbage hidden states (often NaN) into the null block.
- This corrupts block 0, which is referenced by all unused block table entries. Downstream attention reads from block 0 for padding positions, propagating NaN through the model.
- Fix: fill all slot mappings with `-1` (PAD_SLOT_ID) after `_get_slot_mappings` returns in `_dummy_run`, so `concat_and_cache` kernels skip the KV write entirely. This matches V2's `get_dummy_slot_mappings` behavior which already does `self.slot_mappings.fill_(PAD_SLOT_ID)`.

## Root cause

Introduced by #25954 (Jan 24, 2026) which refactored slot mappings into a standalone `_get_slot_mappings()` called unconditionally in `_dummy_run` and passed via `set_forward_context(slot_mapping=...)`. Before that PR, slot mappings were only set up inside `_build_attention_metadata` (conditional on FULL cudagraph mode), so dummy runs on idle DP ranks wouldn't always trigger KV cache writes.

## Impact

Affects all V1 deployments using DP with EP (e.g., DeepSeek R1/V3 with `data_parallel_size > 1` and `expert_parallel_size > 1`). Quantization-agnostic — FP8, NVFP4, and BF16 are all affected. Observed as accuracy regression (97% → 55%) on DeepSeek R1 NVFP4.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified via KV cache NaN instrumentation on a live DeepSeek R1 NVFP4 deployment: `slot_mapping=[0]` confirmed before fix, `slot_mapping=[-1]` after fix, NaN in block 0 eliminated
- [ ] `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -v` (no dummy run slot mapping tests exist yet)
- [ ] lm_eval accuracy check on DeepSeek R1 with DP+EP

title: [Bugfix] Fix tensor shape mismatch in sparse attention with speculative decoding
author: santiramos27
body:
## Purpose

Fixes two tensor shape mismatches in sparse_indexer.py that cause RuntimeError when running DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 with MTP and padded decode batches.

A previous refactor here correctly sliced `decode_metadata.seq_lens` to `batch_size` for `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, but missed two downstream consumers that still used the unsliced tensor or the raw `num_decode_tokens` count:

**Fix 1: persistent_topk receiving wrong seq_lens**

persistent_topk was called with the full `decode_metadata.seq_lens` while logits and topk_indices were sized based on `batch_size * next_n.` The kernel used the unsliced seq_lens to determine output rows, producing a result with fewer rows than topk_indices expected.

 **Fix 2: topk_indices_buffer write-back after unpack_seq_triton**

After unpacking padded topk results, the code assigned back into `topk_indices_buffer[:num_decode_tokens]`. But num_decode_tokens is the total token count before packing, while unpack_seq_triton returns `sum(decode_lens)` rows — which is smaller when `requires_padding=True` (i.e. when short chunked prefills fall below the decode threshold). The write-back now uses `topk_indices.shape[0]` to match the actual unpacked size.

When does this trigger?

The bug surfaces specifically when all three conditions are met:
  - Speculative decoding is active (MTP/EAGLE), so next_n > 1
  - `requires_padding=True` — happens when a chunked prefill shorter than the decode threshold gets mixed into the decode batch
  - The padded batch size differs from the raw decode token count

Without speculative decoding (next_n=1) or without padding, the sizes happen to align and the bug is latent.

Error seen:
```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (104) must match the existing size (98) at non-singleton dimension 0. Target sizes: [104, 2048]. Tensor sizes: [98, 2048] at sparse_indexer.py:168
```

## Test Plan
- Verified on B300 with DeepSeek-V3.2 (MTP next_n=2, next_n=4) using gsm8k eval for correctness

Without MTP

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Fix silent weight corruption with buffer-reusing iterators
author: pedramr
body:
## Summary

`ModelForPooling.load_weights` uses `(*seen_weights, *weights)` which eagerly
consumes the entire iterator at generator creation time. With runai_streamer
(`RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT=0`), the shared I/O buffer is overwritten before
tensors are consumed, silently corrupting all pooling/embedding model weights.

Fix: `itertools.chain` for lazy iteration, `.clone()` on probed weights so
packed-weight remapping (q/k/v_proj -> qkv_proj) survives reuse.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_pooling_load_weights_with_buffer_reuse` — guards `itertools.chain` fix
- [x] `test_pooling_load_weights_clones_probed_weights` — guards `.clone()` via packed-weight remapping
- [x] Both tests FAIL without fix, PASS with fix
- [x] Partial fix (chain only, no clone) → first passes, second fails
- [x] `pytest tests/models/test_adapters.py` — CPU-only, no model downloads
- [x] Verified end-to-end on GPU with embedding model + `runai_streamer` `MEMORY_LIMIT=0`: bit-for-bit identical embeddings vs ground truth

title: [Bugfix][Kernel][ROCm] Fix triton_w4a16 scales mismatch when BLOCK_K > group_size
author: JartX
body:
The Triton W4A16 GEMM kernel (triton_w4a16_gemm_kernel) loads quantization
scales and zero points from a single group index per BLOCK_K tile, but the
kernel launcher does not enforce BLOCK_K <= group_size. When BLOCK_K
exceeds group_size, a single tile spans multiple scale groups, but only the
first group's scales are applied to all rows in the tile. This silently
corrupts the dequantized weights in the tail rows.

In real-world use cases, this was reflected in agent tool calls within contexts exceeding 10K tokens. Typically, the model would start calling tools in a loop with the same arguments or perform the same task multiple times.

In other instances, it would leave the task unfinished, or—in the case of coding agents—start deleting relevant code or hallucinating the instructions.

Following the fix, the model now functions correctly and consistently with its capacity; in this case: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32.

I should clarify that I previously assumed this behavior was inherent to the model because, while working with ROCm RDNA3, I was forced to use Group Size with float16 dtype for the ExLlamaLinearKernel, which only worked passably.

Now, with the kernel introduced in PR #37352 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37352), I can execute in bfloat16. I initially noticed the model was failing even more than with the ExLlamaLinearKernel, but after reviewing the code, I found the error in my specific use case.

After correcting it, I can run Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-W4A16-G32 much more efficiently. Beyond the performance gain, the model now hardly ever makes mistakes and works with much greater precision.

Thanks to @jatseng-ai and @tjtanaa for the kernel!

title: [MRv2]fix: model accuracy regression caused by reusing the stale last_sampled_tokens and draft_tokens
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Summary
- Fix ~13% GSM8K accuracy regression in PD disaggregation caused by stale `last_sampled_tokens` and `draft_tokens` leaking between requests when V2 model runner reuses request state slots
- In `add_request()`, initialize `last_sampled_tokens` to the last computed token and zero out `draft_tokens`

## Root Cause
In PD disagg, the decode side receives requests with `num_computed_tokens == prefill_len` (fully prefilled). The first iteration is a decode step — no prefill step runs to initialize `last_sampled_tokens` via `postprocess()`. The `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` kernel reads the stale value from a previous request that occupied the same slot.

**Bug location:** `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py:add_request()`

## Test plan
- [x] GSM8K score restored: V2+fix = 0.94 (V1 baseline = 0.93, V2 before fix = 0.82)
- [x] Verified with full GSM8K eval at concurrency=32 on Crusoe GB200 NVL72

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Resolve MoRI connector hangs at high concurrency
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #40340.

There are a few parts of the MoRI-IO connector code that can cause indefinite hangs of the connector. This PR resolves them so we can run at least 512 concurrency requests, both for READ and WRITE modes.

Co-developed with @ichbinblau @chunfangamd

### Implementation details

<details> <summary> Click to expand </summary>

1. Disable MoRI's in-band notifications (set `enable_notification=False` in `RdmaBackendConfig`) as we use ZMQ for completion notifications anyhow, and under high concurrency those notifications poison the transfer statuses because the QP send queue is exhausted (causing requests to be stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`).
1. Handle `Failed()` transfers in _pop_done_transfers so prefill frees its blocks. These were otherwise stuck in `_recving_transfers` forever.
1. Keep transfer_id<->request_id mapping on the producer side until the transfer has been marked as completed (finished_sending or notification from decode). Otherwise no requests are marked as done sending and hence are not freed by the scheduler from `get_finished` (except in the backup free-er in `update_connector_output`) 
1. Reap KV blocks after (configurable) deadline for finished request that have not been notified to free the blocks for instance due to `ibv_post_send` failures.
1. (WRITE mode only) fix race condition caused by mismatch between when requests are added to  `transfer_id_to_request_id` and when requests are popped using `pop_finished_write_req_ids`.
1. (READ mode only) Don't report READ requests on D side as part of `done_recving` since these requests are scheduled as RUNNING immediately (and specifically never as WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS). This otherwise triggers an assertion error
1. Replace `status.Wait() ` infinite busy-spin with polling w/ deadline. 
1. Add 1ms sleep in busy-spin `while True` loops
1. Fix mismatches between when request ids and transfer ids are  used throughout the code.

</details>

```dockerfile
# docker/Dockerfile.rocm_dev
ARG BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:local
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

# RDMA userspace libraries required by MoRI-IO.
# libibverbs/librdmacm may already be present in the base image;
# apt-get is idempotent so this is safe either way.
RUN apt-get update -q -y && apt-get install -q -y \
        librdmacm1 \
        libibverbs1 \
        ibverbs-providers \
        ibverbs-utils \
        libibverbs-dev \
        autoconf \
        libtool \
        unzip \
        wget \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Remove the pre-installed bnxt-rocelib 235.x userspace libraries and apt
# package so they don't conflict with the older 230.x build below.
RUN apt-get update -q -y \
    && apt-get remove -y bnxt-rocelib 2>/dev/null || true \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && find /usr/local/lib /usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
         /usr/lib /usr/lib64 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
         -name "libbnxt_re*" -delete 2>/dev/null || true \
    && rm -f /etc/libibverbs.d/bnxt_re.driver 2>/dev/null || true \
    && ldconfig


# Thor2 (Broadcom BCM5760x) RDMA user-space driver (libbnxt_re).
# The inbox libbnxt_re-rdmav*.so shipped by libibverbs is renamed so the
# vendor build takes precedence via libibverbs provider discovery.
RUN wget -q \
        https://docs.broadcom.com/docs-and-downloads/ethernet-network-adapters/NXE/Thor2/GCA1/bcm5760x_230.2.52.0a.zip \
    && unzip -q bcm5760x_230.2.52.0a.zip \
    && cd bcm5760x_230.2.52.0a/drivers_linux/bnxt_rocelib/ \
    && tar -xf "$(find . -name 'libbnxt*.tar.gz' | head -n 1)" \
    && cd "$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'libbnxt*' ! -name '*.tar.gz' | head -n 1)" \
    && sh autogen.sh \
    && ./configure \
    && make \
    && make install all \
    && echo /usr/local/lib >> /etc/ld.so.conf \
    && ldconfig \
    && cp -f bnxt_re.driver /etc/libibverbs.d/ \
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /bcm5760x_230.2.52.0a /bcm5760x_230.2.52.0a.zip
```

    -t ghcr.io/simondanielsson/vllm-rocm-moriio:dev-hang-fixes \

```

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Fix ECExampleConnector load device under TP>1
author: miyakido
body:
## Summary

`ECExampleConnector.start_load_caches` passed the bare device string `"cuda"`
to `safetensors.torch.load_file`. Safetensors resolves that to `cuda:0`, even
when a tensor-parallel worker is running on another selected device.

Under `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, a non-rank-0 worker could therefore load the
encoder cache on `cuda:0` and later fail when combining it with tensors on its
local device. This was reproduced on vLLM v0.17.0 with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct,
TP=4, and 4 x L4 GPUs.

## Fix

Pin CUDA-like loads to the device selected by vLLM's platform abstraction:

```python
device = current_platform.device_type
if current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
    device = f"{device}:{current_platform.current_device()}"
```

The platform abstraction keeps this compatible with CUDA-like backends, while
non-CUDA platforms continue to receive their unchanged `device_type`.

Two regression tests cover both paths:

- CUDA-like platforms load onto the selected device (for example, `cuda:2`).
- Non-CUDA platforms keep the bare platform device type.

## Validation

- [x] GitHub `pre-commit` workflow passes on the amended commit.
- [x] `check-torch-cuda-call`, Ruff check/format, and mypy 3.12 pass locally on
      the changed files.
- [x] The repository's manual-stage hook suite passes locally, excluding the
      Docker graph hook and Linux-only non-root entrypoint check on macOS.
- [ ] Full CI: [Buildkite #82780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82780)
      (running).

The focused pytest file could not be rerun in the current macOS ARM environment
because vLLM does not publish a compatible precompiled wheel for that platform;
the regression tests are included in the requested Linux/GPU CI run.

## Checks

- [x] No matching open PR was found for this EC connector device-placement bug.
- [x] The fix includes targeted regression coverage.
- [x] AI assistance was used: Claude (Anthropic) assisted with the original
      investigation and test scaffolding; Codex (OpenAI) fixed the lint failure,
      updated validation, and prepared the amended commit. The author reviewed
      and validated the original change. AI co-author trailers are included in
      the commit.

title: [Bugfix][CPU][RISC-V] Clamp exp() input to prevent NaN
author: lyd1992
body:
FP32Vec16::exp() in cpu_types_riscv_impl.hpp produced NaN for large inputs because -inf * 0.0 = NaN in IEEE 754 after the polynomial underflows. Clamp input to [-87.33, 88.72] before polynomial evaluation.

Discovered while debugging softmax NaN in the RVV attention path.

title: [Bugfix] Changed speech to text chunk timestamp to cumulative approach
author: TobyB1702
body:
## Purpose
Fix related to issue: #32588 

The bug occurs when transcribing long audio (> 30s) using vLLM whisper, the timestamps of which become increasingly inaccurate (up to 1s per chunk). This happens because the old approach assumes split_audio cuts exactly at 30s, but actually will search within 1-second window before the expected value. So it could land anywhere within that, 29.2 or 29.8 for example. This means the error accumulates and after 10 chunks you could be ~5s off. 

The fix is to switch to a cumulative approach, so each chunk we add to where the last chunk ended. So we simply pass the sum to start time.  

This fix also sets seek in TranscriptionSegment to an int instead of a float in prototcol.py as seek position can be rounded down

AI (Claude Code) was used for understanding and some code generation

## Test Plan

the full command line to reproduce
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_chunk_timestamp_offset.py -v`

The test doesn't exist on main branch so the easiest way is to bring across mains serving.py and rerun to see the failed result. I did this by

title: [Bugfix] Fix token loss in PP mode which causes degraded accuracy
author: starkwj
body:
## Purpose **Issue:** The current PP mode causes degraded accuracy with concurrent requests. gsm8k results with Qwen3-8B, num_concurrent 256:   | gsm8k (strict-match) -- | -- TP | 0.8741 PP 2 + no-async-scheduling | 0.8757 PP 2 (num_concurrent 2) | 0.8741 PP 2 | **0.8324** Maybe related issue - #28839 - #38903 **Root cause** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de3da0b97cd9db8b1d429312992a5759c89ef881/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L1338-L1347 In *gpu_model_runner.py*, the `num_tokens_no_spec` should indicate the number of current tokens without spec. However, in `_update_states` with PP mode, the above code incorrectly updates it to `num_computed_tokens`. For chunked prefill, the `num_computed_tokens` is the number of current computed chunked prompts, which is less than the number of total prompts (i.e., the real `num_tokens_no_spec`). And in *chunked prefill*, the index to update `token_ids_cpu` is incorrect too, as it is less than `num_prompts`. What this code does in chunked prefill: - In async-scheduling, `new_token_ids` is empty, so `token_ids_cpu` not touched. - In no-async-scheduling, `new_token_ids` is the chunk needs to be computed, and `token_ids_cpu` is covered with the same prompt chunk, so it's also meaningless. This is correct in `_bookkeeping_sync`, where it works in non-PP mode and for the last rank in PP mode, as shown below. And actually, in chunked prefill, the below operations are skipped due to no valid sampled tokens (filtered by `discard_request_mask`).
code in _bookkeeping_sync https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de3da0b97cd9db8b1d429312992a5759c89ef881/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3453-L3463
Then, in `_update_states`, `condense()` is called, which reorders requests in the input batch, moves the valid requests at the tail to the empty slots at the front. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de3da0b97cd9db8b1d429312992a5759c89ef881/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L711-L724 As shown above, tokens are copied to the empty slot. However, the `num_tokens` is calculated with `num_tokens_no_spec`. **Thus, with the incorrect update in `_update_states`, it only copies `num_computed_tokens` tokens rather than all prompt tokens, and the remaining prompt tokens are lost (replaced by invalid tokens in the empty slot).**
The code is also incorrect for no-async-scheduling. Why its score of gsm8k seems normal? In no-async-scheduling, for each deocde step, the request is removed from input_batch due to `unscheduled` and re-add_request to input_batch before `condense()`. The `add_request` will add the request to empty slot first, leaving less empty slots at the front, thus greatly reduce the occurrences of swaps in `condense()`. However, it still has probability for this bug, especially when prompts are long and `max-num-batched-tokens` are relatively small.
This PR fixes the incorrect update in `_update_states`, adopts code logic similar to that in `_bookkeeping_sync`. ## Test Plan lm_eval with gsm8k ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions --model_args "model=qwen,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=256,max_length=40960" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 ``` Also benched performance, no changes were observed. ## Test Result before: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8370|± |0.0102| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8324|± |0.0103| after: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8855|± |0.0088| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8772|± |0.0090| and does not affect no-async-ascheduling: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8810|± |0.0089| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8757|± |0.0091| ---

## Purpose
Effective tuning for the fused_moe_triton kernel seems crucial. An optimal .json can results in +15% speedup for GLM4.7-Flash model on gfx1100. title: [Bugfix][Hybrid][NemotronH] Fix mamba_cache_mode=all + speculative decoding crash
author: roikoren755
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the chain of three bugs reported in #39809 that crash NemotronH (and other hybrid Mamba2) models when prefix caching `all` mode is combined with speculative decoding.

This PR also reverts the temporary workaround merged in #40454.

### Evaluation

Verified end-to-end with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super using a shared few-shot prefix to exercise the cache. The full `(PC-off, PC-align, PC-all) × (CUDA graphs, --enforce-eager)` matrix all land at ~92% accuracy, confirming `PC all + SpecDec` is correctness-equivalent to the existing baselines. The logs also show a prefix cache hit rate of around 75%, for both `align` and `all` modes.

### Solution overview

The three issues share a root cause: in `mamba_cache_mode='all'` + spec decode the kernel reads/writes `1 + num_speculative_blocks` consecutive state slots per request, but the surrounding bookkeeping treated the block table and per-request indices as if no speculative slots were reserved. Concretely:

1. `state_indices_tensor_d` is now sized to `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size) + num_speculative_blocks` so each request's block table addresses every slot the kernel actually touches. `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` and the `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` docstring updated to match.
2. The persistent `block_idx_last_*` buffers used during CUDA graph capture are now padded to `num_reqs` (matching how the kernel indexes them) instead of `num_decode_tokens`.
3. When fewer drafts are accepted than scheduled, the next step's read anchor must point to the slot the previous step actually wrote — `(num_computed - 1) // block_size` no longer matches because `num_computed` reflects only accepted tokens. Tracked per request in `mamba_state_idx` and plumbed to the kernel as `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step`.

## Test Plan

Two new regression tests added `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py`:
- test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks
- test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs

Both fail on main without this PR and pass with it.

End-to-end reproducer from #39809 on a 4×GB200 host:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode all \
--trust-remote-code \
--tensor-parallel-size 4 \
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

Sent the same long prompt twice and observed vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 2 passed, 0 failed.

```
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py::test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks PASSED
tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py::test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs PASSED
```

Without the fix:
- test_state_indices_tensor_d_includes_num_speculative_blocks fails with
`assert torch.Size([4, 16]) == (4, 18)`.
- test_block_idx_cudagraph_capture_padded_by_num_reqs fails with
`assert torch.Size([4]) == (3,)`.

E2E: server starts cleanly, completions are factually correct, no crash. With duplicate sends of a >4224-token prompt, `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` increments as expected (8448 cached tokens / 10926 prompt tokens, i.e. 2 full Mamba blocks worth on the second request).

title: [Bugfix] Prevent stale multiproc RPC deadlines from becoming unbounded waits
author: bugkeep
body:
## Summary

Prevents stale `MultiprocExecutor.collective_rpc()` deadlines from becoming
negative response-queue timeouts that can be misinterpreted as unbounded waits.

Supersedes #41213 (minimal inline clamp only) with a standalone
`_remaining_timeout()` helper, sync-path bypass of FutureWrapper,
a `recv()` lower-level guard, and 25 comprehensive tests.

## Root cause

`collective_rpc()` computes an absolute deadline at enqueue time:

```python
deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
```

The `get_response()` closure captures this deadline.  When a synchronous RPC
first drains pending async futures, time passes and the deadline can expire
before the current call's response is read.  Previously the remaining time
was computed as a plain subtraction:

```python
dequeue_timeout = deadline - time.monotonic()  # may be negative
```

A negative float reaches `MessageQueue.dequeue()` → `MessageQueue.recv()` →
`zmq.Socket.poll(timeout=<negative>)`, where ZMQ treats negative values as
undefined behaviour (often an unbounded wait).

## Changes

1. **`_remaining_timeout()` helper** — clamps to `max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic())`, so a stale deadline produces an immediate timeout (0.0) rather than a negative value.

2. **Synchronous RPC bypasses FutureWrapper** — for `non_block=False`, drains pending async futures directly then calls `get_response()` without wrapping in a `FutureWrapper`.  This avoids the pointless allocation and remains semantically identical (same drain order, same aggregation, same exception propagation).

3. **`MessageQueue.recv()` guard** — clamps the millisecond timeout to `max(0, ...)` as defence-in-depth so a negative value can never reach `zmq.Socket.poll()` even if a future code path bypasses `_remaining_timeout`.

## What does NOT change

- Public API is unchanged.
- `non_block=True` path is completely unchanged.
- Pending-future drain order (FIFO via appendleft/pop) is identical.
- Aggregation semantics (`KVOutputAggregator`, `unique_reply_rank`) are identical.
- Exception propagation for both pending futures and the current RPC is identical.

## Test plan

25 unit tests across two files (no GPU or real workers required):

**`tests/v1/executor/test_rpc_deadline_fix.py` (16 tests)**
- `_remaining_timeout`: None → None, future deadline → positive, stale → 0.0, exact-now → ~0.0, very stale → 0.0
- Sync drain: drains all pending futures in correct order, empty queue no-op, aggregation preserved, deadline not stale after drain, multiple sequential drains
- `recv()` guard: negative → 0, None → None, positive → rounded correctly
- Integration: stale deadline sim yields 0.0 timeout; valid deadline yields positive timeout

**`tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor_timeout.py` (9 tests)**
- Uses exact `FutureWrapper` and `_remaining_timeout` source copies with a `FakeClock` for deterministic time-travel.
- `test_future_wrapper_stale_deadline_never_passes_negative_timeout`: the main regression test — deadline +1s, advance 5s past it, asserts `FakeResponseMQ.timeouts == [0.0]` and that dequeue never receives a negative value.
- Non-expired deadline → positive timeout, None deadline → None, very stale → still 0.0, drain-order correctness.

## Related

- Related to #40926 (slow KV connector waits).  This fixes one class of
  timeout bug that could manifest as an unbounded hang in the RPC layer.
  It is not claimed to be a complete fix for #40926.

title: [Bugfix] Fix spawn_new_process_for_each_test silently swallowing test failures
author: dzhengAP
body:
## Problem

`spawn_new_process_for_each_test` was broken — it always passed regardless
of what the test function did, causing silent test coverage failures.

The previous implementation ran `python -m <module_name>` in the child
process, which re-executed the module's `__main__` block instead of
actually calling the test function. `check_returncode()` always saw
exit 0, so any exception raised inside the test was silently swallowed.

Repro from the issue:
```python
@create_new_process_for_each_test("spawn")
def test_failing():
    raise ValueError  # always passed before this fix
```

## Fix

Serialize the test function and its arguments with `cloudpickle` and
pass them to a minimal child script via stdin. The child writes its
full traceback to a temp file on failure; the parent reads it and
raises `RuntimeError` with the traceback included, making CI failures
actionable.

This matches the robustness of `fork_new_process_for_each_test` which
already handled exception propagation correctly.

## Verification

Tested locally with the exact repro from #41415:

```
Testing failure propagation...
FIXED: failure correctly propagated
Test subprocess 'test_failing' failed (exit code 1):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 4, in <module>
    f(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/tmp/test_fix3.py", line 45, in test_failing
    raise ValueError('should propagate')
ValueError: should propagate

Testing success case...
FIXED: success case passes cleanly
```

- Failing tests now correctly raise `RuntimeError` with the full traceback from the child process
- Passing tests continue to work normally

Fixes #41415

title: [Model] Fix Gemma4 MoE activation mismatch
author: lucianommartins
body:
## Summary

Gemma4's `Gemma4MoE` passes `activation="gelu"` (exact GELU via `torch.ops._C.gelu_and_mul`) to `FusedMoE`, but the published model config (`hidden_activation="gelu_pytorch_tanh"`) and the HuggingFace reference implementation both use the tanh-approximated variant. The dense `Gemma4MLP` in the same file already correctly enforces `gelu_pytorch_tanh` with a `raise ValueError` guard.

The root cause is that `MoEActivation` had no `GELU_TANH` variant when `Gemma4MoE` was written, so `"gelu"` was used as the closest available string.

## Changes

FusedMoE activation enum:
- add `GELU_TANH` and `GELU_TANH_NO_MUL` enum members
- add `"gelu_pytorch_tanh"` to `"gelu_tanh"` alias in `from_str()`
- wire gated dispatch to `torch.ops._C.gelu_tanh_and_mul` and non-gated to `F.gelu(approximate="tanh")`
- register in `_CUSTOM_OP_NAMES` and `_WITHOUT_MUL` lookup tables

Backend allowlists:
- add `GELU_TANH` + `GELU_TANH_NO_MUL` to `_supports_activation` in `TritonExperts`, `BatchedTritonExperts`, `MarlinExpertsBase`, and `HummingExpertsBase`

Model fix:
- Change `Gemma4MoE.__init__` activation from `"gelu"` to `"gelu_tanh"`

## Source of truth

title: [Bugfix] Fix /wake_up crash on hybrid models (Mamba/DeltaNet)
author: kevglynn
body:
## Purpose

Fix `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'zero_'` when calling `/wake_up` after `/sleep` on hybrid models that use Mamba, DeltaNet, or other `MambaSpec`-based layers with quantized KV cache.

Fixes #41564

## Root Cause

`init_fp8_kv_scales()` (called via `post_kv_cache_wake_up()` → `wake_up()`) iterates `self.kv_caches` and calls `.zero_()` on each entry, assuming every entry is a `torch.Tensor`:

```python
for cache_tensor in kv_caches:
    if cache_tensor is not None:
        cache_tensor.zero_()
```

But for hybrid models, `MambaSpec` layers store their per-layer state as a **list of tensors** rather than a single tensor (see `_initialize_kv_cache_tensors`, L6717–6740):

```python
elif isinstance(kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec):
    state_tensors = []
    ...
    kv_caches[layer_name] = state_tensors  # list, not tensor
```

These lists are appended to `self.kv_caches` via `bind_kv_cache()`. So `self.kv_caches` contains a mix of `torch.Tensor` (attention layers) and `list[torch.Tensor]` (Mamba/DeltaNet layers). When the loop hits a list, `.zero_()` fails.

**Why Gemma-4 survives:** It uses pure interleaved SWA (all `FullAttentionSpec`/`SlidingWindowSpec`), so every `kv_caches` entry is a tensor.

## Approach

Check whether each entry is a list or a tensor and handle both:

```python
for cache_entry in kv_caches:
    if cache_entry is None:
        continue
    if isinstance(cache_entry, list):
        for t in cache_entry:
            t.zero_()
    else:
        cache_entry.zero_()
```

## Test Plan

- [x] All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, etc.)
- [x] **Hardware validated by @DoradusResearch** on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM12.0a) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--enable-prefix-caching`:

| # | Model | Architecture | `/sleep` | `/wake_up` | post-wake chat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-NVFP4 | Mamba + attention | **200** | **200** | coherent |
| 2 | Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 | Dense + Gated DeltaNet | **200** | **200** | coherent |
| 3 | Qwen3-Coder-Next-80B-A3B-NVFP4 | DeltaNet + SWA MoE | **200** | **200** | coherent |
| 4 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 | Hybrid SWA MoE | **200** | **200** | coherent |
| 5 | Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4 (control) | Pure interleaved-SWA | **200** | **200** | coherent (no regression) |

All five architectures green, 0 restarts since patched deploy. See [full validation comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41602#issuecomment-4375996290).

- [x] Existing sleep/wake tests (`tests/basic_correctness/test_cumem.py`) use pure-attention models and would not exercise this code path — no regression risk.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The root cause was identified by tracing the code path from `/wake_up` → `gpu_worker.wake_up()` → `post_kv_cache_wake_up()` → `init_fp8_kv_scales()` and cross-referencing with how `MambaSpec` layers populate `self.kv_caches`. No duplicate PRs were found addressing this issue.

## Test Result

Pre-commit (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, etc.): all passed.
Hardware validation: all 5 architectures pass (see test plan above).

## Summary

Fixes #41672.

**Root cause:** an inverted boolean condition (`or not thinking_budget_tracks_reqs` instead of `or thinking_budget_tracks_reqs`) in `gpu_input_batch.py`. title: [Bugfix][Quark] Fix W8A8 INT8 garbage outputs on Step-3.5-Flash (and other 3-key fused-MoE Quark exports)
author: JoursBleu
body:
### Summary

After quantizing `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash` to W8A8 INT8 with AMD Quark, serving the checkpoint via vLLM produces garbage tokens (random tokens, frequent NaN logits). If the same weights are offline-rewritten into compressed-tensors format and served by stock vLLM (with no changes whatsoever), everything works fine — this confirms that the INT8 numerics themselves are correct and the bug is in vLLM's Quark loading path. This PR fixes three independent bugs in the Quark INT8 backend; together they are the root cause of the garbage output. After the fix, the Quark-native checkpoint (`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8`) runs directly without any rewrite, and matches the compressed-tensors baseline on GSM8K and is lossless against the BF16 baseline.

The change is scoped to the Quark INT8 path and the single model class `Step3p5ForCausalLM`; **the compressed-tensors path is untouched**.

### Three root causes

**1. `Step3p5ForCausalLM` is missing `packed_modules_mapping`.**

vLLM fuses `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` into `qkv_proj` and `gate_proj`/`up_proj` into `gate_up_proj` (for both the dense MLP and the shared expert). `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` calls:

```python
should_ignore_layer(prefix, ignore=exclude_layers,
                    fused_mapping=self.packed_modules_mapping)
```

When the model class does not declare `packed_modules_mapping` (the default empty dict), `should_ignore_layer` cannot reverse the fused prefix back to the unfused names listed in `quantization_config.exclude`.

In Quark exports, the shared expert is listed in unfused form in `exclude` (`model.layers.X.share_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj`). As a result, `share_expert.gate_up_proj` is not recognized as excluded and is wrongly attached as a Quark INT8 linear, even though the checkpoint contains no INT8 weights or scales for it — `weight_scale` stays at its zero-initialized value, the shared-expert output becomes identically 0 / NaN, and the corruption then propagates through residual + layernorm and ruins the entire forward pass.

After adding the standard `packed_modules_mapping` to `Step3p5ForCausalLM`, `should_ignore_layer` correctly matches the shared expert against the exclude list, and the layer falls back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and loads correctly.

**2. `QuarkW8A8MoEMethod` does not handle Quark's INT8 checkpoint layout.**

Quark's HF safetensors export differs from compressed-tensors only "cosmetically":

- It carries redundant symmetric `weight_zero_point` / `input_zero_point` tensors.
- Per-channel `weight_scale` is stored as 1D `[N]` per expert, with no trailing singleton dimension.

The old Quark MoE method could limp along with the legacy per-tensor INT8 recipe, but Step-3.5 (and similar models) use the modern per-channel + dynamic per-token activation recipe, and the old code path produced incorrect numerics on it.

This PR rewrites `QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` to mirror `CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8MoEMethod` exactly:

- The per-channel scale is registered as 2D `[E, N]` for loading, then unsqueezed to `[E, N, 1]` in `process_weights_after_loading` so the modular int8 MoE kernel sees exactly the same layout as compressed-tensors.
- The per-channel path invokes the kernel via `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config(..., per_act_token_quant=True)`.
- The symmetric `*_zero_point` tensors are registered as placeholders so safetensors loading does not fail on unknown keys, and are dropped in `process_weights_after_loading` before the quant config is built.
- The legacy per-tensor static W8A8 recipe is fully preserved (the shard-merging logic is unchanged), keeping backward compatibility.

**3. The non-MoE `QuarkW8A8Int8` linear also needs 2D scale alignment.**

For ordinary linears, Quark likewise stores per-channel `weight_scale` as 1D `[N]`, while the rest of vLLM and compressed-tensors expect 2D `[N, 1]`. This PR adds a small weight-loader shim that unsqueezes 1D scales before the standard shape check runs, and the parameter itself is allocated as `[N, 1]`. The runtime layout is then identical to compressed-tensors.

### Validation

`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8` on MI355X, TP=2 + EP=2, vLLM `0.19.2rc1.dev109+gaad88f848.rocm721`:

|   | Smoke (`"What is 12 times 17?"`) | GSM8K (1319 q, 8-shot, max_tokens=8192) |
|---|---|---|
| before | garbage | — |
| **after** | "The product of 12 and 17 is **204**." | **1255 / 1319 = 95.15%** |
| Quark→CT-format baseline | OK | 1254 / 1319 = 95.07% |

BF16 baseline is 95.91%; the gap is within noise (lossless).

### Scope / risk

- Only `Step3p5ForCausalLM` and the Quark INT8 backend are touched; other models / other quantization paths are unaffected.
- The `packed_modules_mapping` added to `Step3p5ForCausalLM` is identical to what every other QKV+gate_up model in vLLM ships, and it only affects how Quark/CT `exclude` lists are matched against fused module prefixes — it does not affect weight loading itself.
- The non-MoE `QuarkW8A8Int8` linear change is backward-compatible: per-tensor (scalar) scales are unchanged, and old 1D `[N]` per-channel scales are reshaped to `[N, 1]` at load time.
- The MoE rewrite preserves the legacy per-tensor INT8 path; this PR fixes the per-channel + dynamic-input path.

### Related

- `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8`: the public checkpoint that exposes this bug.

title: [Bugfix] Fix GDN KKT precision loss on Hopper GPUs by aligning tl.dot operand layout with WGMMA
author: Kermit-C
body:
## Purpose

Fix precision loss in `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel` on Hopper-architecture GPUs (e.g. H20, sm_90) that causes GDN-based models to produce **garbage output (e.g. lm_eval gsm8k score = 0 !!!)**.

### Root Cause

[PR #37813](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37813) optimized the GDN conv path, but it also introduced an overlooked side-effect: the `g` tensor passed to `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel` changed from float32 to bf16. Combined with a suboptimal operand layout in the existing `tl.dot` call on line 86, this triggered a precision bug specific to Hopper (sm_90) GPUs.

The problematic line:

```python
b_A += tl.dot(b_kb.to(b_k.dtype), tl.trans(b_k))
```

`b_kb` is already bf16 (result of `b_k * b_beta[:, None]`, both bf16). `b_k.dtype` is also bf16. So `.to(b_k.dtype)` is an identity cast in terms of data type — but in Triton's IR it inserts a `convert_layout` operation that changes the tensor's distributed register layout.

On **Hopper (H20, sm_90)**, Triton lowers `tl.dot` to the WGMMA (Warpgroup MMA) instruction family. WGMMA is highly sensitive to operand layout — when operand A's register layout is perturbed by the spurious `.to()` call, the hardware performs additional rearrangement that loses precision in the dot product accumulator. The error propagates through `exp(b_g_diff)` and ultimately produces NaN in the output, causing downstream GDN layers to generate garbage tokens.

On **Ada (4060ti, sm_89)** and earlier architectures, Triton uses HMMA/WMMA instructions which are tolerant of layout variations — the compiler optimizes away the redundant layout conversion and both patterns produce identical PTX. This is why the issue was not caught during development.

With float32 `g`, the higher-precision `exp(b_g_diff)` multiplication masks the dot product error. With bf16 `g` (introduced by #37813), the lower-precision downstream computation amplifies the error past the NaN threshold.

### Fix

Move `.to()` from the non-transposed operand (A matrix) to the transposed operand (B matrix):

```python
# Before (buggy):
b_A += tl.dot(b_kb.to(b_k.dtype), tl.trans(b_k))

# After (fixed):
b_A += tl.dot(b_kb, tl.trans(b_k).to(b_kb.dtype))
```

This lets Triton combine the transpose + type conversion into a single layout transform that produces the register layout WGMMA expects natively, avoiding the intermediate precision loss. This pattern is already used consistently in other FLA kernels (e.g. `chunk_delta_h.py`).

## Test Plan

### 1. Determinism test (diag_gdn_h20.py)
[diag_gdn_h20.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27528085/diag_gdn_h20.py)

```bash

```

Expected: all comparisons pass with `max_diff=0.000000e+00`.

### 2. lm_eval gsm8k

Validates end-to-end model quality on GDN-enabled Qwen3.5-9B FP8:
> With `gdn_prefill_backend=triton` args

```bash
python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm --model_args "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B,dtype=auto,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,max_model_len=4096,quantization=fp8,max_num_seqs=16,trust_remote_code=True,gdn_prefill_backend=triton" \
    --tasks gsm8k --batch_size auto --num_fewshot 5
```

## Test Result

### 1. diag_gdn_h20.py

**H20 (before fix)**:
```
GPU: NVIDIA H20
Compute: (9, 0)
Test 1: KKT with set_triton_allocator
  ✗ KKT H=16,L=128: max_diff=nan [NaN]
  ✗ KKT H=16,L=256: max_diff=nan [NaN]
  ✓ KKT H=4,L=128: max_diff=0.000000e+00

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma4ToolParser streaming float corruption
author: abinggo
body:
## Summary

Fixes #42047 — `Gemma4ToolParser` produces incorrect float values during streaming (e.g., `108.2` → `108.02`).

**Root cause:** When a bare numeric value ending with `.` (e.g., `"108."`) is terminated by a comma in partial/streaming mode, `float("108.")` evaluates to `108.0`. The JSON serialization `"108.0"` is emitted to the client. When the true decimal digit arrives and the value becomes `108.2`, the streaming diff logic computes a common prefix of `"108."` but the client already received `"108.0"` — the final diff appends `"2"`, producing `"108.02"`.

**Fix:** In `_parse_gemma4_args()` and `_parse_gemma4_array()`, when `partial=True` (streaming mode), withhold bare values that end with `"."` since additional decimal digits may still arrive. This is consistent with the existing end-of-string withholding logic. The final non-partial parse at tool-call-end handles these values correctly.

## Test plan

- [x] Added regression tests in `tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py`:
  - `test_trailing_dot_float_partial_withheld` — verifies `"108."` is withheld in partial mode

title: fix(eagle3): read norm_before_fc from eagle_config for NVIDIA checkpoint
author: ghost
body:
## Purpose

Eagle3 checkpoints from NVIDIA (GPT-OSS series) store `norm_before_fc` inside the nested `eagle_config` dict rather than as a top-level config field. We currently only check the top-level, so the RMSNorm before FC gets silently skipped for these checkpoints, causing degraded acceptance rate.

Fix: read `norm_before_fc` from `eagle_config` first, fall back to top-level attr. Same pattern already used for `use_aux_hidden_state` in the same block.

## Test Plan

```bash
export TARGET=/path/to/Qwen3-32B
export DRAFT=/path/to/Qwen3-32B_eagle3

# 1. correctness — greedy match between baseline and eagle3
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -c "
import torch, gc
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
PROMPTS = ['What is the capital of France?', 'Explain gradient descent in two sentences.', 'Write a Python factorial function.', 'The theory of relativity states that']
P = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=64)
llm = LLM(model='${TARGET}', dtype='bfloat16', gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=2048, trust_remote_code=True)
base = [o.outputs[0].text for o in llm.generate(PROMPTS, P)]
del llm; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()
llm = LLM(model='${TARGET}', speculative_config={'method':'eagle3','model':'${DRAFT}','num_speculative_tokens':3}, dtype='bfloat16', gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=2048, trust_remote_code=True)
eagle = [o.outputs[0].text for o in llm.generate(PROMPTS, P)]
for i,(b,e) in enumerate(zip(base,eagle)): assert b==e, f'mismatch at {i}'
print('PASS')
"

# 2. perf — single-request decode, 512 tokens
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -c "
import torch, time, gc
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
P = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=512, ignore_eos=True)
PROMPT = ['Write a detailed essay about the history of computer science.']
llm = LLM(model='${TARGET}', dtype='bfloat16', gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=2048, trust_remote_code=True)
_=llm.generate(['hi'],SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=5))
t=time.time(); llm.generate(PROMPT,P); base=512/(time.time()-t)
del llm; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()
llm = LLM(model='${TARGET}', speculative_config={'method':'eagle3','model':'${DRAFT}','num_speculative_tokens':3}, dtype='bfloat16', gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=2048, trust_remote_code=True)
_=llm.generate(['hi'],SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=5))
t=time.time(); llm.generate(PROMPT,P); e3=512/(time.time()-t)
print(f'baseline {base:.1f} tok/s, eagle3 {e3:.1f} tok/s, speedup {e3/base:.2f}x')
"

# 3. unit — config parsing branches
python3 -c "
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.eagle.eagle3_utils import get_eagle3_aux_layers_from_config
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
class C: eagle_config={'norm_before_fc':True}
ec=getattr(C,'eagle_config',None) or {}
assert bool(ec.get('norm_before_fc',getattr(C,'norm_before_fc',False)))
class C2:
 eagle_config=None
 norm_before_fc=True
ec2=getattr(C2,'eagle_config',None) or {}
assert bool(ec2.get('norm_before_fc',getattr(C2,'norm_before_fc',False)))
sc=MagicMock(); sc.draft_model_config.hf_config.eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids=[2,32,61]
assert get_eagle3_aux_layers_from_config(sc)==(2,32,61)
print('PASS')
"
```

Tested with Qwen3-32B + Qwen3-32B_eagle3 on 1x H200.

## Test Result

- Correctness: 4/4 greedy outputs match exactly
- Performance: baseline 51.3 tok/s → eagle3 67.1 tok/s (1.31x)
- Config unit tests: all pass
- No regression on models using top-level `norm_before_fc` (fallback path unchanged)

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek v4 topk numerical issue for unaligned max-model-len
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose: It is observed that DeepSeek v4 has numerical issues when passing certain values of `--max-model-len` (e.g., 900000). For instance, the following figure shows the distribution of the number of completion tokens with 100 responses sampled for a selected question from GPQA. It can be seen that the number of generated tokens has a noticeable distribution shift when `--max-model-len 900000` is passed, compared to that not passed. Investigation shows that the root cause is that the indexer persistent topk kernel uses `const int64_t stride = logits.size(1);`. However, the logits produced from [deepgemm's](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/891d57b4db1071624b5c8fa0d1e51cb317fa709f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L361) `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` pads the `max_model_len` dimension to align with 256 and later slices the view to `max_model_len`. Thus, when `max_model_len` is not naturally aligned, the logits become incontiguous, thus the stride calculation is incorrect. This PR fixes this bug. To reproduce the experiment: ``` VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 256 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \ --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache True \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 2048 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --max-model-len 900000 \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 ``` Set and unset `--max-model-len 900000` to see the difference. Prompt: ``` QUESTION = ( "You have prepared a di-substituted 6-membered aromatic ring compound " "containing 8 carbon atoms in total. Peaks in the FTIR spectrum of this " "compound indicate the presence of a carbonyl group as well as an " "aromatic-halogen bond. Identify the correct 1H NMR data for this compound. \n" "\n" "A) 1H NMR: chemical reference (ppm): 6.9 (1H, s), 4.8 (2H, d), 4.6 (2H, d), 1.3 (2H, s)\n" "B) 1H NMR: chemical reference (ppm): 9.9 (1H, s), 7.8 (2H, d), 7.6 (2H, d), 3.7 (2H, s)\n" "C) 1H NMR: chemical reference (ppm): 4.8 (2H, d), 4.6 (2H, d), 1.3 (3H, s)\n" "D) 1H NMR: chemical reference (ppm): 7.8 (2H, d), 7.6 (2H, d), 2.3 (3H, s)" ) ``` ## Test Plan - Test the num token distribution is normal - Test e2e eval accuracy ## Test Result The figure shows that after applying the patch, the num token distribution becomes normal. In addition, e2e GPQA results: ``` main TP without max-model-len: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 11754 | 3361 | 89.39% | 0.00% main DEP without max-model-len: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 12232 | 4058 | 88.88% | 0.00% main TP with --max-model-len 900000: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 25955 | 12300 | 81.82% | 5.05% main DEP with --max-model-len 900000: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 17770 | 7457 | 89.39% | 0.00% branch TP with --max-model-len 900000: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 12573 | 3514 | 88.89% | 0.00% branch DEP with --max-model-len 900000: nemo-run_1/0 ----------------------------------------- gpqa ---------------------------------------- nemo-run_1/0 evaluation_mode | num_entries | avg_tokens | gen_seconds | symbolic_correct | no_answer nemo-run_1/0 pass@1 | 198 | 12381 | 4197 | 87.88% | 0.00% ``` ---

title: [Bugfix] Fixes MiniCPM-O resampler device placement to avoid tensor device mismatch
author: j9smith
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #42322. MiniCPM-O 2.6 crashes on startup with `Expected all tensors to be on the same device`.

This is caused by `Resampler2_5._set_2d_pos_cache` creating the `pos_embed` buffer on CPU during init (found in `minicpmv.py`). Typically, it would be moved to GPU via `MiniCPMVBaseModel._ensure_resampler_device` which is generally called during the `load_weights` of `MiniCPMVBaseModel`. `MiniCPMOBaseModel` overrides the parent's `load_weights` to skip `tts` prefixes, but never calls `_ensure_resampler_device`. The resampler never gets moved to GPU, and the buffer stays on CPU; the profiling run reaches `x + pos_embed` (CUDA and CPU) and crashes. 

The fix is minimal: add `self._ensure_resampler_device()` to `MiniCPMOBaseModel.load_weights` to match the pattern found in `MiniCPMV`. Both `MiniCPMO2_6` and `MiniCPMO4_5` inherit from `MiniCPMOBaseModel` so both are fixed.

## Test Plan
Reproduce the bug in #42322 using the provided command, apply the fix, then re-run:
```bash
vllm serve openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len=16000
```
Tested on fresh vLLM install (v0.20.1).

## Test Result
Before the fix, engine core fails to start during the profile run with the same trace as in #42322. 

After applying the fix, the engine core initialises successfully, weights load, and the API server starts and accepts requests.

title: [Bugfix] Fix layerwise reload alias-buffer corruption
author: rasdani
body:
## Purpose

Fix layerwise reload corrupting non-persistent buffers that alias checkpoint-loaded
parameters.

Layerwise reload records a module's parameters and buffers before restoring the
module to meta tensors, then materializes and copies processed tensors back into
the original kernel tensor storage. That is correct for independent buffers, but
it is unsafe for non-persistent buffers that are only views/aliases of model
parameters.

This already affects same-module aliases, and it also affects a more realistic
Mamba/Nemotron shape:

- `MambaMixer2` registers `conv_weights` as a non-persistent buffer.
- `conv_weights` aliases the child parameter `conv1d.weight`.
- `MambaMixer2` also owns direct parameters such as `A`, `D`, and `dt_bias`.
- During reload, the parent `MambaMixer2` can be materialized/finalized for
  those direct parameters.
- If `conv_weights` is captured as an independent buffer, the materialized
  buffer can be copied back into the original buffer storage.
- Because that buffer storage aliases `conv1d.weight`, this can overwrite the
  child conv weight after it was loaded.

The first important boundary is metadata capture: the alias check must look
through `layer.parameters(recurse=True)`, not only `layer._parameters`, so
non-persistent buffers aliasing parameters anywhere in the layer subtree are
excluded from layerwise restore metadata.

There is a second boundary during copy-back. `initialize_layerwise_reload` saves
the original kernel tensors before the module is restored on meta tensors. Those
saved kernel tensors still include the original alias buffer so it can be
re-registered later. But after metadata capture intentionally omits the alias
buffer, the temporary materialized layer does not have that buffer anymore. The
copy-back path must therefore skip only the omitted alias-buffer case instead of
blindly calling `getattr(layer, name)`.

## Changes

- Skip non-persistent buffers that share storage with any parameter in the
  current module subtree during layerwise reload metadata capture. Parameter
  storage pointers are precomputed once per layer to avoid rescanning the
  subtree for each buffer.
- During copy-back, skip original kernel buffers that are absent from the
  materialized layer. This preserves omitted alias buffers for re-registration
  without copying from a missing or independently-materialized temporary buffer.
- Add a direct same-module alias regression test.
- Add a parent-buffer/child-parameter alias regression test matching the
  `MambaMixer2.conv_weights -> MambaMixer2.conv1d.weight` pattern.

## Production context

We hit this while debugging NaN generations after repeated checkpoint-format
weight reloads for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`.

Out-of-tree instrumentation in a production-style 5-node PrimeRL run confirmed
the relevant alias shape in live vLLM workers:

- `layer_class=MambaMixer2`
- `buffer_name=conv_weights`
- `non_persistent=true`
- `alias_matches=[conv1d.weight]`
- `direct_param_names=["A", "D", "dt_bias"]`

Across the 8 TP workers in that run, the recursive guard detected and skipped
320 `MambaMixer2.conv_weights` buffers. The old direct-parameter-only check would
not detect this parent-buffer/child-parameter alias.


## Test Plan

```bash
  python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_layerwise_reload_skips_non_persistent_parameter_alias_buffers \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_layerwise_reload_skips_child_parameter_alias_buffers \
  -q --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader
```

## Test Result

```text
2 passed, 17 warnings in 7.44s
All checks passed!
```

## Notes

- No user-facing docs change: this is a correctness fix for existing layerwise
  reload behavior.
- AI assistance disclosure: this PR includes AI-assisted debugging and code
  drafting; the submitter should review all changed lines and ensure commits are
  signed off per the vLLM DCO requirements.

## Purpose

This PR addresses the following issues

1. Functionality broken after this PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41263 (fixed by removing `x = self.ffn_norm(x)`)

title: Fix DFlash prefix cache corruption due to missing lookahead block
author: shreyas269
body:
## Summary

Fixes a KV cache corruption bug in DFlash that causes persistent MGL degradation under prefix caching with concurrency.

## How we found this

While trying out DFlash, under high concurrency with prefix caching enabled, we observed MGL degradation on requests that were otherwise running correctly. Their KV cache was being corrupted by other newly-arriving prefix-hit requests. We saw a steady decrease in MGL. Specifically, those new request's first DFlash drafter pass was writing KV into shared prefix blocks because their slot mapping was never set up (no lookahead blocks were allocated for them). We didn't see this degradation in sglang under the same workload, which confirmed this was a vllm-specific bug. Once we traced the corruption back to the missing block allocation on first prefill, the fix was straightforward.

## Root cause

The target prefill and the first drafter pass run in the same scheduler step for both Eagle and DFlash. The DFlash drafter issues `num_spec_tokens + 1` query tokens (1 bonus token + N mask tokens) at positions beyond the prefill.

These positions require allocated KV blocks because DFlash draft attention is bidirectional and the drafter writes KV at future positions via block table lookup. If the block table doesn't cover those positions, the drafter writes into the wrong block.

The scheduler had this logic when allocating blocks for a new request:

```python
effective_lookahead_tokens = (
    0 if request.num_computed_tokens == 0 else self.num_lookahead_tokens
)
```

From the comment it looks like this was added as a P/D disaggregation edge case guard to avoid allocating extra blocks for brand-new requests. However, `request.num_computed_tokens` is still 0 at the point where `allocate_slots` is called for a new request's first scheduling pass (it's only updated after allocation succeeds, at a later line). This means zero lookahead blocks are allocated at prefill time, yet the DFlash drafter immediately needs to write KV beyond the allocated range.

When the correct blocks don't exist, the drafter ends up writing KV into the last prefill block instead...which with prefix caching is shared across requests. It silently overwrites valid prefill KV data in that block.

**Without prefix caching:** The corrupted last block belongs only to the current request. In the next scheduling step, `request.num_computed_tokens > 0`, so lookahead blocks are allocated correctly. The drafter has one bad step...and then recovers. This is likely why MGL impact was negligible without prefix caching and we still saw good speedups with DFlash.

**With prefix caching under concurrency:** Multiple requests share the same prefix blocks. When a new request's drafter writes KV into the wrong block, it corrupts a shared prefix block. All other requests using that prefix...including ones that were running fine...now read corrupted KV. This is what we observed: MGL degradation on healthy requests, caused by new arrivals corrupting their shared prefix cache. Kind of only impacts MGL in a special case where the unalloted KV blocks are overwritten very fast due to high prefix-hit and conurrency.

## Changes

~~### 1. Scheduler (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`)~~

~~- Added `self.use_dflash` flag, initialized from `speculative_config.use_dflash()`.~~
~~- Set `self.num_lookahead_tokens = self.num_spec_tokens + 1` for DFlash (the +1 is for the bonus token position).~~
~~- When DFlash is active, unconditionally allocate lookahead blocks regardless of `request.num_computed_tokens`:~~

```python
if self.use_dflash:
    effective_lookahead_tokens = self.num_lookahead_tokens
else:
    effective_lookahead_tokens = (
        0 if request.num_computed_tokens == 0
        else self.num_lookahead_tokens
    )
```

EDIT: The scheduler fix (reserving `num_spec_tokens + 1` lookahead slots for DFlash on first prefill, and narrowing the `num_computed_tokens == 0` guard) landed separately in [#43733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43733). This PR is rebased on top of it and no longer touches the scheduler.

### 2. GPU Model Runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`)

Fixed the drafter input-fit check. The existing code used `max_seq_len + self.num_spec_tokens` to decide if a sequence fits within the drafter's max model length. For DFlash, the drafter actually queries `num_spec_tokens + 1` positions (bonus + masks), so sequences could be incorrectly admitted:

```python
num_drafter_query_tokens = self.num_spec_tokens + (
    1 if spec_config.use_dflash() else 0
)
```

## Test plan

- Added `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py` with three unit tests:

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py -v
=================================================================================================== test session starts ===================================================================================================

tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py::test_dflash_prefill_reserves_lookahead_blocks PASSED                                                                                                                 [ 33%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py::test_dflash_first_prefill_query_window_fits_allocated_blocks PASSED                                                                                                  [ 66%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py::test_dflash_drafter_window_reserves_bonus_token PASSED                                                                                                               [100%]

```
