title: [ROCm][MLA] [K3] Fix fp8 KV cache decode on the AITER MLA backend
author: fanxingran
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 at TP8 has 12 MLA heads per rank and cannot serve correctly with
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on the ROCm AITER MLA backend. On unmodified main, a full
GSM8K run at that configuration scores **74.00%** with **285 of 1319 answers
degenerate**; with this PR it scores **97.19%** with **none**. The backend fails
three different ways depending on head count and query length, and the third is
the dangerous one because nothing reports it.

1. **Assertion, for head counts that divide 16.** Gluon has exactly one fp8-KV
   regime, `bh16bn128`, and it asserts `batch_size == 1`
   (`aiter/ops/triton/gluon/mla_gluon.py:956`), so it cannot serve a real decode
   batch at any head count. The constraint is fp8-specific -- the sibling
   `bh16bn64` bf16 regime takes any batch. The asm decode already ships true fp8
   kernels for this shape (`mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen*_gqaratio16*.co`) but is never
   reached, because a head count below 16 is routed to Gluon regardless of dtype.
   Because batch 1 passes, a single-request smoke test does not catch this; the
   first request that arrives alongside another one takes the server down.

2. **`KeyError`, at speculative query lengths.** `_mtp_decode_qlen` came from a
   hardcoded list of method names, `("mtp", "deepseek_mtp")`. Drafters not on
   it got metadata sized for `qlen=1` while the router still admitted queries up
   to `1 + 2 * num_spec`, so the persistent gate never opened and aiter fell
   through to indexing `get_block_n_fp8[num_heads * qlen]`. That table holds only
   `{8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 384, 512}`, so at 16 heads every qlen in
   `5..7` and `9..15` is a `KeyError` -- a crash at a random point mid-run.

3. **Silently wrong output, for head counts that do not divide 16.** This is
   Kimi-K3's case, and it is what the 74.00% above measures. A 12-head rank is
   padded to 16 and runs the asm decode, but `use_persistent_metadata` was gated
   on `num_heads >= 16`, which reads as False for it, so the kernel fell back on
   its internal metadata. bf16 tolerates that; fp8 does not. 21.6% of requests
   emit one or two plausible tokens and then repeat a single token to the length
   cap -- `We!!!!!!...`, `The!!!!!!...`, `Let!!!!!!...` -- the signature of a NaN
   reaching the sampler. At `qlen == 1` nothing raises, since `16 * 1 = 16` is in
   the table above, so on a short smoke test this surfaces only as degraded
   quality and is easy to misread as quantisation loss. It is not: emulating the
   fp8 cache on top of a bf16 one, leaving the code path untouched, produces
   correct output.

### What changes

Five changes, all in decode routing. No kernel or aiter change.

1. `_mtp_decode_qlen` is derived from `reorder_batch_threshold`, the largest
   query length decode can be handed, instead of a method-name whitelist. Closes
   (2) for every drafter at once.
2. A quantized cache never routes to the Gluon decode, whether or not the head
   count divides 16.
3. The verify branch becomes a `use_gluon_verify` predicate and excludes fp8. It
   was inlined in `forward_mqa` with no dtype check, so a small-head fp8 verify
   was pulled back into Gluon after `use_gluon_decode` had rejected it. As a
   predicate the builder can also see it, which (4) needs.
4. The persistent-metadata gate keys off the routing, `not use_gluon_decode and
   not use_gluon_verify`, rather than `num_heads >= 16`. Only Gluon ignores the
   schedule, and for fp8 the fold path requires it:
   `asm_mla.cu:903 ... only support gqa_ratio=16 fp8 mla decoding with
   qo_len <= 4 and qo_len > 4 in persistent mode on gfx950`.
5. `_kv_cache_dtype_str` is kept on the builder so `_build_decode` can make those
   decisions; it was computed and dropped in `__init__`.

What lets fp8 leave Gluon is the q-row fold: a padded 16 heads x qlen 8 folds
onto the `nhead=32, qseqlen=4` kernel, which ships as a `.co` in the package.

Change 4 gives bf16 no accuracy benefit -- non-persistent bf16 passes accuracy
and is ~1% faster in my measurements. It is justified by fp8 correctness alone.

### Why `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm` is not a substitute

#50578 added a knob that forces both small-head paths onto asm, which overlaps
with changes 2 and 3. It does not replace this PR, and for the configuration
measured above it is a no-op.

At 12 heads and `qlen == 1`, `use_gluon_decode` already returns False on main:
`16 % 12 != 0`, so the decode is on asm before the knob is consulted. The 74.00%
comes entirely from change 4 -- the schedule that a padded rank is denied -- and
the knob does not touch that gate. At `qlen > 1` the knob does keep fp8 out of
Gluon, but the same gate then denies the schedule, and the asm fp8 path rejects
`qlen > 4` outright without it.

The knob is also dtype-blind and opt-in: forcing `asm` moves bf16 divisor counts
off Gluon too, where they are faster, and a user who leaves the default gets
silently wrong answers rather than an error.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py` is new and pins both predicates: fp8
reaches neither Gluon entry point at any head count, query length, or setting of
`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING`; `>= 16` heads is unchanged; bf16 divisors keep
the Gluon decode; bf16 non-divisors take asm; bf16 small-head verify still
flattens onto Gluon. The bf16 cases monkeypatch `_gluon_mla_decode_supported` and
`_aiter_mla_small_head_mode` so the file is not gfx950-only. It also carries
`test_padded_query_is_contiguous`, a regression test for the tile-and-slice
padding (`asm_mla.cu:805 only support Q.is_contiguous()`), which landed without
one. `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` gains fp8 and 12-head cases on the
persistent gate, and its metadata-sizing test now sweeps a parallel drafter and
an eagle drafter alongside `deepseek_mtp`.

End to end on Kimi-K3-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/Kimi-K3-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 128 --trust-remote-code
```

## Test Result

Unit tests: 425 passed.

**GSM8K on Kimi-K3-MXFP4, TP8 (12 heads/rank), full 1319-problem test set,
zero-shot greedy, concurrency 32. The two fp8 rows differ only by this patch:**

| KV cache | branch | GSM8K | correct | degenerate | wall clock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 | main, unpatched | 74.00% | 976/1319 | 285 | 989 s |
| fp8 | main + this PR | **97.19%** | 1282/1319 | **0** | 530 s |
| bf16 | reference | 97.19% | 1282/1319 | 0 | 419 s |

An fp8 cache costs no measurable accuracy once the schedule reaches the kernel:
the patched fp8 run lands on the same 1282/1319 as bf16. The unpatched run is
also 1.9x slower in wall clock, because every degenerate request runs to the
2048-token cap.

All 37 remaining fp8 failures are ordinary arithmetic or interpretation errors --
coherent, on-topic, correctly formatted answers with the wrong number. None is
degenerate.

**Serving performance, same server, ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`:**

| concurrency | output tok/s | TTFT mean | TPOT mean | ITL p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 49.6 | 201 ms | 20.0 ms | 20.6 ms |
| 8 | 301.3 | 524 ms | 26.1 ms | 27.0 ms |
| 32 | 953.5 | 757 ms | 32.8 ms | 33.4 ms |

Serving in the production configuration (TP8, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`,
`enforce_eager=False`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), the engine
initialises and captures 35 piecewise and 19 full graphs, and serves normally.

Kernel level, gqa16 + qlen8 + fp8 runs `a8w8_qh32_qseqlen4_gqaratio32_ps` in
131.5 us with persistent metadata and fails `AITER_CHECK` without it, which makes
change 4 a requirement rather than an optimisation.

Routing, for reference:

| heads | qlen | cache | path |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1 | bf16 | gluon decode |
| 8 | 1 | fp8 | asm (padded) |
| 12 | 1 | bf16 | asm (padded) |
| 12 | 1 | fp8 | asm (padded) |
| 16 | 1 | fp8 | asm |
| 8 | 8 | bf16 | gluon verify (flattened) |
| 8 / 12 | 8 | fp8 | asm (padded, q-row fold) |

```bash
aiperf profile \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tokenizer moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8038 --api-key EMPTY \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --num-prefix-prompts 8 --prompt-prefix-length 63240 \
  --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 4760 --synthetic-input-tokens-stddev 0 \
  --output-tokens-mean 350 --output-tokens-stddev 0 \
  --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true \
  --extra-inputs min_tokens:350 --extra-inputs max_tokens:350 \
  --warmup-request-count 16 --sweep-type zip \
  --concurrency 1,8,16,24,48 --request-count 5,40,80,120,240 \
  --random-seed 42 --ui simple
```

| Concurrency | Requests | Output tok/s | Per-user tok/s | ITL avg / p50 (ms) | TTFT avg / p50 (ms) | E2E avg (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5 | 28.4 | 47.70 | 21.0 / 21.0 | 4982 / 5837 | 12,299 |
| 8 | 40 | 122.4 | 23.75 | 48.5 / 38.8 | 5727 / 1539 | 22,643 |
| 16 | 80 | 199.3 | 19.59 | 55.5 / 52.0 | 8403 / 1355 | 27,765 |
| 24 | 120 | 258.2 | 15.98 | 66.8 / 63.2 | 8938 / 1871 | 32,247 |
| 48 | 240 | 360.6 | 10.62 | 99.8 / 102.1 | 11302 / 2008 | 46,140 |

`--sweep-type zip` pairs the two lists element-wise rather than taking their
Cartesian product, so each row is one (concurrency, request-count) pair — the
request count is the sample size at that operating point, not a second dimension.

485/485 requests completed, 0 errors, output length exactly 350 at every point.

Prefix cache hit rate over the measurement window was 83.4% (`vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total`
/ `vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total`), against a 92.9% ceiling (63,240 of 68,089
input tokens are shared)

title: [BugFix] Pick the DP world-group port at bind time via the coordination store
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

With `--data-parallel-size N`, the DP world group's rendezvous port comes from `_data_parallel_master_port_list` — probed once at config time and consumed by `get_next_dp_init_port()` when the engines finally call `init_process_group`, **minutes later** (after worker spawn, CUDA init, and model load). Nothing holds the port in between, so any other process — most commonly a sibling vLLM instance cold-starting on the same host, the standard shape in RL rollout fleets — can take it. Startup then fails at its very last step with the engines hanging on:

```
(Worker pid=...) torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to
listen on any local network address. port: <n>, ... EADDRINUSE
```

#36330 fixed exactly this defect for the elastic-EP stateless groups: rank 0 binds an ephemeral port, keeps the listening socket, and publishes the port through a coordination TCPStore. This PR extends that mechanism to the last remaining pre-allocated consumer, the world group:

- `launch_core_engines()` creates the coordination store for online DP (dp>1, engine rank 0 local; the initial MoE-only gate was removed in a follow-up commit, see below) when none exists yet, and hands its port to engines through the existing startup handshake (`_coord_store_port`).
- `init_distributed_environment()`: for the DP path, group rank 0 creates the world-group TCPStore on port 0 — the kernel assigns the port and the store owns it from birth — then publishes the resulting port via the coordination store; other ranks read it and connect. All ranks pass the store to `init_process_group` (`store=` argument), so the port is never released between choice and use. Without a coord store the previous behavior is unchanged.

## Design notes for reviewers

Answers to the questions this diff naturally raises.

**Why publish through a TCPStore rather than the handshake or spawn args.** The port does not exist until group rank 0 binds — after every engine has spawned and after the handshake replies have gone out (the frontend replies to each HELLO as it arrives; rank 0 has not bound yet at that point). Delivery therefore needs a channel that (a) works after all startup messages, (b) blocks until the value appears (ranks reach group init in arbitrary order), and (c) is reachable from both consumer levels: EngineCore processes (DP gloo group, store-based since #36330) and workers (world group), which have no handshake connection to the frontend at all. A key-value store with blocking `get` is the smallest thing satisfying all three, and #36330 already built it — this PR only extends where it is created (MP path, before the Ray branch) and adds one consumer.

**Why rank 0 creates the store on port 0 and reads the port back.** Ownership must never gap: the world-group TCPStore itself binds port 0, owns the kernel-assigned port from birth, and `.port` reads it back for publication — the same readback pattern the coordination store (and zmq's `LAST_ENDPOINT`) already uses. The already-bound store is then passed to `init_process_group` via `store=`; torch requires `store` and `init_method` to be mutually exclusive, hence `init_method=None if world_pg_store else distributed_init_method` at both call sites. Rank 0 passes `wait_for_workers=False` because workers can only connect after the port is published, so the master cannot block for them inside its own constructor; PG init synchronizes through store keys as usual. An earlier revision of this PR bound a raw socket manually and handed it to `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)`; review simplified it to `TCPStore(port=0)` — same invariant, one layer less, and it drops the fd-adoption/libuv compat surface (cf. the `use_libuv=False` pin in `StatelessProcessGroup.create` for pytorch#150215).

**An externally-built store is equivalent to the torch-built one.** The constructor arguments mirror torch's own `_create_c10d_store` (`world_size`, `is_master=(rank == 0)`, group timeout, `multi_tenant=True`); both paths converge in `_new_process_group_helper`, which cannot tell who built the store. `store=` is the public contract torchelastic uses in production. Two known differences, both benign: (1) `wait_for_workers=False` on rank 0 (see above) moves a missing-worker failure from store-construction timeout to PG-init rendezvous timeout — the behavior torchelastic deployments already run with; (2) torch wraps rendezvous-built stores in `PrefixStore("default_pg")` but takes a passed store raw — harmless because the store is freshly created and dedicated to this group, and all members take the same branch.

**Store-creation guards.** Each condition excludes a deployment where creating the store would be useless or wrong: `dp_size > 1` (no consumer otherwise), `not offline_mode` (scope: offline keeps existing behavior), `dp_rank == 0 and local_engine_count > 0` (the store must bind on the DP master node; an API-server-only frontend would `bind()` an IP that is not its own), `not enable_elastic_ep` (the Ray actor manager creates its own store later, unchanged from #36330). An earlier idempotency check on `_coord_store_port` was dropped: no in-tree writer can set the field before this block runs.

**Fallback path is byte-for-byte the old behavior.** With `_coord_store_port` unset (offline, external launcher / SPMD, elastic, or an older frontend during version skew), `world_pg_store` stays `None` and both changed call sites degrade to their previous form.

**How the store address travels.** One field added to the existing handshake copy-list covers remote (headless) MP engines; local engines receive it in the config at spawn, Ray actors in the actor-constructor config, and workers inherit it when the executor spawns them. Non-MoE MP engines are rewritten to independent dp=1 (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) and never consume the store; the non-MoE case that needs it is the Ray DP backend (no such rewrite), which is covered via the actor-constructor config.

**Lifetimes.** The coordination store lives on the `launch_core_engines()` frame, which runs `wait_for_engine_startup()` after its yield — so it stays alive exactly until all engines are ready, then is discarded. The world group's own rendezvous TCPStore is a separate, process-lifetime object. The two are deliberately not merged: reusing the coordination store as the group's rendezvous store would make the frontend process a runtime dependency of every engine collective.

## Reproduction & A/B results

Hardware: single GB200 node (aarch64, 4 GPUs), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (2026-08-04). Arm "fixed" = same image with this patch applied. Model: a 9-layer MoE test checkpoint with dummy weights (`--load-format dummy`); any small MoE reproduces, e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`.

Two experiments, all rounds on identical images/configs:

1. **Deterministic squatter**: start `vllm serve <moe> -dp 4 -tp 1` with `VLLM_PORT` set (making the config-time probe deterministic); a squatter process waits until the EngineCore processes exist (probe done, world-group bind not yet) and then binds-and-holds `[VLLM_PORT, VLLM_PORT+16)`:

   ```python
   # squat.py — run alongside the server, after EngineCore appears in its log
   import socket, time
   socks = []
   for p in range(42000, 42016):
       s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("0.0.0.0", p)); s.listen(); socks.append(s)
   time.sleep(600)
   ```

2. **Concurrent cold start (RL shape, no artificial interference)**: two `-dp 2 -tp 1` instances on one node, same `VLLM_PORT`, started simultaneously.

| experiment | main | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| squatter | **6/6 startup failure** (EADDRINUSE at world-group init, process hangs) | **8/8 healthy** (full band squatted) |
| concurrent cold start | **6/6 startup failure** | **6/6 healthy** (both instances) |

The failure mode on main matches field reports: the server does not exit — it hangs after minutes of model loading, which is the expensive way to fail.

## Relationship to existing work

- **#36330** (merged) introduced the coordination-store mechanism and fixed the stateless-group half of this defect; this PR completes the class by migrating the world group. Same defect statement, same cure.
- Related symptom reports: #39015 (EADDRINUSE on 29500-family defaults), #28498 (port-conflict tracker), #14919.
- Sibling PRs for other port-race sites: #50960 (zmq shm broadcast, merged), #50965 (`get_open_port` reserved-range livelock, merged), #50969 (Ray executor TCPStore host), #50999 (single-node executor `file://` rendezvous).
- Duplicate-work check: [open PRs touching dp master port](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+data_parallel_master_port), [open PRs mentioning 39015](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+39015+in%3Abody) — none migrate the world group to the coordination store.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -k "world_group or coordination_store"
```

- A/B experiments above (deterministic + statistical, 26 rounds total, zero exceptions).
- Existing DP suites (`tests/v1/test_async_llm_dp.py`, distributed tests) exercise the changed init path end to end; behavior without a coord store is unchanged by construction.

## Test Result

- See table above; `pre-commit` clean on the changed files (the forbidden-import hook's `pickle` flag on `parallel_state.py` is its pre-existing allowlisted import surfacing under a worktree path prefix).

## AI Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, the A/B experiments, and drafting this description. Opened as a draft for the submitter's final line-by-line review before requesting maintainer review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Reproduced nightly A/B (2026-08-07)

Actual run: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on h200-0 (baseline, image `sha256:40e504de…`) and h200-1 (PR head, image `sha256:928dde7d…`), each with 8× H200. The repro calls `init_distributed_environment()` with the same coordinated-online-DP branch this PR changes. A squatter binds the exact port returned by the baseline `get_next_dp_init_port()` after its probe socket closes and before `init_process_group()` starts.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| base `24c939c47d` | `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError`: `EADDRINUSE` while TCPStore listens |
| PR head `ad4aec4ed` | passes: rank 0 binds `:0`, creates the TCPStore from that held socket, then initializes the world group |

To reproduce: checkout base/head, run the same nightly image with `--network host`; set `data_parallel_size=2`, inject a `get_next_dp_init_port()` that returns a port a background `socket.bind()+listen()` has just claimed, and call `init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, backend="gloo")`. The base follows `tcp://<squatted-port>` and fails; the head uses `_coord_store_port` and succeeds. This is deterministic rather than a timing-only cold-start test.

## Non-MoE DP completion (2026-08-07)

The original coordination-store creation was incorrectly gated on `model_config.is_moe`.  This misses ordinary replicated DP models: `init_distributed_environment()` still creates the DP-expanded world group whenever `data_parallel_size > 1`, so it fell back to the pre-allocated `_data_parallel_master_port_list` and retained the exact probe-to-bind race.

Deterministic nightly A/B (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`) on both h200-0 and h200-1 uses production `launch_core_engines()` with a non-MoE DP=2 config and a fake process manager.  PR head `ad4aec4ed` fails `AssertionError: non-MoE DP did not receive a coordination TCPStore`; commit `2827357fb7` passes on both hosts: `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`.  The added focused pytest passes, and ruff, mypy-3.10, and full changed-file pre-commit pass.

The change removes only the MoE gate; all online local rank-0 DP launches now retain the coordination TCPStore until EngineCore startup, allowing rank 0 to bind-and-hold the actual world-group listener before publishing its port.

## Real GPU serving validation (2026-08-07)

On h200-0, mounted the PR head into `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` and ran `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18018 --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --data-parallel-rpc-port 0 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enforce-eager` on two H200 GPUs. Both non-MoE DP EngineCores initialized, the API reached `GET /v1/models` (200), and `POST /v1/completions` returned a completion. This exercises the same non-MoE DP launch branch protected by commit `2827357fb7`.

## Fresh non-MoE nightly confirmation (2026-08-07)

After the follow-up commit `2827357fb7`, h200-1 re-ran production `launch_core_engines()` for non-MoE, MP DP=2 in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (head `sha256:928dde7d…`, `--gpus all --network host`). The current head printed `PASS non-MoE DP received a coordination TCPStore`. This confirms the rebase/current branch still covers the non-MoE variant that `ad4aec4ed` initially omitted.

## port=0 simplification validation (2026-08-08)

Commit `613d35eacf` replaces the manual socket bind/listen/detach + `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=...)` handoff with `TCPStore(port=0)` + `.port` readback (review suggestion). Validated by driving the real modified `init_distributed_environment()` in two spawned processes (dp=2 config with `_coord_store_port` set): rank 0 created the world-group store on a kernel-assigned port and published it, rank 1 read it from the coordination store and connected, `init_process_group(store=)` formed the 2-rank world group, and a gloo `all_reduce` returned `[2.0, 2.0]` with clean exits. ruff check/format pass. The earlier GPU serving validation predates this commit; it should be repeated before undrafting.

## Test coverage (2026-10-06)

Two tests, both CPU-only (gloo), run as part of `pytest v1/engine`:

- `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_world_group_port.py`: two spawned processes bring up a DP=2 world group with the pre-allocated port already taken by another socket. With a coordination store the group binds its own port and both ranks all-reduce correctly; without one the pre-allocated path still works. Checked against unpatched `main`: the taken-port case fails with `EADDRINUSE` on the pre-allocated port, the fallback case passes. On this branch both pass (27 s).
- `test_coordination_store_held_only_by_the_online_dp_master` (rewritten from the earlier non-MoE test): a table over launch configurations. The online DP master holds a reachable store for both the mp and ray backends; non-master nodes, offline mode, elastic EP and single-engine deployments do not. Against unpatched `main` the two "holds a store" cases fail and the four "no store" cases pass.

## MI355 CI failure (build 93141) and fix (2026-10-07)

`:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP Extended` hung for 30 minutes in `test_async_llm_dp.py` with DP=2/TP=2 on both attempts, while the L4 run of the same step passed. In each attempt one worker of the DP-rank-1 engine never reached the world-group init: it was stuck on the coordination store (`wait timeout ... keys: /world_pg_port` in the retry), and its three peers then waited 30 minutes on its gloo key.

Root cause: `get_cached_tcp_store_client` caches one connected client per process. `DPEngineCoreProc` populates it in `_init_data_parallel` before it creates the executor, so with the default fork start method every worker inherited the same connected socket, and the two TP siblings of one engine interleaved their requests on it. The L4 run of the same step shows no spawn override either, so it forks as well; whether the interleaving corrupts the stream depends on whether the siblings' requests overlap, and that run did not hit it. The hazard is therefore not ROCm specific. This PR is the first to read the coordination store from workers at init, so the latent cache issue surfaced here.

Fix: the port exchange needs the store once per worker, so it now opens its own short-lived client instead of the process-wide cached one. The cached client itself is still not fork-safe for its other callers (elastic EP); that is pre-existing and left for a follow-up.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Tolerate NaN-corrupted logprobs in engine-core
author: almersawi
body:
## Purpose

Fix a total-outage bug in the Rust frontend's engine-core client: a single request asking for `logprobs`/`prompt_logprobs` while the model produces NaN logits permanently kills the client — `/health` returns 503 and every subsequent request (including ones with no logprobs) fails with `engine-core error: messagepack ext value decode failed: token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs` until process restart.

Rank 0 is an engine output that must be accepted: the sampler computes the rank as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), which is 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN because every `>=` comparison against NaN is false. The decode failure is frame-scoped (one bad row fails the whole batched `EngineCoreOutputs` payload), happens on the shared output-reader path, and is recorded as a sticky health error, so a per-request data anomaly becomes a server-wide outage.

**Fix:** in `PositionLogprobs::from_decoded_row`, accept and preserve `sampled_rank = 0` along with the engine's original logprob values. This keeps decoding valid for the other requests in the batch. The existing Rust OpenAI serving helper converts NaN and negative infinity to `-9999.0` when constructing HTTP responses; engine-core decoding preserves the numerical results for all consumers.

**Why this does not duplicate existing PRs:**
- #48585 fixes the same *class* of defect (non-finite logprobs reaching the serving layer) but in the **Python** frontend, and for logprob *values*, not ranks. This PR addresses the Rust engine-client rank-zero decode failure; the Rust HTTP helper already handles NaN and negative infinity.
- #50725 is a different code path (process abort from an empty stop string); it only shares the blast-radius pattern.
- #50002 proposed aborting requests on optional NaN detection and was superseded by #50283; this PR handles rank-zero payloads that reach the frontend.
- #45060 establishes all-NaN logits as a real engine state vLLM already handles elsewhere.

Healthy payloads retain their existing behavior. Model evaluation N/A: this changes wire-payload decode tolerance while preserving the engine's numerical output.

AI assistance was used for the original fix and the follow-up changes and tests. The follow-up preserves rank 0 and raw engine values and adds coverage for the existing HTTP conversion.

## Test Plan

Two regression tests cover the layer boundary:

1. `zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates` decodes a shared `EngineCoreOutputs` batch, preserving rank 0, NaN, and negative infinity in both sample and prompt logprobs while keeping the healthy request intact.
2. `chat_logprobs_clamps_nan_and_negative_infinity_for_json` verifies that the existing OpenAI response conversion emits `-9999.0` for NaN and negative infinity while preserving a finite logprob.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server -E 'package(vllm-engine-core-client) | test(routes::openai::utils::logprobs::tests)'`: **118 passed**.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and commit-time pre-commit hooks: passed.

Commands ran from `rust/` with a fresh short `TMPDIR` for tests and an existing Cargo target directory. No GPU was required.

Model evaluation N/A: the change preserves the engine's numerical output and adjusts frontend decode tolerance.

---

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. (N/A — internal decode-tolerance fix, no docs affected)
</details>

title: [Bugfix][MLA] TritonMLA: fix illegal memory access on causal multi-token decode
author: olka-amd
body:
## Purpose
`TritonMLA` declared single-token decode support, so a speculative-decode verify block reached `forward_mqa` unflattened: `query_len * num_reqs` query rows against `num_reqs` rows of `block_table` / `seq_lens`. `decode_attention_fwd` launches one program per query row and indexes `tl.load(B_Seqlen + cur_batch)`, so every row past `num_decodes` is an out-of-bounds read.

Reaching it takes a group whose reorder threshold is raised past 1. Ordinary MLA spec decode does not qualify: `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` inherits `query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY`, so multi-token queries route to prefill. The threshold is raised by the non-causal route (DSpark draft) which sets its flags after the base `__init__` has asserted `SINGLE_ONLY ⇒ threshold == 1`.
`build()` then splits a *causal* batch with the raised threshold, and `forward_mqa` expands tables only under `if not causal`. Where that happens there is no fallback on either affected platform:

- **NVIDIA sm_86** — `triton_mla` is the only MLA backend whose   `supports_compute_capability` admits `major == 8` (CUTLASS/FlashInfer require 10,   FlashAttn 9, FlashMLA 9 or 10). Reported as `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal   memory access` (#51848).
- **ROCm without AITER MLA** — `rocm.py` falls back to `[TRITON_MLA]` alone.

Fixes #51848.

On Kimi-K3 + DSpark, TP8, MI325: (18.01 → 45.00 tok/s), no quality regression (verified on gsm8k: **95%**)

## The fix
`decode_attention_fwd` has no causal flag, but it reads each row's KV extent from `seq_lens`. A uniform verify block is a contiguous suffix, so intra-block causality is expressible as per-row extents: flatten to one decode row per query token and give row `t` extent `seq_len - (query_len - 1 - t)`.

1. `forward_mqa`: derive `query_len` from `q.shape[0] // seq_lens.shape[0]` and    expand `block_table` / `seq_lens` to match, causal or non-causal.
2. `_cudagraph_support` → `UNIFORM_BATCH`, `query_len_support` → `UNIFORM`, so the    reorder threshold admits `query_len > 1`. `attn_logits` workspace grows to match  (workspace locks after capture).
3. `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` asserts layers agree on  `non_causal_multi_token_decode` instead of `any()`, so a non-causal draft group cannot be merged with a causal target group.

## Testing

Validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`ba07e4a48f`), gfx942. Rebased onto `origin/main` `9fd750f00d`

### Unit tests

`tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` (new, 15) plus `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (87): **102 passed**. The new file replaces the kernel with a spy and asserts on the `block_table` and `seq_lens` the backend actually submits, so it needs no GPU or Triton runtime.

### The decode path actually taken

`tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` already covers this: `spec_decode_small` (4x4) and `spec_decode_medium` (6x8) install an ngram `SpeculativeConfig`, with `torch` SDPA as reference. `decode_attention_fwd` was instrumented to confirm which path runs.

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 \
  pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q -k "1.0-1.0-auto-1-"
```

| | result | TritonMLA decode launches |
|---|---|---|
| before, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 0 (routed to prefill) |
| after, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 4, causal staircase |
| before, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 12 (single-token) |
| after, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 16 (12 + 4 causal) |

The "after, all batch specs" row re-verified on 2026-08-21 against the final tree, with 16 launches and the same shapes:

```
x2  q_rows=1   bt_rows=1   seq_lens[:8]=[1024]
x4  q_rows=2   bt_rows=2   seq_lens[:8]=[32, 40]
x2  q_rows=3   bt_rows=3   seq_lens[:8]=[512, 1024, 2048]
x2  q_rows=8   bt_rows=8   seq_lens[:8]=[128, 256, 512, 1024]
x2  q_rows=16  bt_rows=16  seq_lens[:8]=[125, 126, 127, 128, 253, 254, 255, 256]
x2  q_rows=32  bt_rows=32  seq_lens[:8]=[2048]
x2  q_rows=48  bt_rows=48  seq_lens[:8]=[505, 506, 507, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512]
```

Extents match `seq_len - (query_len-1-t)`. The 12 single-token launches are unchanged in count and shape, so the ordinary decode path does not regress. 
`bt_rows == q_rows` throughout, confirming the `block_table` expansion tracks the flatten. Skips are prefill-backend unavailability on this platform, not decode skips.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, greedy (`temperature=0`, `seed=42`), `max_tokens=1024`, 8 concurrent clients, raw completions:

| | |
|---|---|
| accuracy | **0.9507** (1254 / 1319) |
| mean acceptance length | **3.279** of max 4.0, 40,823 drafts |
| throughput | 0.449 q/s, 46.0 tok/s, 135,175 output tokens |
| wall | 2,936 s |
| worker faults / NaNs | none |

Configuration: gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8 + EP, target `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, drafter `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on `TRITON_MLA` via `--attention-backend`, `dspark` method with 3 speculative tokens, 32,384 ctx. 

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors   --enable-auto-tool-choice   --tool-call-parser kimi_k3   --reasoning-parser kimi_k3   --enable-prompt-tokens-details   --mm-encoder-tp-mode data   --max-model-len 32384 --max-num-seqs 8  --speculative-config '{ "model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens":3, "method": "dspark", "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}'
```


Spec-Bench:
```bash
---------------Speculative Decoding---------------
Acceptance rate (%):                     63.11     
Acceptance length:                       2.89      
Drafts:                                  16798     
Draft tokens:                            50394     
Accepted tokens:                         31804     
Per-position acceptance (%):
  Position 0:                            81.74     
  Position 1:                            61.65     
  Position 2:                            45.94     
==================================================
```
**The drafter is on TRITON_MLA precisely because this is the path the PR fixes.**

**There is no same-flags unpatched baseline.** Without this patch the above configuration is the crash the PR fixes, so "unpatched, same flags" does not produce a number. This run is evidence that the causal flatten is correct under sustained load, not a before/after comparison.

Independently corroborated by @maeehart on gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8+EP, 7 spec tokens, same target/draft backend pairing, 262144 ctx: **GSM8K 95.6% strict and flexible over all 1,319 questions**, needle retrieval passed at 65K/131K/250K, 98.26% prefix-cache hit, no faults or NaNs. Their run bundles #50578 and AITER
fixes, so it is integration evidence rather than an isolated measurement. 

@reger-men's gfx950 throughput numbers were obtained with a different implementation and are explicitly **not** a measurement of this PR.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cudagraph mode | PIECEWISE (downgraded) | **FULL + PIECEWISE** |
| throughput | 13.01 tok/s | **61.3 tok/s (4.0×)** |
| per-step latency | 233.9 ms | **50.4 ms** |

Removing per-launch overhead also removed cross-rank arrival skew that had been making TP collectives spin-wait: `vllm::all_reduce` 2.157 s (60.8% of Self CUDA) → 0.061 s (2.85%), arrival spread 313.8 µs → 7.1 µs.

## Correctness

Same config (61.3 tok/s, including two unrelated tuning changes not in this PR):

| benchmark | result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full test set (1319) | **97.2%** (1282/1319), 95% CI [96.3, 98.1] |
| GPQA Diamond, 0-shot CoT (198) | **90.9%** flexible / **90.4%** strict |

Hardware:

- [x] Boots with FULL cudagraph capture, no downgrade message
- [x] GSM8K 97.2%, GPQA Diamond 90.9%
- [x] Concurrency sweep 1→128, zero errors across 100 800 generated tokens
- [x] Causal-tail A/B showing acceptance is unaffected
- [x] NVIDIA sm_86 — [nickus](https://github.com/nickus) on 4x RTX 3090: illegal memory access without the patch, serves with it


## AI assistance

AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

## Related work
- [#47310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47310)  predates this PR and proposes the `query_len_support` half of this change and diagnoses the same flag coupling — credit there for that analysis. It has gone stale: Unmodified since 2026-07-09.
-  [#51171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51171)  (open, 2026-08-05) also corrects cudagraph support reporting for  non-causal draft groups, but keys a conditional `get_cudagraph_support`   override on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. That leaves the *causal* path   still declaring single-token support — which is this bug. Causal is the base   case, so the flag pair is set unconditionally here. The two changes are   compatible; #51171 additionally moves an AITER host sync out of `forward_mqa`,   which this PR does not touch.
- [#51685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51685) (open, 2026-08-10) reworks the same decode path for a native fp8 KV cache (`triton_mla.py` +97/-33). Different purpose, no overlap in intent.
-  [#51705](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51705)  (open, 2026-08-10) is a Kimi-K3 DSpark decode-context-parallelism  feature (+760/-107) that happens to carry this PR's `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`
  fix verbatim — the same `any()` → set-and-pop rewrite under a byte-identical   assertion message, differing only in a local variable name. This PR is six days   earlier and is scoped to the bug; #51705 needs the same correction as a   prerequisite for its own grouping work. 
- [#51848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51848) is an issue, not a PR, and was closed on 2026-08-11. It is the independent sm_86 report of this bug. Its reporter confirmed there that this PR supersedes it and declined to open a competing one.
- [#50911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50911) is complementary: the non-causal draft path on TokenSpeed/NVIDIA. No file overlap. 
- [#52218](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52218) (draft, opened 2026-08-13) — *"[Attention] Support speculative decode in Triton MLA"*. Same fix, same mechanism: uniform multi-token query support, the verify block flattened to decode rows, causal prefix lengths per row, padding rows clamped, split-KV workspace grown. This PR predates it by nine days and is a superset: #52218 is a draft touching only `triton_mla.py`, and does not correct `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`, so a non-causal draft group can still be merged into a causal target group.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Mamba all-mode CPU offload boundary alignment
author: jairitAge
body:
Fixes #51094.

## Summary

- Treat `mamba_cache_mode="all"` like `"align"` when constraining OffloadingConnector hit windows.
- Recompute the last token at an exact offload-chunk boundary instead of restoring a Mamba point state that already includes it.
- Extend the existing Mamba CPU-offload boundary test to cover both cache modes.

## Root cause

`resolve_mamba_align_size()` only enabled boundary alignment for `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. In `"all"` mode, an exact chunk-boundary lookup could return the full boundary while restoring the point state at that boundary. Mamba then resumed from a state that had already consumed the last prompt token, silently changing generated output.

## Testing

- All pre-commit hooks applicable to the changed files pass (ruff, format, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and repository validation hooks).
- Pytest collection confirms the existing GPU test now expands to separate `align` and `all` cases.
- Direct helper validation: `none -> None`, `align -> 32`, `all -> 32`.
- H100 model test on current `main` (`43c4bdca`) with Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, OffloadingConnector, `mamba_cache_mode=all`, and a 2816-token exact boundary: cold run and CPU-refetch run produced the same 32 token IDs; connector debug showed the refetch constrained to 1408 tokens.
- The issue reproduction on v0.25.1 documents the negative control: without this change, the exact-boundary refetch changes output.

## Duplicate check

I searched open issues and PRs for `mamba_cache_mode=all`, `resolve_mamba_align_size`, and exact OffloadingConnector boundaries. #50409 concerns align-mode local replay-boundary caching and does not cover all-mode CPU-offload hit-window alignment. No PR currently fixes #51094.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with source analysis, patch preparation, and test execution. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the reported test results.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Let pooling requests set padding
author: Hert4
body:
## Purpose

Pooling endpoints build `TokenizeParams` from a fixed field list in
`_build_pooling_tok_params`, not from `tokenization_kwargs`, and that list had no padding
field. So there was no value a caller could send to `/v1/embeddings` that pads the prompt —
offline `LLM.embed` accepts `tokenization_kwargs={"padding": "max_length"}`, online had no
equivalent.

Models trained with a fixed sequence length and no attention mask are silently wrong
without it. SigLIP is the case that surfaced this: padding tokens are part of the input and
the pooled embedding is read from the last position, so unpadded text embeddings are not
comparable with the image embeddings. The request returns 200 with a correctly shaped
vector; only the values are wrong.

## Fix

Add a `padding` field to the pooling request, taking the Transformers spellings
`"max_length"` and `"do_not_pad"`, and apply it through the existing
`TokenizeParams.with_kwargs` — which is already where vLLM translates that vocabulary. No
new mapping logic.

```python
# offline
llm.embed(prompts, tokenization_kwargs={"padding": "max_length", "max_length": 64})
# online
extra_body={"padding": "max_length"}
```

A closed set rather than a free-form dict, so what a client may send online stays explicit.
Transformers' `padding=False` is deliberately not accepted: `with_kwargs` guards the padding
mapping with a truthiness check, so `False` is popped and silently ignored, while
`"do_not_pad"` works. A rejected value is better than one that quietly does nothing. Fixing
that guard looks like a separate change.

`vision_embedding_offline.py` and `vision_embedding_online.py` both already had a
`run_siglip`, and both embedded text without padding — demonstrating this bug rather than
the fix. Both now pass it.

Whether a model should be able to declare padding as a default, so callers do not have to
know, is a separate question and not in this PR.

## Test plan

`test_padding` sits next to `test_truncate_prompt_tokens` in
`tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py`. Against a real server it asserts that
`padding="max_length"` raises the prompt token count, that `"do_not_pad"` matches the
default, and that an unsupported value is rejected.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py::test_padding -q
```

## Test result

Run on an NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), together with the existing truncation test as a
control:

```
tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py::test_padding             PASSED
tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py::test_truncate_prompt_tokens PASSED
2 passed in 33.18s
```

Separately, serving `google/siglip2-base-patch16-224 --runner pooling --max-model-len 64`
and comparing `/v1/embeddings` against a HF reference tokenized with
`padding="max_length", max_length=64`:

| request | cosine vs HF reference |
|---|---|
| `extra_body={"padding": "max_length"}` | 1.000000 |
| no padding | 0.616077, 0.644452 |

The padded result matches the reference exactly. Without it the embedding is not usable for
retrieval, and before this PR there was no way to ask for it over HTTP.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Revert adaptive C128A metadata packing
author: tobymao
body:
## Summary

Revert the adaptive C128A top-k width and packed persistent-buffer views introduced by #50004.

The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. With #50004, runtime metadata writes packed rows using a batch-dependent `active_topk_width`, while the captured consumer retained the capture-time row stride. Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets.

This change restores:

- `c128a_max_compressed` as the metadata width
- capacity-strided slices of the persistent decode and prefill buffers
- each persistent buffer's `stride(0)` for Triton metadata writes
- removal of the test that asserted the packed layout being reverted

Fixes #52448.

## Validation

```text
git diff --check
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py
```

All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import, and forbidden-import checks.

The full revert was also evaluated with the exact #52448 request on 2x NVIDIA GB300 using `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` revision `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062`, TP=2 plus expert parallelism, DSpark-7, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max_model_len=70000`, concurrency 32, and `max_tokens=16384`:

- 256 priming requests plus 256 measured requests
- 0/256 issue-signature hits
- 0 request errors and 0 `length` finishes
- 253 `tool_calls` finishes and 3 `stop` finishes
- 8.445 s median measured latency

## Contribution notes

- Not a duplicate: `52448 in:body` found no other open PR. The open C128A/sparse-MLA keyword matches (#48805, #41836, and #41834) address warmup, prefill, or model enablement rather than reverting #50004. This updates the existing #51318 instead of opening another PR.
- AI assistance was used for investigation, patch preparation, validation, and this PR update. The submitting human must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before merge.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states
author: ivanium
body:
## Summary

Fix Mooncake Store persistence for Mamba `align` mode by saving the exact core-selected boundary-state blocks and keeping those physical blocks alive until every worker rank has finished the asynchronous store attempt.

This fixes a correctness bug that could persist null, stale/reassigned, or live speculative Mamba state under a valid prefix hash. A later external prefix hit could then restore poisoned recurrent state and produce garbled or runaway output.

## Root cause

Mooncake's normal save path resolved each group's source block positionally from a worker-side snapshot of the request's block IDs. That is valid for append-only attention block tables, but a Mamba `align` table is sparse and mutable:

- superseded state positions are replaced by the null block and their physical blocks are freed;
- speculative scratch blocks are relocated to different logical positions;
- the connector's block-ID mirror is append-only and does not observe those in-place changes.

Consequently, a positional Mamba save could interpret `NULL_BLOCK_ID` as a physical source, or read a block that had already been freed, reassigned, or was still speculative, while using the correct chained prefix hash as its key. Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` deduplication could then preserve the bad value and prevent a later correct save from replacing it.

The production symptom was exposed by the DSpark/EAGLE lookup path landing on an affected interior key. Without that path, a later valid CoW boundary key could win and mask the corruption.

## Design

- Core emits exact `(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens)` entries for committed Mamba `align` boundary states, including the CoW target for a sub-block partial tail. The connector never reconstructs these source IDs positionally.
- Mooncake excludes Mamba groups from the normal positional `store_mask`; exact boundary handoffs are the only Mamba writer. The normal path also skips null or missing source IDs for every group as a defense-in-depth guard.
- The scheduler claims each accepted physical block with `BlockPool.touch()` before it can be recycled. Consumer-only roles are gated before claiming or queueing handoffs.
- Each claimed block receives a monotonic handoff ID. A one-ID/one-pin mapping makes reference release and the bounded in-flight capacity exact, even though a request-level batch ID could work while all entries in a request complete together.
- Workers report a cross-rank completion watermark. After seeing its first handoff, a rank reports watermark `0` while that handoff is pending rather than omitting metadata; this prevents aggregation from ignoring a lagging rank and releasing a block early. Dedup, successful upload, pressure drop, cancellation, and store failure are all terminal outcomes for lifetime purposes.
- The scheduler releases the connector-owned refs only through `BlockPool.free_blocks()` after the aggregated watermark says every rank is terminal. The configurable in-flight cap bounds pinned GPU blocks if acknowledgements stop; saves beyond the cap remain best-effort and are dropped.
- Resumed prefills use the tracked prefill/save boundary, not the request's original prompt length, so replayed generated tokens retain the same cross-group save coverage.
- Mamba speculative scratch relocation remains an in-table move, but now fails closed unless `BlockPool.is_block_writable()` confirms the block is non-null, exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`), and unhashed. If shared or pinned speculative blocks become valid in the future, this path must use CoW instead of relocating them.

This implementation is intentionally limited to Mamba `align` mode. Mooncake Store's configuration validation rejects incompatible non-align/`all` Mamba layouts; this PR does not add `all`-mode support.

## Retention semantics

`VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` remains effective even though Mooncake's positional `store_mask` is false for Mamba:

1. Core `MambaManager.cache_blocks()` applies the retention policy first.
2. Only retained/materialized states receive a block hash.
3. Handoff emission skips null or unhashed blocks.
4. Mooncake stores the exact retained states from those handoffs.

Therefore dense default retention, sparse interval checkpoints, and replay-boundary behavior are preserved. External persistence is still best-effort: an eligible checkpoint may be absent if the handoff cap is reached or the store operation fails.

## Scope and overlap

This is not duplicate work:

- #50359 validates external lookup boundaries.
- #46896 and #46906 concern Mamba all-mode support and retention policy.
- #51362 independently adds the same defensive null/missing-block check to Mooncake's normal save loop. That check is included here, but this PR also removes unsafe positional Mamba saving and fixes exact source selection, asynchronous lifetime, retention-aware handoff, partial-tail handling, and speculative ownership. In that sense, this PR subsumes #51362's behavior rather than relying on it.

## Validation

Focused Mooncake Store and prefix-cache suites were run through the final design, including exact block-ID handoff, dense and sparse retention, partial tails, resumed prefills, more than two Mamba groups, null/missing sources, consumer skip-save behavior, cross-rank watermarking, bounded pins, failure paths, and exclusive speculative ownership.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py
```

Result: 183 passed. Additional focused reruns after the watermark, save-gate, and ownership-invariant changes passed (195 tests), and a broader Mooncake Store + prefix-cache run in the k3-debug container on a GB300 worker passed (219 tests). Ruff and `git diff --check` also passed.

Serving/model evaluation on `k3-pd-mooncake aa-lcr`:

- post-fix: 0/200 garbled responses;
- `llm_judge`: approximately 0.77/0.76;
- external prefix hit rate: approximately 91–98%;
- pre-fix baseline: garbled/runaway outputs, with `llm_judge` approximately 0.76/0.78.

No model kernels or numerical computation were changed.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending the final submission.

title: [BugFix] Preserve divergent FA hits with external Mamba state
author: majunze2001
body:
The original fix is by @ywang96, with a follow-up refinement by @ivanium

## Summary

`truncate_computed_blocks()` asserts that every KV cache group holds at least
`num_computed_tokens // block_size` blocks. For a hybrid (full-attention + Mamba) model
served with a KV connector, a Mamba group can legitimately hold fewer: its blocks are whole
recurrent state, not per-token KV, and an external hit can supply the state at a boundary the
local group no longer covers. The assert turns that benign divergence into an engine-fatal
`AssertionError`, killing the prefill workers mid-run.

Fix: keep both asserts for groups that must cover the endpoint, and clamp only `MambaSpec`
groups.

```python
assert num_computed_tokens % manager.block_size == 0
num_blocks = num_computed_tokens // manager.block_size
if isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec):
    num_blocks = min(num_blocks, len(group_blocks))
else:
    assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
```

A blanket `min()` over all groups would also stop the crash, but would silently mask a short
attention group — a real bug if it ever happens. Scoping to `MambaSpec` keeps that loud.

## Root cause

`truncate_computed_blocks()` has one caller, `Scheduler.schedule()`:

```python
if partial_tail and ext_tokens > partial_tail:
    new_computed_blocks = self.kv_cache_manager.truncate_computed_blocks(
        new_computed_blocks, block_aligned_local
    )
```

Both conditions must hold, which is why this is not hit by ordinary prefix caching:

- `partial_tail != 0` — the local hit ends on a prefix-match boundary that is not a block
  boundary. Requires `--prefix-match-unit` finer than the KV block size. For Kimi-K3 the
  platform raises the attention block to 1536 so the attention page covers the Mamba page,
  and `--prefix-match-unit 128` then makes a non-zero tail the common case.
- `ext_tokens > partial_tail` — the connector must hold *more* of the prefix than the local
  cache retains. `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` reports tokens beyond `block_aligned_local`,
  so when store and local cache hold the same prefix length the two are equal and the
  harmless `elif partial_tail:` branch runs instead. Divergence needs local eviction while
  the external store retains.

Both are satisfied by long chunked prefills: the request re-enters scheduling per chunk and
re-runs the lookup against its own earlier chunks, while concurrent requests churn the GPU
pool that the external store outlives.

Introduced in #49502, which added both the function and its caller. Still present on `main`.

## Reproduction

A PD deployment on 6 nodes (prefill 2 x TP8, decode 4 x TP1 -> DP16/EP16), MultiConnector
with NIXL plus MooncakeStore, `--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128`, attention
block 1536, 800 GB store against a 1,980,479-token GPU pool.

16 requests of 98,944 prompt tokens each (`64 * 1536 + 640`, so the tail is
128-aligned and not 1536-aligned), raw token-id prompts, concurrency 8. Prefill died 7
requests in:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:797   in schedule
    self.kv_cache_manager.truncate_computed_blocks(
vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:792 in truncate_computed_blocks
    assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
AssertionError
```

All 7 requests that reached prefill logged external loads. The store was at 78% with zero
`insufficient space` warnings, so capacity pressure is not involved.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (bash + curl, no deps)</summary>

Two passes: the first populates the connector, the second replays the same prompts against
it. A single pass on a cold store writes but never reads (`Get=0`) and cannot reach the
guarded branch, so it would pass misleadingly — the script reads
`vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` and reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS when no
external hit occurred. Prompts are raw token-id lists so prefix lengths are exact.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: ./repro_truncate_assert.sh <router_port> [num_prompts] [prompt_tokens]
#   METRICS_URL=http://<prefill-host>:<port>/metrics  # recommended; else INCONCLUSIVE
# Exit: 0 fix verified, 1 reproduced (non-200), 2 inconclusive (no external reads).
set -uo pipefail

PORT=${1:?usage: repro_truncate_assert.sh <router_port> [num_prompts] [prompt_tokens]}
NPROMPTS=${2:-16}
BLOCK=${BLOCK:-1536}          # attention block size the platform picks for the hybrid model
LEN=${3:-$((64 * BLOCK + 640))}   # 640 = multiple of the 128 match unit, not of 1536
CONC=${CONC:-8}
MAXTOK=${MAXTOK:-4}
URL="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/completions"
MODEL=${MODEL:-moonshotai/Kimi-K3}

WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# x stays below 2^31 so x*1103515245 fits a 64-bit signed int exactly.
gen_tokens() {
  local seed=$1 n=$2 x i; local -a a
  x=$((seed * 7919 + 13))
  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
    x=$(((x * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF))
    a[i]=$((1000 + x % 90000))
  done
  local IFS=,; printf '%s' "${a[*]}"
}

ext_hits() {
  [ -n "${METRICS_URL:-}" ] || return 0
  curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '/^vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total/{print $2; exit}'
}

send() {
  local i=$1 t0 code dt
  t0=$(date +%s)
  code=$(curl -sS -o "$WORK/resp_$i.json" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1800 \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              --data-binary "@$WORK/body_$i.json" "$URL" 2>"$WORK/err_$i")
  dt=$(($(date +%s) - t0))
  printf 'req %3d  HTTP %s  %4ds' "$i" "$code" "$dt"
  [ "$code" != 200 ] && printf '   <<< FAILURE  %s' \
    "$(head -c 200 "$WORK/resp_$i.json" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n')"
  printf '\n'
}
export -f send; export WORK URL

echo "prompts: $NPROMPTS x $LEN tokens, concurrency $CONC, tail mod $BLOCK = $((LEN % BLOCK))"
[ $((LEN % BLOCK)) -eq 0 ] && { echo "!! block-aligned: partial_tail would be 0" >&2; exit 2; }

for ((i = 0; i < NPROMPTS; i++)); do
  { printf '{"model":"%s","prompt":[' "$MODEL"; gen_tokens "$i" "$LEN"
    printf '],"max_tokens":%d,"temperature":0}' "$MAXTOK"; } > "$WORK/body_$i.json"
done

fails=0; declare -A delta
for pass in 1 2; do
  echo; echo "--- pass $pass ---"
  before=$(ext_hits)
  seq 0 $((NPROMPTS - 1)) | xargs -P "$CONC" -I{} bash -c 'send {}' | tee "$WORK/p$pass.txt"
  after=$(ext_hits)
  n=$(grep -c FAILURE "$WORK/p$pass.txt" || true); fails=$((fails + n))
  [ -n "$before" ] && [ -n "$after" ] && \
    delta[$pass]=$(awk -v a="$before" -v b="$after" 'BEGIN{printf "%d", b-a}')
  echo "  external hits this pass: ${delta[$pass]:-unknown}   non-200: $n"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && break
done

echo
[ "$fails" -gt 0 ] && { echo "REPRODUCED -- $fails non-200; check prefill for the assert"; exit 1; }
[ -z "${METRICS_URL:-}" ] && { echo "INCONCLUSIVE -- no METRICS_URL, cannot prove the connector was read"; exit 2; }
[ "${delta[2]:-0}" -le 0 ] && { echo "INCONCLUSIVE -- pass 2 had no external hits; raise num_prompts"; exit 2; }
echo "PASS -- $((NPROMPTS * 2)) requests, 0 failures, pass 2 served ${delta[2]} tokens externally"
```

</details>

## Test

End-to-end, same recipe and workload, only the patched file differing:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| requests completed | 7 of 16, engine dead | 16 of 16, twice |
| `num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)` asserts | 1 | 0 |
| external loads logged | 28 (7 reqs x 4 ranks) | 64 (16 reqs x 4 ranks) |
| store reads | — | `Get: Req=256/256, Item=7168/7168` |
| connector clients | 8 -> 4 (ranks died) | 8, unchanged |

The second pass is the one that matters: a cold store is written but never read
(`Get=0`), so it cannot exercise the branch. Re-running against the warm store produced
external hits on all 16 requests — more store read traffic than the run that crashed —
with the engine intact.

Unit tests, run inside the built aarch64 image so `vllm._C` is present:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py   20 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k hybrid                       4 passed
```

The 4 cover both parameterizations of `test_hybrid_fa_deeper_hit_uses_external_mamba_state`
and of `test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector`. They need network for
`ModelConfig("facebook/opt-125m")`; with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and that config uncached they
fail in pydantic validation before reaching any scheduler code.

Lint, using the revisions CI pins (`ruff==0.14.0` from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`;
`requirements/lint.txt` pins only `pre-commit` itself):

```
ruff check                 All checks passed
ruff format --check        3 files already formatted
mypy 2.3.0                 Success: no issues found in 1 source file
```

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "truncate_computed_blocks"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "partial-tail hybrid prefix cache"
```

The first returns nothing: no open PR touches this function. The second returns adjacent
work, none of it this fix:

- #49502 (@Dao007forever) introduced both the function and its caller. **Merged**
  2026-07-27, not open.
- #50507 (@chaunceyjiang, open) extends partial-tail prefix reuse for hybrid models via the
  lookup and restore paths. It does not touch these asserts.
- #46453 (@howarlii, open) reports per-group hit divergence for hybrid + connector, but
  through `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group` convergence and different asserts
  (`num_new_tokens > 0`, `num_locally_computed_tokens <= ...`), and predates #49502.
- #50454 (@gdevenyi, open) is the same class of failure on the native offloading connector,
  asserting in `offloading/scheduler.py`, not through `truncate_computed_blocks`.
- #50630 (@mosafariuk, open) describes the adjacent design gap: no capability flag declares
  which KV kinds may be peeked past a candidate boundary, so each implementation excludes
  Mamba by hand.

No open PR or issue reports this assert.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change: the follow-up commit is co-authored with OpenAI
Codex, and the reproduction, e2e verification, and this description were produced with
Claude Code. A human author reviewed every changed line.

title: [Security] Fix P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion via unbounded peer sessions
author: jperezdealgaba
body:
## Summary

- **Fixes GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9** — an API client could submit many unique non-listening peer addresses via `kv_transfer_params`, each creating 3 ZMQ sockets (DEALER + monitor + PAIR) that were never reaped. ~340 such peers exhausted the ZMQ context's `MAX_SOCKETS=1023` limit, crashing EngineCore.
- Adds five defense-in-depth layers: session capacity limit (`VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS`, default 128), handshake deadline (`VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S`, default 30s), idle session eviction (`VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S`, default 300s), graceful error boundary in `_get_or_create_session`, and expanded ZMQ monitor events (`EVENT_CLOSED`, `EVENT_HANDSHAKE_FAILED_*`).
- All new limits follow existing vLLM patterns (`VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` for env vars, `_reap_unbound_stores` for eviction, `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` for deadlines).

## Changes

### `vllm/envs.py`
- Add `VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS` (default 128), `VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30), `VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 300)

### `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/session.py`
- Track `_connected_at` and `_last_activity_at` timestamps
- Check handshake deadline in `poll()` — marks connection dead if connected but not ready beyond the timeout
- Update `_last_activity_at` on message recv and send

### `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py`
- `_get_or_create_session()`: enforce session cap, catch transport errors (returns `None` instead of propagating)
- `_accept_new_peers()`: reject inbound connections at capacity
- `on_new_request()`: handle `None` from `_get_or_create_session` by recording the request as failed
- New `_reap_idle_sessions()` method called in `_poll_once()` after existing reap methods

### `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/control/zmq.py`
- Expand monitor subscription to include `EVENT_CLOSED` and `EVENT_HANDSHAKE_FAILED_*`
- `_check_monitors()` now drains all pending events per connection and handles all fatal events

### `docs/usage/security.md`
- New "P2P KV-Offload Peer Session Limits" subsection documenting all three env vars and deployment recommendations

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_envs.py::test_p2p_resource_limit_defaults_and_override` — env var defaults and overrides
- [x] `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestSessionCapLimit` — outbound/inbound cap enforcement, existing session reuse, `on_new_request` failure recording (4 tests)
- [x] `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestGetOrCreateSessionErrorBoundary` — transport error returns `None` (1 test)
- [x] `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestIdleSessionEviction` — idle eviction, active kept, pending work protected, disabled when 0 (4 tests)
- [x] `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py::TestHandshakeDeadline` — timeout marks dead, no timeout when ready, activity timestamp updated (3 tests)
- [x] `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py::TestExpandedMonitorEvents` — fatal events set, mask coverage, disconnect detection (3 tests)
- [x] All 195 existing + new P2P tests pass (76 manager + 100 session + 19 zmq transport)

title: [Bugfix] Make DSV4 sparse MLA work end-to-end for plain decode, MTP, and DSpark
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 could not run reliably through the SM120 sparse MLA backend. This fixes the seven defects that blocked it across all three decode modes -- plain decode, MTP, and DSpark -- verified end-to-end on 8xRTX PRO 6000 Blackwell across in-flight batching and prefill/decode disaggregation.

Commits 1-5 unblock DSpark. Commits 6-7 fix a hang that is **not** DSpark-specific: it strands any MTP (`next_n > 1`) server on this backend once the batch drains, and is a pre-existing defect on `main` rather than a regression from this PR. It is filed as #51593, with the full root-cause analysis in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51593#issuecomment-5237934676).

## Why this is not a duplicate

This consolidates #51042 after coordination with the maintainers (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51042#issuecomment-5230492529). @ilmarkov is `Co-authored-by` on the SWA-width commit, whose `amd/rocm.py` hunk and `decode_swa_width` field are his work. Two deliberate design differences are described in that comment.

Duplicate checks run for `dspark`, `sparse MLA SWA width`, `mxfp4 gemm1_alpha`, and `deepseek v4 expert placement`; no other open PR covers the remaining four commits.

For commits 6-7, checks run for `persistent_topk`, `indexer seq_lens spec decode`, and `51593 in:body`. Two open PRs are adjacent but do not overlap:

- **#43970** (MLA indexer / MTP) touches the same two files. Its "drop padded MTP decode slots" applies to the variable-length flatten branch, which computes `seq_len - decode_len` = `0 - 0` = `0` and is already safe. The uniform and native spec-decode paths that produce the negative length are untouched by it. The two changes are complementary and do not conflict.
- **#49139** fixes a different bug in `persistent_topk.cuh` (radix histogram reuse after short rows). Worth flagging the interaction: its precondition is a CTA group processing rows that cross `RADIX_THRESHOLD`, and the out-of-range lengths fixed here cause exactly that spuriously. That PR is still needed for genuinely long rows.

## What is fixed

1. **SWA widths** — non-causal draft batches allocate `decode_swa_indices` wider than `window_size`, but the FlashInfer DSV4 path reshaped with `window_size` and crashed the draft. The dense width is now carried on the metadata. The non-causal width pads to a multiple of 64 (192 for the K=5 shape: 128 sliding-window + 5 draft entries) rather than 128 (256), matching the kernel's 64-entry tile; both dispatch after flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380, and 192 measures 13-16% faster at >=8 tokens.

2. **Workspace lanes** — the DSpark target and draft CUDA graphs retain workspace views concurrently, so one buffer per ubatch let a resize for one orphan the other's live tensor. The second lane is allocated only for V2 DSpark.

3. **Graph replay and draft KV** — `sample_idx_mapping` was zero-filled, so capture executed padding rows that scattered into request slot 0; captured backbone outputs could be freed before replay read their storage; draft KV could be written into physical block 0, the null block. Draft sampling also moves to a disjoint Philox counter range, since the rejection sampler keys both its acceptance uniform and its recovery Gumbel noise by token position.

4. **MXFP4 SwiGLU parameters** — `FlashInferExperts` injected the GPT-OSS activation constants (`gemm1_alpha=1.702`, `gemm1_beta=1.0`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=7.0`) for every mxfp4 weight dtype. DeepSeek V4 uses this path under `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, so its SwiGLU was evaluated with GPT-OSS constants and generation collapsed. GPT-OSS is unaffected: `GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod` supplies the same constants through its quant config, which the added test pins.

5. **SM120 gate** — a FlashInfer build can expose the sparse MLA decode API without carrying the DSV4 specialization a configuration needs. That now fails at model init with the required `(num_q_heads, top_k)` shape instead of an opaque kernel launch failure at the first decode.

6. **Negative indexer context lengths under MTP** — padded decode slots carry `seq_len == 0`, and with `next_n > 1` both spec-decode paths computed a negative per-token context length for the first token of each padded request (`0 - 2 + 0 + 1 = -1`). The sparse-MLA top-k kernels consume `lengths` as `uint32`, so `-1` is read as ~4.29e9. Clamped at 0 in both paths, matching the variable-length path which already yields `0`. With `next_n == 1` the expression collapses to `seq_len`, which is why plain decode never hit this.

7. **Top-k kernels hardened against out-of-range lengths** — `persistent_topk_kernel` cast `lengths` to `uint32` *before* testing `RADIX_THRESHOLD`, so the bogus ~4.29e9 forced the row onto the multi-CTA radix path. Because the `cta_in_group != 0` early exit is decided from the host-side `max_seq_len` while the per-row branch reads device memory, the two disagreed and stranded the group leader on the inter-CTA barrier forever — the kernel never retired, the async output-copy event never fired, and the engine hung waiting for a response that was never sent. The row length is now clamped to `min(stride, max_seq_len)` before any decision, which also removes an out-of-bounds read into the next row. `cooperative_topk` compares signed (so it cannot hang) but then casts to `uint32`, emitting indices `0..TopK-1` instead of `-1` padding; clamped as well.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, gsm8k `n=1319`:

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | acceptance | FlashInfer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| target-only, TP4 | 0.9454 | 0.9454 | — | main @ 7f614b86 |
| DSpark, TP4 | 0.9477 | 0.9477 | 65.5% | main @ 7f614b86 |
| DSpark, TP4+EP4 | 0.9462 | 0.9462 | 67.1% | dc963cc0 |
| DSpark + P/D (mooncake) | 0.9492 | 0.9500 | — | dc963cc0 |

Standard rejection sampling is distribution-preserving, and DSpark lands 0.0023 from target-only against a difference-stderr of ~0.009 (0.26 sigma), on the same checkpoint and the same tree.

MTP on the base checkpoint (`num_nextn_predict_layers = 1`), the configuration that #51593 hangs on, gsm8k `n=1319`:

| configuration | strict-match |
| --- | --- |
| MTP, TP4 (commits 6-7 applied) | 0.9477 |

That sits inside the 0.9454-0.9492 band spanned by the target-only and DSpark rows above, on the same checkpoint and tree, so the clamp does not move accuracy. No unfixed baseline is quoted for this row: without commits 6-7 the same server wedges under the drain reproducer within 30-180 s (see Test plan), and I did not obtain a clean unfixed eval run to compare against.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report Cohere stop sequences correctly
author: taking-lying-flat
body:
## Summary

- report Cohere v2 stop-sequence termination as `STOP_SEQUENCE` instead of `COMPLETE`
- preserve the OpenAI-compatible `stop_reason` through the Cohere streaming state machine
- distinguish matched string stop sequences from EOS and integer stop-token IDs
- add non-streaming and streaming regression coverage

## Root cause

vLLM represents EOS, stop-token, and stop-string termination with `finish_reason="stop"`. A matched stop string is carried separately in `stop_reason`, but the Cohere v2 conversion only inspected `finish_reason`. As a result, its existing `STOP_SEQUENCE` mapping was unreachable in both response paths.

## User impact

Cohere v2 clients can now distinguish a configured stop-sequence match from ordinary completion in both regular responses and SSE `message-end` events.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

I searched open pull requests using `cohere stop_reason`, `cohere stop sequence`, and `Cohere STOP_SEQUENCE`, and found no open PR covering this behavior. PR #45807 addresses the analogous Anthropic Messages API conversion, not the Cohere v2 endpoint or its streaming state.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \

```

title: [Bugfix] Fix cross-batch buffer race corrupting DiskBackend loads
author: fjosw
body:
## Purpose

I had a look at the recently merged DiskBackend for KV offloading (#49644), thanks @chengy-sysu. I noticed a subtle bug in `_do_load`'s double-buffer pipeline: pending H2D events were tracked in a list local to each call and, unlike `_do_store`, never drained before returning. A later `_do_load` call's preadv could therefore overwrite a buffer slot while the previous call's trailing H2D copy was still reading it, silently corrupting the GPU KV cache on reload.

This PR drains the trailing events before `_do_load` returns, mirroring `_do_store`'s existing pattern, and adds a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it.

Tagging @ivanium & @aoshen02  who reviewed https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49644.

AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter.

## Test Plan
```
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend.py -v
```
## Test Result

All 3 tests pass with the fix. `test_do_load_drains_inflight_before_next_batch` fails on main (preadv overwrote slot(s) [0, 1] while a prior batch's H2D was still reading them) and passes with this patch.
