title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid fastsafetensors deadlock for PP draft models
author: gcanlin
body:
## Summary

- keep `fastsafetensors` enabled for the target model, where every pipeline stage participates in its WORLD-group collectives;
- fall back to the standard safetensors loader only for an external draft model when PP > 1;
- apply the PP-safe draft load configuration to EAGLE/EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark without changing PP=1 or other load formats.

Fixes #50959.

## Why a draft-only fallback

With speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism, the external draft model is instantiated only on the last PP stage. `fastsafetensors` currently uses WORLD-group broadcasts, so ranks on that stage wait for ranks that never enter the draft loader.

Using the stage's TP subgroup is not yet a safe workaround: the installed `fastsafetensors` PyTorch adapter passes subgroup-local source ranks to `torch.distributed` as global ranks. On the second PP stage this fails immediately with `ValueError: Global rank 0 is not part of group`.

The draft checkpoint is much smaller than the target checkpoint, so this PR preserves the fast target load while selecting the existing, collective-free loader for only the draft. The `LoadConfig` is copied, leaving the target configuration unchanged.

## Test plan

### Duplicate-work check

I checked open PRs before implementation. #50514 implements EAGLE3-style speculative decoding with PP, and #53901 extends that work on ROCm; neither fixes the `fastsafetensors` partial-WORLD load tracked by #50959. I did not find another open PR for #50959.

### Unit tests

```bash
uv venv --system-site-packages /tmp/testenv
uv pip install --python /tmp/testenv/bin/python pytest
/tmp/testenv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_draft_load_config.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py
```

Result: **39 passed**. Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, and repository pre-commit checks also passed.

### Kimi-K3 DSpark end-to-end

Validated on current `main` (`2c7d7dd64a`) plus the latest #50514 head (`b3b01d5b37`) using 2 nodes × 8 B200 GPUs:

```bash
vllm serve /models/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/models/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
```

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Target load | `fastsafetensors`, 221.77 s |
| Draft load | automatic standard-safetensors fallback, 6.13 s |
| Startup | DSpark CUDA graph capture completed; `/health` returned 200 |
| Generation | one semantic sanity request succeeded; 8/8 concurrent requests returned HTTP 200 |
| Spec decode | 1,055 proposed draft tokens, 623 accepted (59.1%) across 211 draft steps |
| Runtime errors | no `ERROR`, traceback, engine restart, or CUDA fault on either node |

I did not rerun a full model-quality evaluation because this change only selects the loader for draft initialization and does not alter loaded tensors or inference. The generated-output sanity check and nonzero speculative acceptance verify that the draft weights are usable.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, code editing, testing, and drafting this description. I reviewed the changes and the reported results.

title: [Bugfix] Don't let a structured-output request sample from an unmasked row
author: ArcheyChen
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn. ## Purpose Part of #54437. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` constrains a row only while `apply_bitmask` holds, and a `-1` placeholder in the scheduled draft window sets `seen_padding`, so every row after it is filled with `_full_mask` — every token in the vocabulary allowed: ```python # vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): apply_bitmask = not failed and not seen_padding and i >= constraint_start self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) if token == -1: seen_padding = True ``` That is sound when the `-1` means "`validate_tokens` rejected this draft": the first `-1` then sits at exactly the draft the grammar rejected, that draft's own row is still masked, so it is rejected and acceptance never reaches the permissive rows. It is not sound when the `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler", which happens because the draft hand-off carries no identity — `DraftTokensHandler` keeps one slot that every `execute_model` overwrites (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`), and it also clears the payload entirely for a batch with no structured-output requests. The worker meanwhile verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens`, so acceptance can walk straight into rows that constrain nothing and the request emits tokens the grammar never allowed. #54437 has the full chain, a model-free reproduction on `main`, and field measurements. This PR is the fail-closed half: it makes the permissive rows unreachable regardless of why the drafts went missing. The identity fix for the hand-off is a separate change. **Not a duplicate of #56802.** That PR implements the other half of #54437 — identity for the hand-off, so the drafts are not lost in the first place. It is complementary: its lookup miss path falls back to exactly the invalidation this PR adds, so on a miss without this PR the bitmask still fails open. ## Change Carry, per structured-output request, how many leading drafts the bitmask actually constrained, and invalidate the drafts from that index on, so `is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0` pins the accepted length before sampling can reach a permissive row. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: `get_grammar_bitmask` fills `num_acceptable_drafts` with `len(strip_speculative_padding(window))`, reusing the helper #48200 introduced. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: `GrammarOutput.num_acceptable_drafts`, a defaulted field, so existing constructors keep working. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/structured_outputs.py`: `grammar_invalid_drafts` turns that into a mask over logit rows, built on device: a draft is invalid when its local position exceeds its request's `num_acceptable_drafts`. The local position is `expanded_local_pos`, which `expand_idx_mapping` derives from the device `cu_num_logits` — the same (request, position) keying `apply_grammar_bitmask` uses, so it stays correct when adaptive verification trims drafts on device and `cu_num_logits_np` is only an upper bound. When every request's scheduled drafts are within its limit (fully back-filled, the normal case) it returns `None` on the CPU and launches nothing. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: `sample()` calls it after applying the bitmask and hands the mask to the rejection sampler. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`: verification runs against `draft_sampled.masked_fill(mask, -1)`. `apply_sampling_params` and the watermarking context still receive the real draft ids, so penalties and bad-words are unaffected. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`: shard the new per-request list the same way as the bitmask. No kernel change: `rejection_sampler_utils` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution rather than from the residual. That matters — `max(p - q, 0)` is the residual of a *genuine* rejection, and forcing one where `p ≈ q` collapses it across the vocabulary. When the drafts are fully back-filled nothing is invalidated and behaviour is unchanged. Absent the field — an older scheduler, or warmup — the whole window is invalidated, which is the conservative choice. Production diff is 85 added / 3 removed lines across those six files. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit coverage for the new helper, plus the suites this PR's call paths touch. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q ``` `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py` — 5 cases covering `grammar_invalid_drafts`: whole window, partial window, nothing to do, per-request offset, and **adaptive verification with an uneven reallocation** (the device layout differs from `cu_num_logits_np`). **End-to-end reproduction.** Not committed, per review. Save the file below as `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py` and run it on `main` and on this branch: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py -q ``` It drives the real `GPUModelRunner.sample()` → `apply_grammar_bitmask` → `RejectionSampler` path with a bitmask whose leading rows carry a real mask and whose later rows are `_full_mask`, and with the drafts the worker holds on the GPU disagreeing with the scheduler's padded copy, which is what a lost hand-off produces. Temperature 0, one request, four logit rows, so it is deterministic.
tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project """Acceptance must stop at the last bitmask row that carries a real mask. `grammar_bitmask` stops constraining rows once it meets a -1 placeholder in the scheduled draft window, and the worker verifies the drafts it holds on the GPU rather than the scheduler's padded copy. When the two disagree -- the hand-off lost a step's drafts, see #54437 -- acceptance can walk into a row where every token is allowed. The grammar here admits only LEGAL. The scheduled window is back-filled one draft deep, so rows 0 and 1 carry a real mask and rows 2.. are `_full_mask`, while the drafts on the GPU would carry acceptance into row 2 and emit ILLEGAL. """ from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import pytest import torch from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import GrammarOutput from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import NO_LOGPROBS from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.rejection_sampler import RejectionSampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.structured_outputs import StructuredOutputsWorker VOCAB = 128 K = 3 # drafts per step NUM_LOGITS = K + 1 # + the bonus row LEGAL = 7 ILLEGAL = 99 # Index of the first -1 in the scheduled window: rows 0..1 are masked. NUM_ACCEPTABLE = 1 def _bitmask() -> np.ndarray: """Rows 0..NUM_ACCEPTABLE constrained to LEGAL, the rest fully permissive.""" mask = np.zeros((NUM_LOGITS, cdiv(VOCAB, 32)), dtype=np.int32) for row in range(NUM_LOGITS): if row <= NUM_ACCEPTABLE: mask[row, LEGAL // 32] = 1 << (LEGAL % 32) else: mask[row, :] = -1 # every token allowed return mask def _input_batch(device: torch.device) -> SimpleNamespace: cu_np = np.array([0, NUM_LOGITS], dtype=np.int32) # draft_sampled = input_ids[logits_indices]; entry i + 1 is draft i, so the # drafts the GPU holds are [LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL]. input_ids = torch.tensor( [LEGAL, LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL], dtype=torch.int32, device=device ) return SimpleNamespace( num_reqs=1, req_ids=["g"], num_draft_tokens=K, num_draft_tokens_per_req=np.array([K], dtype=np.int32), input_ids=input_ids, logits_indices=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), positions=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int64, device=device), cu_num_logits_np=cu_np, cu_num_logits=torch.from_numpy(cu_np).to(device), idx_mapping_np=np.array([0], dtype=np.int32), idx_mapping=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_idx_mapping=torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_local_pos=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32), ) def _logits(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor: """Every row prefers its own draft, so nothing but the mask can reject one.""" logits = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, VOCAB, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) logits[0, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[1, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[2, ILLEGAL] = 10.0 # row 2 is permissive, so this wins there logits[3, LEGAL] = 10.0 return logits def _rejection_sampler(device: torch.device) -> RejectionSampler: sampler = object.__new__(RejectionSampler) sampler.num_speculative_steps = K sampler.enable_adaptive_verification = False sampler.use_block_verification = False sampler.synthetic_conditional_rates = None sampler.watermark_key = None zeros_f = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) # greedy sampler.sampler = SimpleNamespace( compute_nans=False, logprobs_mode="raw_logprobs", use_fp64_gumbel=False, apply_sampling_params=lambda logits, *args, **kwargs: logits, sampling_states=SimpleNamespace( temperature=SimpleNamespace(gpu=zeros_f), seeds=SimpleNamespace(gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)), max_num_logprobs=lambda _: NO_LOGPROBS, ), req_states=SimpleNamespace( prefill_len=SimpleNamespace( gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) ) ), ) return sampler @pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA") def test_acceptance_stops_at_the_last_masked_row(): device = torch.device("cuda") input_batch = _input_batch(device) logits = _logits(device) runner = object.__new__(GPUModelRunner) runner.device = device runner.vocab_size = VOCAB runner.batch_sharder = None runner.sampler = None runner.model = SimpleNamespace(compute_logits=lambda hidden: logits) runner.rejection_sampler = _rejection_sampler(device) runner.speculator = SimpleNamespace(draft_logits=None) runner.structured_outputs_worker = StructuredOutputsWorker( max_num_logits=NUM_LOGITS, vocab_size=VOCAB, device=device, mask_stride=NUM_LOGITS, num_bonus_tokens=1, ) grammar_output = GrammarOutput(["g"], _bitmask()) # The scheduler reports how many leading drafts the bitmask constrained. # Absent on an older scheduler, where the whole window is invalidated. grammar_output.num_acceptable_drafts = [NUM_ACCEPTABLE] hidden = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, 8, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) sampler_output, num_sampled, _ = runner.sample(hidden, input_batch, grammar_output) accepted = int(num_sampled[0].item()) emitted = sampler_output.sampled_token_ids[0, :accepted].tolist() assert ILLEGAL not in emitted, ( f"emitted {emitted}: a draft verified against a permissive row was " f"accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint" ) # Draft 0 may be accepted; draft 1 must not be, because accepting it moves # sampling into row 2, which constrains nothing. assert accepted == NUM_ACCEPTABLE + 1 assert emitted == [LEGAL] * accepted ```
## Test Result End-to-end reproduction on `main` @ `2798f668`: ``` E AssertionError: emitted [7, 7, 99, 7]: a draft verified against a permissive row was accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint E assert 99 not in [7, 7, 99, 7] 1 failed, 14 warnings in 1.00s ``` Token 7 is the only token the grammar admits; token 99 is one it never admits. On this branch, same base: ``` 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.26s ``` and the Test Plan selection is `71 passed, 1 xfailed`. ### Model evaluation One RTX 4090, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, Qwen3-8B + `Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` (K=4), `--async-scheduling`, xgrammar. `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 200`: | | exact_match, strict-match | exact_match, flexible-extract | |---|---|---| | `main` @ `0bfc7a15` | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | | this PR @ `ec112592`, same base | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | gsm8k carries no structured-output requests, so that is the "speculative decoding is untouched" half. For the structured-output half, a mixed grammar + plain load with every grammar response validated against its JSON schema (4 concurrency mixes, 49 grammar requests) gives 0 schema violations, 0 `grammar rejected tokens` and 0 `Failed to advance FSM` on both `main` and this PR — which is the expected result at `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, where the hand-off does not get clobbered. Both were measured at `ec112592`. The review round since changed only how the invalid drafts are located, and that code runs only for a batch that holds a structured-output request whose drafts were not fully back-filled — which neither gsm8k (no grammar requests) nor the `pp=1` load (always fully back-filled) produces. I have not re-run them for that reason; happy to if you want the numbers on the current head. Beyond that: both this change and the identity fix have been running in production on a 2-node x 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding, K=7, xgrammar). Before them, `tool_choice=required` and `json_schema` failed 100% of the time whenever a second structured-output request was resident; after, 72/72 concurrent grammar requests complete with zero `grammar rejected` lines and zero engine errors. Independently, @xinli-sw [reports](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442#issuecomment-5822629259) that this PR fixes a `pipeline_parallel_size=2` x `tensor_parallel_size=8` deployment with DSpark (K=3) on 16x B200. ## AI assistance This PR contains AI-generated code. The root-cause analysis, the instrumentation behind the numbers in #54437, and the patch were produced with Claude, with the consumption-time-snapshot idea and the fail-closed requirement contributed by GPT-5.6. The adaptive-verification issue in review was caught by an AI reviewer and fixed with Claude. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the evaluation above, and validated the behaviour end-to-end on the deployment described. Commits carry: ``` Co-authored-by: GPT-5.6 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) ```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Restore the chat template content format mismatch warning
author: pra2107tham
body:
## Purpose

`resolve_chat_template_content_format` returns an explicitly specified
`--chat-template-content-format` without ever comparing it against the format
detected from the template. The warning that was written to catch exactly that
mismatch has been unreachable since #19735.

## Root cause

#19735 added an early return so that a specified format skips the Jinja AST
parse:

```diff
+    if given_format != "auto":
+        return given_format
...
-    return detected_format if given_format == "auto" else given_format
+    return detected_format
```

Detection also fed `_log_chat_template_content_format`, which has exactly one
caller — below that early return. So the forced path exits before the logger,
and the logger is only ever reached when `given_format == "auto"`. The guard

```python
if given_format != "auto" and given_format != detected_format:
```

is false on every reachable path. `git log -S` puts this at #19735 (June 2025).

## Impact

Forcing a format the template cannot consume fails in one of two ways. Running
vLLM's own detection helpers over the 35 templates in `examples/` (33 usable):

| forced format | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | correct on every template |
| `string` | correct on every template |
| `openai` | 17 raise `TypeError`, 8 silently corrupt, 8 fine |

The 17 concatenate with `+` and raise `can only concatenate str (not "list") to
str`, surfacing as HTTP 500. The other 8 interpolate with `{{ message.content }}`,
so Jinja calls `str()` on the list and renders the Python repr into the prompt:

```
### Instruction:
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Reply with exactly OK.'}]
```

HTTP 200, no exception, nothing in the logs. For those 8 templates
(`alpaca`, `inkbot`, `teleflm`, `llama3.2_pythonic`, `phi4_mini`, `toolace`,
`xlam_llama`, `xlam_qwen`) this warning is the only signal in the system.

## Changes

- Restore detection before the return and select with a ternary, as the code did
  prior to #19735. The override still wins; only the comparison is added back.
- Gate the info line on `auto`, so users who already passed the flag are not told
  they can pass it to override.
- Cache the resolved content format, so restoring detection does not add
  per-request work (see below).
- Inline the logging and use `info_once` / `warning_once`, removing
  `_log_chat_template_content_format`.

## Test

Verified against `examples/template_chatml.jinja` (detected `string`) and
`tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja` (detected `openai`):

| template | given | returned | logged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chatml | `openai` | `openai` | warning |
| chatml | `string` | `string` | — |
| llama3.1 | `openai` | `openai` | — |
| chatml | `auto` | `string` | info |

The override is honoured in every case and only the genuine mismatch warns.

`pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py` gives 28 passed with the existing
content-format tests unaffected. The 3 failures (`ultravox`,
`Llama-Guard-3-1B`, `paligemma-3b-mix-224`) are `403 Cannot access gated repo`
and reproduce identically on a clean tree. Built and run from source on Apple
Silicon (CPU backend, Python 3.12); `pre-commit run` passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- **This does not close #54486.** That issue asks for the combination to be
  rejected before request handling; this only restores the diagnostic. Filing it
  as the symptom that surfaced the regression.
- **Performance.** Detection now runs even when a format is given, so per
  review it is cached. `lru_cache` was not usable — `tools` is a list and
  `ModelConfig` sets `__eq__` without `__hash__` — so this follows the existing
  `_PROCESSOR_CHAT_TEMPLATES` idiom and keys a bounded dict on the fields that
  select the template. Only the presence of `tools` is in the key: it decides
  whether the processor template is tried, and its contents never reach the AST.
  The bound matters because a request can carry its own `chat_template`.

  Measured on Qwen2-VL-2B, explicit chat template: **~16 us -> 0.109 us** per
  call once warm. With `chat_template=None` it was already ~0.2 us, since
  `_try_get_processor_chat_template` and `_detect_content_format` are memoized;
  the cost sat in `tokenizer.get_chat_template()` on the explicit path. Detected
  format is unchanged against an uncached resolve for all 35 templates in
  `examples/`.

- **Eight advisory warnings.** Forcing `string` on a template that also supports
  `openai` renders correctly but still warns, since the formats differ. That
  seems right — you have silently given up multimodal capability — and the
  warning's own text is advisory. Happy to narrow it to the
  `detected == "string"` direction if preferred.
- **Overlap with #53824.** That PR touches the same two files but a different
  function (`_iter_nodes_assign_content_item`, improving detection accuracy).
  Complementary rather than duplicate — it makes detection more correct, this
  makes a wrong override visible — but there may be a textual conflict in the
  test file depending on merge order.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed
line, and the test results above were run locally. The commit carries a
`Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

title: [Bugfix][Security] Bound embedding densification before to_dense()
author: LeizhenZhang
body:
## Purpose

Client-supplied embedding payloads are deserialized and then immediately densified:

```python
with check_sparse_tensor_invariants_threadsafe():
    tensor = torch.load(buffer, weights_only=True)
    return tensor.to_dense()          # <-- unbounded
```

`weights_only=True` blocks arbitrary code execution, and
`check_sparse_tensor_invariants()` rejects indices that fall outside the declared
shape. Neither bounds the *declared shape itself*.

A sparse COO tensor holding **one** in-bounds non-zero element with a declared
shape of `(2**20, 2**20)` is a completely valid tensor. It passes the invariant
checks, serializes to about 1.5 KB, and `to_dense()` then asks the allocator for
4 TiB.

To be precise about what I measured: at that size the allocator simply refuses
(`RuntimeError: DefaultCPUAllocator: can't allocate memory: you tried to
allocate 4398046511104 bytes`, peak RSS unmoved). The damaging regime is the
shapes that *fit*, because the dense allocation is bounded by the declared shape
rather than by the request, and the attacker picks the shape. Those are fully
resident, and several concurrent requests sized near the host is what turns that
into an outage. I have not reproduced a kill on a shared machine and am not
claiming one.

Measured amplification on a plain checkout (`torch.save` of a
`(20000, 20000)` sparse tensor with 1 stored element):

```
serialized payload size = 1560 bytes
RSS before to_dense()   = 337 MB
RSS after  to_dense()   = 1866 MB      # +1.49 GiB from a 1.5 KB payload
```

The existing `ndim` validation in `ImageEmbeddingItems` / `AudioEmbeddingItems`
cannot help here, because it runs *after* `to_dense()` — the memory is already
allocated by the time the shape is looked at. The same is true of the
`hidden_size` / `dim()` checks in `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, which are all
sequenced after the `to_dense()` call.

Reachable from:

| Entry point | Requires | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` content part `{"type": "image_embeds", ...}` | `--enable-mm-embeds` | `parse_image_embeds` → `MediaConnector.fetch_image_embedding` → `ImageEmbeddingMediaIO.load_base64` |
| same, `audio_embeds` / `video_embeds` | `--enable-mm-embeds` | `AudioEmbeddingMediaIO` / `VideoEmbeddingMediaIO` |
| `/v1/completions` with `prompt_embeds` | `--enable-prompt-embeds` | `safe_load_prompt_embeds` |

Both entry points are behind an opt-in server flag, so this is not reachable on a
default server — but on a server that does enable them, any client that can send a
request can trigger it. The dict form of `image_embeds` fans out
(`{k: fetch_image_embedding(v) for ...}`), so one request can carry several such
payloads.

### The fix

Add `safe_to_dense(tensor, *, parameter=...)` in `vllm/utils/sparse_utils.py` and
route all seven `to_dense()` call sites through it. It rejects a payload whose
dense footprint (`numel() * element_size()`) exceeds
`VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` **before** `to_dense()` allocates anything, raising
`VLLMValidationError` so the caller gets a 4xx rather than a dead server.

It also checks that the payload actually deserialized to a `torch.Tensor`.
`safe_load_prompt_embeds` already did this; the three media IO classes did not, so
a non-tensor payload surfaced as an `AttributeError` (500) instead of a 4xx.

On the default: `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` defaults to 2 GiB, which is a guard
rail rather than a tight bound. 2 GiB is what a legitimate 128K-token float32
`prompt_embeds` at `hidden_size=4096` costs, so anything lower would start
rejecting real requests. The point is to turn "unbounded" into "bounded and
configurable"; deployments facing untrusted clients will want to lower it.
Setting it to `0` disables the check, consistent with the other limits in the
same table in `docs/usage/security.md`.

I checked open and closed PRs/issues for overlap (`to_dense`, `prompt_embeds
sparse`, `image_embeds limit`, `sparse_utils`, `safe_load_prompt_embeds`,
decompression-bomb wording) and did not find an existing fix or report for this.
Happy to change the env var name, the default, or fold the check into the
`MediaIO.get_max_bytes()` mechanism instead if that fits better.

## Test Plan

New file `tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py`:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py -v
```

It covers `safe_to_dense` directly and each of the three
`*EmbeddingMediaIO` classes (the objects reached from `/v1/chat/completions`),
via both `load_base64` and `load_file`:

- an oversized-but-valid sparse tensor is rejected, and the error names the
  offending parameter and the env var
- the attack payload really is small (asserted `< 4096` base64 chars), so this is
  amplification and not just a large upload
- dense tensors and small sparse tensors still load unchanged
- a non-tensor payload is rejected as a validation error
- the limit is configurable, exact at the boundary, and disabled by `0`

Existing coverage that must keep passing:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/test_sparse_tensor_validation_unit.py \
       tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py \
       tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
       tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py -v
```

## Test Result

New tests, all passing:

```
$ pytest tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py -q
16 passed, 16 warnings in 6.19s
```

Existing coverage, unchanged:

```
$ pytest tests/multimodal/test_sparse_tensor_validation_unit.py \
         tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py \
         tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py -q
2 failed, 74 passed, 16 warnings in 117.31s
```

The two failures are `test_empty_prompt` and `test_out_of_vocab_token_ids`, which
launch a `RemoteOpenAIServer` subprocess. They fail with
`FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'vllm'` in my local
setup, before any request is sent — not related to this change. Notably
`test_load_prompt_embeds`, which round-trips `strided` / `sparse_coo` /
`sparse_csc` / `sparse_csr` layouts through `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, passes for
every parametrization.

Before/after on the same payload, using a `(30000, 30000)` shape (3.35 GiB dense)
rather than the 4 TiB shape from the tests, so the "before" branch actually
completes instead of just failing the allocation:

```
declared shape        : (30000, 30000)
payload (base64)      : 2612 chars
dense size implied    : 3.35 GiB
peak RSS at start     : 835 MiB
invariant checks      : PASSED (indices are in bounds)
BEFORE -> to_dense()  : allocated (30000, 30000), peak RSS now 4270 MiB
AFTER  -> rejected    : `image_embeds` declares shape (30000, 30000), which would
                        allocate 3600000000 bytes (3433 MiB) once densified,
                        exceeding the 2147483648 byte limit. Set
                        VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES to increase this limit.
peak RSS at end       : 4270 MiB
```

A 2612-character request field costs 3.4 GiB of resident memory before this
change, and is refused with a 4xx after it.

`pre-commit`-relevant checks on the touched files:

```
$ ruff check <touched files>     # All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <touched files>   # 8 files already formatted
```

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Don't evict a remote engine a transfer is still reading from
author: jyizheng
body:
## Purpose

`_evict_stale_engines` documents the invariant it relies on:

> Engines with active transfers or pending handshakes cannot be stale:
> - Active transfers touch `_engine_last_active` in `start_load_kv`.

They touch it once. `pull_worker._read_blocks_for_req` stamps it when a read is issued and never again while that read runs, so a transfer that outlives `engine_ttl` — 3600 s by default, and a peer that has lost its NIC holds one indefinitely — leaves its engine looking idle.

Eviction then calls `release_dlist_handle` and `remove_remote_agent` on the state that transfer is reading through. Nothing consults `_recving_transfers`, and the release happens inside NIXL rather than in Python, so the symptom is a worker process that dies without a traceback:

```
Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor
```

Observed on a 10-prefill/3-decode disaggregated deployment. All three decode workers died within seconds of each other, six seconds after a new-remote handshake — which is where eviction runs — having spent the previous three hours idle, so a batch of TTL-expired engines had accumulated.

This holds back engines with a transfer still in flight. They become evictable again as soon as it finishes or fails, so the memory bound the TTL exists to enforce is unchanged for any engine that is genuinely idle.

## Test Plan

`test_engine_with_inflight_transfer_is_not_evicted` ages an engine past its TTL while a request is still reading from it, asserts nothing is released, then removes the transfer and asserts the engine evicts normally.

## Test Result

Against the unpatched worker the engine is evicted and both `release_dlist_handle` and `remove_remote_agent` are called with a transfer outstanding; patched, neither is.

title: [ROCm][RDNA3] Fix W4A16 split-K accuracy and determinism
author: AIwork4me
body:
## Problem

The RDNA3 (gfx11) W4A16 GPTQ kernels accumulate split-K partials in
bf16/fp16 via CAS atomics. The narrowing happens **before** accumulation,
and low-precision addition is not associative — so whichever split block
wins the CAS first changes the result. That numerical error is present on
**every affected forward pass**, in every decoding configuration.

Greedy decoding is merely where it becomes visible: at temperature 0 the
rounded logit wobble can flip `argmax` between repeated identical
generations (the trail in #50603). Under sampling (e.g. T=0.6) the same
error hides under the sampler's own noise while still sitting under every
reported metric.

## Root cause

```
FP32 per-block partial
  -> bf16/fp16 narrowing (8 / 11 mantissa bits)
  -> CAS-atomic accumulation in execution-dependent order
```

gfx11 has no packed bf16/fp16 atomic, so the epilogue emulated one with a
CAS retry loop — which also made the accumulation order scheduler- and
contention-dependent.

## Fix

Keep the compute kernels and dispatch unchanged; replace only the epilogue
on both paths:

```
FP32 per-split partials
  -> fixed ascending-z FP32 reduction
  -> one final bf16/fp16 cast
```

* Every path writes each output element exactly once; `k_split == 1`
  (WMMA) and `z_count == 1` (scalar) keep/store directly — no scratch, no
  reduce, no atomics.
* The FP32 partials scratch is `at::empty`: coverage is total by
  construction (every reducer-visible `(z, m, n)` slot has exactly one
  writer in all seven WMMA variants and the scalar kernel; the invariant
  is documented at `alloc_wmma_partials`), so there is no zero-fill pass.
* Scratch is per-call via the caching allocator, row-tiled so the bound is
  independent of the caller's M.

## Accuracy (W7900/gfx1100, FP32 dequantized reference)

Max abs error, synthetic uint4b8/group-128 weights, K=4096:

| path | dtype | legacy CAS | this PR | factor |
|------|-------|-----------:|--------:|-------:|
| scalar | bf16 | 0.24–0.37 | 0.0625 | 4–6x |
| WMMA | bf16 | 0.15–0.23 | 0.09–0.11 | ~2x |
| WMMA | fp16 | 0.024–0.038 | 0.011–0.018 | ~2x |
| scalar | fp16 | ~0.95 | 0.002-0.015 | **94-201x** (see 2026-10-01 update: exact factored dequant) |

bf16 is the headline; fp16 carried 11 mantissa bits so the removed CAS
rounding cost it ~8x less (as expected). The scalar-fp16 row was the
classic exllama bit-trick rounding the per-group offset constant to fp16
— fixed by the exact factored dequant in the 2026-10-01 update below
(now 0.002-0.015 on the same shapes).

The earlier "0.028 → 0.0061" measurement is the same bf16 improvement
factor on real Muse weights. bf16 residual error now sits at the final
output cast (1 ulp); WMMA at the B-tile narrowing.

## Determinism

Fixed inputs now produce bit-identical outputs on every call: 20/20
benchmark shapes repeatable; real Muse q_proj at M=1 gives 1 distinct
result / 100 calls (previously up to 200/200 distinct). Repeatability
alone is not correctness, so the tests also check values against the FP32
reference — a stale `at::empty` scratch slot would be bitwise-repeatable
and wrong, and is caught by the tolerance analysis in the test module.

## Performance (W7900/gfx1100, median of 100 CUDA-event timings)

Rows are **bf16**; fp16 differs in dispatch (bf16 reaches WMMA at
M ≥ 16, fp16 not until M ≥ 64 — at M=16 fp16 is still on the scalar path):

| M | N | K | path | k_split | scratch MB | before µs | after µs | Δ |
|--:|---:|---:|------|--------:|-----------:|----------:|---------:|---:|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 0.25 | 44.5 | 39.7 | -10.8% |
| 8 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 2.0 | 61.8 | 57.2 | -7.5% |
| 16 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 16x16_1w | 4 | 1.0 | 58.8 | 53.7 | **-8.7%** |
| 64 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 64x64_4w | 4 | 4.0 | 120.5 | 112.0 | **-7.0%** |
| 128 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 8.0 | 123.5 | 114.7 | **-7.2%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 378.4 | 350.8 | **-7.3%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 554.7 | 527.4 | -4.9% |
| 512 | 25600 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | **1** | **0** | 3070.7 | 2894.2 | -5.8% |

(Historical W7900 campaign numbers; superseded WMMA-dispatch note: fp16
now reaches WMMA from M>=12, see the 2026-10-01 update.)
Full tables for both dtypes incl. N/K/k_split/scratch
per row: `05-benchmark.md` in the evidence package:
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
(immutable: same tree at commit
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/9bc79045c157dd12a2728cad4e52fd9b21b0ccc3/validation-54706-jartx-w7900)

Notes:
- "before" = this branch's original HEAD (zero-filled WMMA scratch);
  "after" = with the dead zero-fill removed (`at::zeros` → `at::empty`
  once total coverage was proven). Same-M/different-N matters: at M=512,
  N=4096 → k_split=4 (32 MB scratch) while N=25600 → k_split=1 (none).
- Versus a locally restored legacy-CAS control build, the deterministic
  epilogue is now at parity or **faster** for prefill shapes (bf16 M=16:
  53.7 vs 55.3 µs); only M=1 decode pays a residual ~4–10% (scratch
  round-trip at tiny output) — the price of bit-reproducibility.
- Numerics are bit-identical before/after the memset removal on all 20
  shapes (zero-init was dead traffic).
- A follow-up fix (CodeRabbit finding) gave the V7/V8 k_split==1 path
  the same direct-store branch the 64x64 path had: no scratch, no
  reduce, partials == nullptr. N=25600 row: bf16 3020.1 -> 2894.2 µs
  (-4.2%), fp16 2858.3 -> 2668.6 µs (-6.6%); split-K shapes unchanged
  within noise; numerics bit-identical.

## Why not FP32 atomics?

gfx11 does have `global_atomic_add_f32`; an FP32 scratch accumulated with
native atomics plus one cast pass would remove nearly all the rounding
error with no reduce kernel. We still chose the fixed-order reduce:
FP32 addition is also non-associative, so atomic accumulation remains
order-dependent — vastly better numerically, but not bit-reproducible.
Since bit-exact reproducibility is an explicit goal of this PR, the
fixed ascending-z reduction is the design that guarantees it.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_determinism.py` — 24 tests:

* bit-repeatability through the public op (scalar/WMMA × bf16/fp16),
  with the scalar regression at K=4096 (16 concurrent writers — well
  inside the old failure regime, whose onset was 2–4 writers);
* FP32-reference correctness for scalar and WMMA, split-K and
  direct-store (k_split == 1 / z_count == 1) paths, both dtypes, with
  tolerances derived from each path's rounding structure;
* explicit V7/V8 (128x64) no-split coverage at M=512, N=25600, K=6656
  (repeatability + FP32 reference, both dtypes; routing asserted via a
  replica of the k_split heuristic);
* test hygiene: repo-standard `dist_init` fixture (no `__enter__` leak,
  no hardcoded MASTER_PORT).

On a locally restored legacy-CAS build, 8 tests fail (7 repeatability +
the scalar-bf16 reference check at max_abs 0.30 vs 0.10 tolerance,
measured on the then-20-test suite); on this PR, 24/24 pass.

## Validation

- W7900D / gfx1100, ROCm 7.14 runtime, torch 2.14; upstream base
  `40b2f62061575905aaac8bc360eaea62a4baeb67`
- targeted tests 24/24 PASS (bf16 + fp16, scalar + WMMA, incl. V7/V8
  no-split)
- FP32-reference correctness + A/B legacy control: see above
- benchmark matrix: dtype × M{1,8,16,64,128,512} × N{4096,25600} ×
  K{4096,6656} with path/k_split/scratch per row (full evidence package
  below)
- independent RX 7900 XT evidence from @cadamcat (A/B table in #50603)
- full W7900/gfx1100 reproducibility package (environment, correctness
  and A/B-control evidence, complete benchmark tables):
  https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
- Muse eager ctx512: 1 unique / 8 greedy generations; 0
  same-input/different-output events across 16,640 intercepted W4A16
  GEMM calls

## Scope

gfx11 / RDNA3 W4A16 only; no attention-routing changes. The residual
Muse eager/8192 divergence after this fix was traced to ROCm paged
attention V-cache tail consumption and is fixed by #53856. Investigation
trail: #50603; full earlier evidence in the
`validation-50603/rdna3-w4a16-upstream-cleanup` tree linked there.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for code iteration, validation orchestration, and
drafting. I reviewed the final diff, kernel behavior, test results,
performance data, and evidence and can explain the change end to end.




---

## Rebase validation (2026-09-09, post-#54809)

Rebased onto upstream/main `385dce36` after #54809 (GPTQ act-order/g_idx
removal) and revalidated on gfx1100 (W7900D, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.14,
ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain — same environment as the original campaign):

- conflicts resolved semantically; the post-#54809 no-g_idx op contract
  (`gptq_gemm_rdna3(a, b_q_weight, b_qzeros, b_scales, use_v2_format)`)
  kept native — no `b_g_idx`/`b_q_perm`/`has_g_idx`/`w_gidx_param_name`
  anywhere in the PR
- gfx1100 build PASS; gfx942 (non-RDNA3 stub pass) compile guard PASS
- targeted determinism/FP32-reference suite: **24/24 PASS**
- upstream RDNA3 tests (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `test_rdna3_compile_guards`,
  `test_rdna3_w4a16_selection`, `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16`): 148 passed,
  5 skipped (non-gfx1100 guards), 0 failed
- V7/V8 `k_split == 1` direct-store confirmed (no scratch, no reducer,
  profiler-verified); split-K control: deterministic FP32 reducer active,
  scratch 33.6 MB as designed; scalar z_count=1/z_count=16 paths verified
- performance within noise of the pre-rebase reference:
  no-split M=512 N=25600 K=6656 — bf16 2877 µs / fp16 2633 µs (was
  2894 / 2669); split-K M=512 N=4096 K=6656 — bf16 545 µs / fp16 507 µs
  (was ~528 / ~501); scratch 0 / 33.6 MB unchanged
- DCO green on all replayed commits; historical W7900 measurements above
  remain the pre-rebase evidence package (unchanged)

Note: the two commits added on top of the original six adapt the tests to
the post-#54809 API and apply the repo's current formatter pins
(ruff 0.14.0 / clang-format 21.1.2); no semantic changes.


## Update (2026-10-01): exact fp16 dequant, M>=12 WMMA dispatch, fused fp16 split-K reduce

Addressed @JartX's two review items (semantically ported from
dafcde3f8bb9 and 5e8db861e02 — neither cherry-picks cleanly) and rebased
onto current upstream/main `ccda9098`.

### 1. fp16 dequant is now exact (the "~0.95" row is gone)

The old bit-trick bakes `z = scale * (-1024 - zero)` into an **fp16**
constant; that representation rounding (~0.008 abs at scale≈0.02, repeated
for every weight of a group×column) was the error — not the epilogue. The
dequant now uses the exact factored form

```
sum_k a_k * w_k  =  y * sum_k a_k * (1024 + q_k)  +  z * sum_k a_k
```

with **fp32** (y, z) pairs per nibble slot and the z·sum_a correction
applied once per 32-K round (same structure the bf16 path already had).
Ported to the dense scalar kernel **and** the MoE kernel (its baked error
was previously masked by the dense reference being equally biased).

Accuracy vs the FP32 dequantized reference on gfx1100 (public op path,
100-repeat calls, K=4096–6656, M=1/4/8):

| path | dtype | before | after | factor |
|------|-------|-------:|------:|-------:|
| scalar | fp16 | 1.03–1.37 | 0.002–0.015 | **94–201x** |
| scalar | bf16 | 0.06–0.12 | 0.06–0.12 | bit-identical (unchanged) |

### 2. WMMA dispatch: both dtypes from M ≥ 12

Measured scalar/WMMA crossover on this gfx1100 (both ops timed directly,
identical inputs, median of 300; full table in the dispatch comment): at
M ≥ 12 WMMA wins or ties on every measured shape for both dtypes
(1.00–1.69x); below that scalar wins and is the more accurate path. fp16
previously stayed scalar until M=64 — that speed came with ~100x more
dequant error; with the exact dequant the crossover moved to 12, same as
bf16. An M=11 (scalar) / M=12 (WMMA) boundary test pins it via profiler
kernel names.

### 3. Split-K reduction fused into the fp16 kernel — with per-call state

The fp16 scalar path now reduces in the GEMM kernel: each block publishes
arrival on its tile's ticket; the last z block sums the z-slices in fixed
ascending order (batched loads) and rounds once — still bit-reproducible,
one launch fewer, partials read while L2-hot.

**The ticket array is per-call** (`at::zeros`, one int per tile,
re-armed in-kernel), **not** the device-global `g_w4_tickets` of the
reference: nothing in vLLM serializes quantized W4A16 GEMMs on one device
(DeepSeek V4/V4.1 aux-stream forks, LoRA dual-stream, and the
SharedExperts side stream all overlap quantized linears today), so
cross-launch global state would be a correctness hazard. Per-call tickets
from the stream-aware caching allocator keep concurrent invocations
independent by construction; verified by a two-stream concurrent-vs-serial
(bit-exact) test and CUDA-graph capture/replay tests.

The **bf16** path keeps the separate reducer: measured on gfx1100, fusing
it was neutral at M=1 and up to ~10% slower at M=4–8 (the fused reduce
serializes a multi-row tile's reduction into one block per tile), so bf16
behavior is unchanged.

Performance, interleaved A/B/C in one session (original baked / exact +
separate reduce / final; min of 4-rep medians × 3 rounds; public op):

| dtype | M | vs original | vs separate-reduce |
|-------|--:|------------:|-------------------:|
| fp16 | 1 | **−6.3 … −11.3%** | −8.1 … −8.8% |
| fp16 | 4 | −6.7 … −8.2% | −11 … −12% |
| fp16 | 8 | −2.2 … −7.6% | −6 … −16% |
| bf16 | 1–8 | −1.4 … +0.1% (noise) | — (unchanged path) |

i.e. the final fp16 kernel is both ~100–200x more accurate **and**
6–11% faster at decode than the pre-review state.

### Validation (gfx1100 / ROCm 7.2.1 toolchain, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.14, base `ccda9098`)

- targeted determinism/reference suite: **54/54 PASS** (fp16+bf16, scalar+
  WMMA, split-K z∈{2,16,17,26} incl. K%256≠0 clipped tails, no-split,
  G∈{32,64,128}, M_COUNT∈{1,2,4,8}, M=100 multi-row-tile, dispatch
  boundary, 100x repeats, two-stream, graph capture/replay)
- upstream RDNA3 suites (`test_rdna3_w4a16`, `_compile_guards`,
  `_selection`, `_moe_w4a16`): **151 passed, 5 skipped** (non-gfx1100
  guards), 0 failed

title: [XPU] Preserve non-contiguous strides when pinning CPU tensors for UVA view
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
## Purpose

When obtaining an XPU accelerator view from an unpinned CPU tensor, the previous implementation invoked `cpu_tensor.contiguous()` before pinning the memory. This operation converted non‑contiguous strided views (e.g., the transposed weight‑scale tensor `scale_kn.t()`) into contiguous ones, discarding their original stride patterns. Later, applying `.t()` on these contiguous copies produced non‑contiguous tensors again, which triggered extra implicit `.contiguous()` copies during GEMM execution and degraded performance.

## Changes

- Modify the XPU‑specific `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor` to allocate pinned memory via `torch.empty_strided` using the original tensor's size and stride, instead of first making the tensor contiguous.
- Add a new test `test_non_contiguous_strided_view` under `tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py` to validate both pinned and unpinned non‑contiguous strided views.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
author: MohitAMD
body:
## Summary
Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation, the prefill
(producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead blocks that the
decode (consumer) side never allocates. The producer's local block list therefore ends up
**longer** than the consumer's remote list, and the first prefill→decode KV write crashed
with `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` (e.g. 8003 vs 8000 at n=3),
making MTP unusable on MoRI-IO.

## Fix
The surplus is trailing lookahead scratch, not prompt KV, so it must be dropped **before**
the producer saves — not masked at transfer time.

- **Clamp on the WRITE producer save path** (`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler`): a new
  `_clamp_to_prompt_blocks` trims each **full-attention** KV group to its prompt length
  (`ceil(num_prompt_tokens / block_size)`), block-size-agnostic and per-group so it works
  under the hybrid multi-KV-group manager. Sliding-window groups are left untouched.
- **Chunked-prefill final-chunk detection by token progress** (`_is_final_prefill_chunk`):
  the save fires when `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled >= num_prompt_tokens`, which is
  immune to speculative-lookahead block inflation (a block-count check is not). This also
  correctly handles a final chunk that allocates **no new blocks** (`new_block_ids is None`),
  which previously dropped the save and hung the decode leg.
- **Keep the loud invariant**: `compute_block_transfer_offsets` still raises on a genuinely
  longer-local list — a real bug in READ mode — rather than silently clamping. The relaxation
  lives only in the WRITE save path where the surplus is legitimate.
- **Fail closed on unsupported combos**: MoRI-IO WRITE mode + sliding-window attention (with
  or without spec decode) raises `NotImplementedError`, because the positional prompt-prefix
  save would ship out-of-window null blocks. READ + SWA (+ spec) is unaffected: block ids are
  pre-clipped to computed tokens before the connector sees them.

## Tests
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py`: WRITE-mode clamp (single- and
  multi-group), chunked-prefill accumulation, the lookahead final-chunk regression (final
  chunk with `new_block_ids=None`), and the WRITE spec+SWA guard (reachable only under a
  uniform SWA model with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`: retains the loud longer-local
  `ValueError` guard and the shorter-local READ-mode partial-transfer behavior.

## Validation
GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP **1P1D / 1P2D PD-disagg** (vLLM v0.27.1 + AITER v0.1.19), MTP n=3:
- KV transfer succeeds (clamp fires, e.g. `8003 -> 8000` / `8 -> 5`); no more ValueError.
- Coherent output, **0 token-0 (`!`) corruption**, FULL cudagraph engaged.
- 8k/8k decode-heavy shows the expected MTP TPOT win (1.36–1.45×) at low concurrency.

## Not a duplicate
This is the only open PR addressing MoRI-IO KV block-offset handling under speculative
decoding. It builds on (does not duplicate) the upstream hybrid/multi-KV-group MoRI-IO
refactor: it keeps that connector's structure and guards, and only adds the spec-decode
clamp + lookahead-safe final-chunk detection on top.

## AI assistance
Prepared with AI assistance (Cursor). All changed lines and tests were reviewed, and the
behavior was validated end-to-end by the submitter on GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP PD-disaggregated
serving (1P1D/1P2D).

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py` (ROCm + mori) — 62 passed
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean
- [x] MoRI-IO PD-disagg smoke with `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` on both roles
- [x] Non-spec PD-disagg regression (equal local/remote path unchanged)

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fall back for high-rank MoE LoRA
author: xiaoyu-xyz
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55158.

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank` values above 128, but the non-fully-sharded
MoE LoRA dispatch unconditionally selected the one-shot Triton kernel, whose
rank dimension is limited to 128. This caused engine initialization to fail
during CUDA graph warm-up even when the loaded adapter's actual rank was only
4, because the MoE LoRA buffers are padded to the configured maximum rank.

This change:

- keeps ranks up to 128 on the existing one-shot fast path;
- routes larger ranks to the existing two-kernel shrink/expand path;
- lets that fallback preserve the existing `add_inputs=False` contract used by
  dual-stream and other MoE LoRA callers; and
- retains the one-shot assertion as a defensive kernel-local guard.

Rank tiling could extend the one-shot kernel in the future, but the existing
fallback is a smaller correctness-first fix and avoids changing the kernel's
register-pressure/performance characteristics.

## Duplicate check

No exact open issue or fix PR was found after searching for the assertion text,
function name, `max_lora_rank=256`, and MoE LoRA rank fallback. PR #42290's
review did identify both the missing rank fallback and the dual-stream risk,
but those comments were not addressed before merge and current main still has
the mismatch. Related issues and PRs are listed in #55158.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff format --check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uv run --no-sync pytest -q \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py \
  -k large_rank_fallback
```

The targeted numerical test compares the Triton result with a PyTorch
reference across:

- rank 128 (one-shot boundary) and 256 (fallback);
- `add_inputs=True` and `False`; and
- one and two LoRA slices, covering both TMA descriptor layouts on supported
  GPUs.

An end-to-end check starts the public Nemotron MoE model from #55158 with
`--max-lora-rank 256` and verifies that CUDA graph warm-up completes and a LoRA
request returns HTTP 200.

## Test Result

- Ruff format: passed.
- Ruff lint: passed.
- Python syntax and custom-op real/fake signature checks: passed.
- Targeted numerical test on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: passed
  (`8 passed, 417 deselected`). This covers rank 128/256,
  `add_inputs=True/False`, and one/two LoRA slices.
- End-to-end test on 2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with TP=2: passed. At commit
  `29a6af589`, the public Nemotron MoE model and rank-4 dummy adapter started
  with `--max-lora-rank 256`; both PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA graph capture
  completed, `/health` returned HTTP 200, and a request to the `dummy` LoRA
  model returned HTTP 200.

GPU test environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, compute
capability 8.0.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with code-path analysis, drafting the patch and tests,
and duplicate-work research. The human submitter reviewed every changed line,
validated the design, and verified the reported GPU test results.

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
author: drakosha
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90
  sparse backend; nothing else touches these call sites.

## Testing

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on, CPU offload
with a 256 GiB region. Both fixes have been running in production here since 2026-08-29
and 2026-09-01 respectively.

- fp8 fix: without it the server does not start; with it `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` is
  selected and the KV pool holds 4,503,445 tokens against 2,532,577 in bf16.
- workspace fix: available KV memory 29.44 -> 32.06 GiB, GPU KV cache size
  4,503,445 -> 4,904,494 tokens (+8.9%). Note that run also raised `--max-num-seqs`
  16 -> 32, so part of the freed memory went back into per-sequence buffers.
- Regression battery after the workspace change: needle retrieval on 1M-token prompts
  4/4 at depths 0.05/0.35/0.65/0.95; 32 concurrent 118k-token prompts, 32/32 with 0
  failures and 0 preemptions; an eviction cycle of eleven 500k-token prompts against a
  4.9M-token KV pool, where the return visit is served from CPU offload (61.0s cold,
  3.5s on return, `external_prefix_cache_hits_total` +492,800).

## Model evaluation

fp8 KV against bf16 on the same checkpoint: GSM8K 0.888 vs 0.880, MATH exact 0.9050 vs
0.9071 (symbolic 0.9671 vs 0.9664), MBPP 0.910 vs 0.920, IFEval prompt strict 0.880 /
instruction strict 0.925. All within noise. The workspace change moves no math: same
kernels, same inputs, only a smaller scratch allocation, and the needle battery above is
identical before and after.

AI assistance was used for this work.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
author: xijiaat
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing while Prefill is still alive with the same engine ID**. Without recovery, vLLM's cached `_remote_agents` entry and prepared dlists can keep subsequent requests on the stale path.

A receive failure schedules a descriptor-free `check_remote_metadata(agent)` check. This queries **local metadata existence, not peer health**. Only confirmed absence makes the peer eligible for recovery; a transfer error or probe exception alone does not.

## Implementation

- Track failed and locally invalid peers in `NixlBaseConnectorWorker`. One `_cleanup_remote_engines()` pass handles both replacement and invalidation, reusing `_cleanup_remote_engine()` to release resources.
- Defer probes and cleanup while background handshakes are pending. For invalid peers, reject new reads and wait for all existing receive handles to settle before cleanup. Replacement cleanup retains its existing queued-request guard.
- Clear recovery state in the shared per-engine cleanup, including TTL eviction and shutdown. A peer that is both replaced and invalidated is cleaned once; the replacement's address mapping is preserved.
- Route new and handshake-ready requests through the pull worker's existing read entry point. After cleanup, a fresh request re-handshakes the unchanged engine ID and uses newly prepared descriptors. Failed requests are **not replayed with old remote block IDs**.

The production changes are in `nixl/base_worker.py` and `nixl/pull_worker.py`. Recovery remains **pull-only**, with an explicit push-mode TODO. There is no new router API, configuration, or metadata probe on successful transfers.

Following Yannik's review, tests reuse `TestPeerReplacement` and `FakeNixlWrapper` instead of a separate hand-built recovery fixture. The existing receive/HMA fixtures and push test stub initialize the new fields. Nick Hill's read/handshake simplification is retained with authorship preserved.

## Related Work and Scope

Related to #49238. This is a follow-up to merged #50047, not another replacement detector:

| Change | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| #50047 | A new engine ID is confirmed at the same address. |
| This PR | The engine ID is unchanged, but NIXL has lost the decoder's local peer metadata. |

Both now use one base-worker cleanup pass, rather than separate replacement and recovery passes. The scope split was discussed in [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047#issuecomment-5629552908).

#52232 addresses HMA failure propagation and is **not included here**. Recovering future requests does not by itself guarantee that the failed HMA request returns an error instead of invalid output. TTL policy and the native UCX race discussed in NIXL #1987 are also outside this patch's scope.

Stuck reads or handshakes defer recovery; this patch does not forcibly release active resources. Native cleanup exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed. Recovery is not a claim that every UCX failure is recoverable.

## Validation

### Refactor and CI

| Check | Result and revision scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local source-AST/mock regressions after the refactor and September 29 main merge | 32 passed: 20 previous recovery cases plus 12 existing receive-lifecycle cases. These external harnesses are not full-import vLLM tests. |
| Old-fixture negative control | The same 12 receive-lifecycle cases fail with the original missing-field fixtures. |
| Recorded-main behavioral negative control | 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passing controls. |
| Local pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` | Passed on the September 29 merged revision. |
| [Buildkite #91865](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91865), September 29 merged revision | NVIDIA KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**; AMD KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**. The overall build reports "passed and blocked"; not every defined pipeline job was executed. |
| [Subsequent automatic main merge](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8aba1056b6b811b4770fd6bba860b54835c84ca6), September 30 | Pre-commit and DCO passed. No full Buildkite result is attached to this new head at the time of this update; #91865 tested the preceding revision. |

The failures in earlier CI #91736 were missing recovery fields in fixtures that bypass the worker constructor. Those fixtures are now initialized, and the subsequent KV Connector shards pass.

Regression coverage includes confirmed-missing versus healthy/probe-error cases, same-ID re-handshake with fresh descriptors, pending-handshake gating, sibling-handle drain ordering, new-read rejection, healthy-peer isolation, replacement/invalidation overlap, notify-only requests, expiry accounting, cleanup exceptions, TTL eviction, and shutdown.

Local full-import pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` and the incomplete vLLM runtime environment; the 32 local cases are not a substitute for CI. There is **no new native NIXL/GPU or model-serving evaluation of the refactored revision**. Historical experiments below remain evidence only for their stated revisions and configurations.

### Reproduction Commands

From a vLLM checkout with the repository's test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Focused replacement and local-invalidation coverage.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -k TestPeerReplacement -v --tb=short

# Broader connector CPU regression suite.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -v --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

These commands select the current tests; they are not presented as the exact Buildkite shard commands. The old `-k peer_recovery` selector no longer describes the consolidated tests.

<details>
<summary>Historical native and serving evidence, before the current refactor</summary>

### September 23 H20 validation

Full vLLM Python imports in isolated H20 containers: **357 selected CPU tests passed**, including 18 recovery cases; the corresponding main-only selection passed 339. Eight selected baseline cases produced 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passes.

Real NIXL/UCX probes passed with 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers. With the peer still alive, the probe deliberately removed local metadata, observed the stale-read failure, invoked patched cleanup, and explicitly reloaded the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads continued working. Automatic re-handshake was covered separately by pytest.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python source used native extensions from the existing vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main. No weights were loaded for this validation. This is not a model-serving, natural-disconnect, or NVLink/RDMA validation of the current revision.

[Exact commands, full selected logs, and native probe](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/34c74ce35e1f68958e5881a1907bf84d).

### Original TP1 P/D serving experiment

The original implementation was tested with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`, and the existing TP1 packed-layout fix. With no active reads, a controlled hook removed only Decode's local remote metadata, retaining the Python cache. A real stale read failed with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`; fresh requests automatically re-handshook the unchanged Prefill engine ID and returned the expected short answers.

The **recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid tokens**. Adding #52232 and an API terminal-error follow-up produced a passing 10-request scenario: two normal controls, four controlled failures across Chat/Completion and streaming/non-streaming, and four fresh Chat recoveries. The failed requests emitted no generated content. This combined result must not be attributed to the recovery-only diff. Attribution for the HMA change belongs to Tyler Michael Smith.

The original recovery-only CPU selections passed 353 distinct cases across two runs. The combined recovery/HMA/API experiment passed 425 selected tests, not 425 tests of this standalone patch. Full original logs retain earlier failures and an independently wrong pre-injection arithmetic control.

This is controlled failure-path evidence, not general accuracy, natural transport-failure reproduction, multi-rank native-race coverage, or a guarantee of production readiness.

[Selected raw logs, response bodies/SSE, commands and patches](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/a975858a507d6c45fd394b3675cc0ab9). Internal addresses and paths are anonymized. The HMA/API evidence is also reported in [#52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232#issuecomment-5552174526).

### Maintainer simplification

Nick Hill's [simplification](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec) was incorporated with authorship and sign-off preserved. It reuses main's in-flight-transfer guard rather than a second request-to-engine map: receive metadata remains available until the handles settle. The subsequent refactor retains that approach and moves cleanup into the base worker as suggested by Yannik Hinteregger.

</details>

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this report. The human submitter reviewed and approved the original contribution; subsequent compatibility adaptations remain subject to human review. Historical results and limited failure-path tests are not claims of comprehensive model evaluation or production readiness.

title: [MyPy][4/N] Fix mypy errors in medium-hard tests/ dirs
author: theSatvik
body:
## Purpose

PR 4 of #49569, covering the "medium-hard" test directories. Fixes every mypy error in them at the stricter `follow_imports=silent` setting and routes them into `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so the fixes are enforced. Claimed [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-5552556980).

**511 errors → 0** on current `main` (`10f6ab01a`):

| Directory | Errors on `main` | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tests/v1/kv_offload` | 232 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/worker` | 94 | 0 |
| `tests/parser` | 64 | 0 |
| `tests/model_executor` (incl. `model_loader`, `kernels`) | 49 | 0 |
| `tests/renderers` | 28 | 0 |
| `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text` | 20 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/metrics` | 13 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/streaming_input` | 11 | 0 |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | 0 | 0 |

With #51043 merged, `tests/model_executor` is a single silent-group entry, and this PR no longer touches `tests/model_executor/layers`.

## Approach (reworked per review)

- **No `cast()` anywhere.** Fixes use, in order:
  1. Runtime-true narrowing (`assert x is not None`, `assert isinstance(...)`, small typed narrowing helpers, e.g. for `EMABackpressureDetector` in `test_backpressure.py`).
  2. Stubs fixed once per file (`MockVllmConfig`, stand-in builders with honest return types).
  3. `MagicMock(spec=...)`, only where it can't make a test vacuous.
  4. A scoped `# type: ignore[code]` with a reason.

  `cast(X, None)`, `cast(Any, ...)` and `_NO_BACKEND` are gone. `supports_eagle3` uses `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)`.
- **Ignores.** Monkeypatched methods use `monkeypatch.setattr`, as PR 3 did. That includes the 4 older `method-assign` ignores that were already in these dirs on `main`, so there are 0 left. The 36 remaining scoped ignores (12 `type-abstract`, 7 `list-item`, 6 `misc`, 3 `call-arg`, 3 `attr-defined`, 2 `override`, 2 `dict-item`, 1 `call-overload`) each carry a reason. Starting fresh from `main` with `--warn-unused-ignores`, the migrated directories had 8 unused ignores; they now have 0. The two `apply_post_tokenization` ignores were already unused on `main` before the overloads below went in, so the overloads didn't remove them. The overloads are kept because they give callers the precise return type.
- **`vllm/` fixes folded in:**
  - `RayPrometheusMetric.labels() -> Self` (the 7 casts in `test_ray_metrics.py` disappear and that file is unchanged from `main`).
  - `@overload`s on `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`.
  - `"azacinto_foscolo"` in `AudioAssetName`.
  - `StreamingInput.prompt: PromptType | EngineInput`, because its consumers, `process_inputs` and `extract_prompt_components`, already take `PromptType | EngineInput`.
- **HiSparse.** No cast and no issue: production always passes a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup`, and the base class only appears because the test registers without a HiSparse config.

## Defects the type checker surfaced

1. **`RoutingMethodType.FUSED_TOPK` doesn't exist** (`tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`). Any read of `DummyRouter.routing_method_type` raised `AttributeError`, and `FusedMoE` does read that property. Fixed to `TopK`.
2. **Dead setup writes in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`.** `worker.refines_row_mirrors` and `worker._layer_mirror_callbacks` exist nowhere in `vllm/`, left behind by an upstream refactor. `test_hisparse_appends_reference_slots_within_a_mirror_phase` reads as if it toggles a row-mirror mode, but that setup did nothing. Removed.
3. **Dead observer attributes in `test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py`.** `slot_mapping_observer` and `host_mirror_forward_observer` likewise exist nowhere in `vllm/`. Removed.
4. **`CPUExpertsFp8` → `CPUExpertsInt4`.** The old test built its "monolithic" expert from a non-monolithic class, so it never reached the replay-support check. #59455 has since fixed this independently on `main`, so it's no longer in this diff.
5. **Wrong helper annotation in `test_obj_tier.py`.** `lookup_and_wait` was annotated `-> list[bool]` but returns `list[LookupResult]` (matches `test_fs_tier.py` now).
6. **Missing isinstance check in `test_factory.py`.** It lacked the `assert isinstance(spec, CPUOffloadingSpec)` its siblings have.
7. **`DUMMY_TOOLS` raw dicts (found, not changed here).** In `tests/parser/engine/replay_harness.py`, raw dicts are assigned to `request.tools`, and pydantic never validates them (no `validate_assignment`). The tool-schema helpers skip non-`ChatCompletionToolsParam` entries, so the parsers see no tool schema. Since fixing it changes what runs, it's left out of this PR; happy to send it separately.

## Behaviour changes

**None.** The three changes you flagged (`DUMMY_TOOLS`, `mock_request`, `block_ids`) are reverted. Every change is now a type annotation, a runtime-true assert, an equivalent rewiring, the `FUSED_TOPK` fix, or removal of writes to attributes nothing reads.

## Annotation issues in `vllm/` worked around (follow-up candidates)

- **`GDNAttentionBackend`** doesn't implement the abstract `get_impl_cls`, so mypy treats it as abstract, which causes the `type-abstract` ignores in the worker tests. Model classes that subclass protocol interfaces with optional members are treated as abstract for the same reason.
- **`EMABackpressureDetector.default_config`** is annotated `-> dict | None` but always returns a dict.
- **`VllmJitKernel.dispatch(self, **kwargs: Any)`** makes subclasses with named keyword-only parameters fail the override check.
- **`supports_eagle3` / `supports_eagle` overloads** list `type[object]` first. With `nn.Module` resolving to `Any`, a model *instance* matches the class overload, and `TypeIs` narrows it to `type[SupportsEagle3]`. That's why `test_plamo3.py` and `test_qwen3_omni.py` use `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)` (the helper's exact body) instead of calling the helper.

## Test Plan

```bash
# strict-group mypy on every target file + changed vllm/ files, all CI Python versions
mypy --python-version {3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13} <target dirs> vllm/{assets/audio,engine/protocol,renderers/params,v1/metrics/ray_wrappers}.py
mypy --python-version 3.10 --warn-unused-ignores <target dirs>
ruff check / ruff format --check (v0.14.0) and typos on all changed files
python -c "from tools.pre_commit.mypy import group_files; ..."   # routing
# CPU (macOS, torch 2.13, VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty):
pytest tests/parser tests/renderers
pytest <every changed test file outside parser/renderers>
```

## Test Result

- **mypy:** `Success: no issues found in 254 source files` with `--warn-unused-ignores` on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; 0 `cast` added.
- **ruff / format / typos:** clean. All changed test and `vllm/` files route to the strict default group.
- **`tests/parser` + `tests/renderers` (CPU):** 6,814 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures are in `test_hf.py` and need gated Hugging Face models (Llama-3.2 / PaliGemma return 401). They fail identically on `main`.
- **Other changed test files (CPU):** 936 passed, 132 skipped, 89 failed, 1 collection error. I re-ran the exact same tests on `main`'s test files in the same environment, and the failure set is identical: 0 fail only on this branch. They need CUDA or compiled ops (`kv_offload/cpu` transfers, Triton launchers) or extra packages (`datasets`).

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for the type cleanup, this review rework and verification. The submitter is responsible for every changed line and for defending the contribution before merge.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][MLA] Align packed block strides for V3.2 sparse MLA
author: 200lz
body:
## Purpose

V3.2 sparse MLA did not publish the physical block-stride alignment its selected kernel requires. This PR sets the existing `block_stride_alignment` contract at the producer, lifts the field to `KVCacheSpec`, and lets the allocator consume it without an MLA type check. HiSparse hot-page and stride constraints are combined in one LCM so sequential rounding cannot invalidate the first constraint.

The requirement is selected by backend and cache format. Flattened-row paths, including FlashInfer sparse, share their predicate with warmup. SM100 FlashMLA paged FP8/NVFP4 additionally require independent native TMA alignment (`fp8_ds_mla`: 656 bytes; `nvfp4_ds_mla`: 352 bytes), without flattened-row warmup. Existing BLHNC/BLNHC support is retained.

This adopts LucasWilkinson’s minimized suggestion in 200lz/vllm#1: six files, +187/-27, including compact alignment/merge tests and the existing producer/allocator/binder contract test. Layout gating/threading, admission/auto-fit rewrites, and HiSparse PP capacity work are outside this PR.

## Scope and validation

This complements #56254’s existing alignment propagation and pool rounding by supplying the missing V3.2 producer requirement; upstream #53781 already fixed the fused-writer issue. Those changes are not duplicated here.

CPU validation on exact suggestion `1d45dcafade7903237c627d941fda7df26341d76`: **258 passed, 41 skipped**. A clean temporary merge with main `79468c20ef23227d4e051f807e10fd54fb24e24f` passed **265 tests, 45 skipped**. The PR branch itself was not merged with main.

That work reproduced the FP8 TMA assertion before correction and passed the packed FP8/NVFP4/backend cases afterward; the broader earlier B200 bundle had 182 passes.
