title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Use group-local ranks for torch P2P transfers
author: LostFox11
body:
## Purpose

With pipeline parallelism, EPLB passes EP-group-local peer ranks to its
communicators, but the torch NCCL and Gloo backends pass them as `P2POp.peer`,
which is a global rank. For an EP group containing global ranks `[2, 3]`,
local peer `1` is therefore interpreted as global rank `1`, outside the group,
and expert-weight transfer fails.

Use `group=...` and `group_peer=...` for both send and receive in the two
torch.distributed communicators. Add a transfer regression covering PP=1 and
PP=2 with two ranks per EP group and both backends.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-08 found no matching open PR in searches for
`EPLB`, `EPLB P2POp`, and `group_peer`. The related explicit EP topology PR
#52099 does not modify this communicator file.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation, regression, and local
validation. Backend and model validation were performed by the PR author.

## Test Plan

On a configured vLLM environment with four GPUs:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py \
  -k test_eplb_communicator_pipeline_parallel -q
```

The regression exchanges rank-tagged tensors within each two-rank EP group
and checks the received values against the global rank of the expected peer.
The four-rank case covers the nonzero-rank group `[2, 3]`.

## Test Result

The author validated EPLB with pipeline parallelism using both `torch_gloo`
and `torch_nccl`:

- Before the fix, both backends raised the following error:

  ```text
  ValueError: Global rank {global_rank} is not part of group {group}
  ```

- After the fix, tests completed successfully with both backends.
- Model evaluation after the fix: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B**, using the **Gloo**
  backend, achieved **96.51% GSM8K accuracy**.

Additional local checks:

- Supplemental local CPU validation with PyTorch 2.14.0: both communicator
  classes were loaded from the production source and exercised with real Gloo
  process groups and real `P2POp`/`batch_isend_irecv`. Only CUDA stream contexts
  and synchronization were replaced with CPU no-ops; the NCCL class also used
  Gloo transport, so this is not NCCL device-transport validation.
- Before the fix, both classes fail in group `[2, 3]` with
  `Global rank 0/1 is not part of group`; the two-rank PP=1 controls pass.
  After the fix, all four combinations of communicator and world size (2, 4)
  transfer the expected tensor values successfully.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and format checks, Python compilation, and
  `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py`: all applicable hooks passed with
  the Python 3.12 virtual environment on `PATH`.
- Native pytest command above: blocked during collection by missing `tblib`
  in the local macOS environment. The backend and GSM8K results above come
  from the author's separate test environment.

- Keep the request tensors captured by FlexAttention at their allocated capacity so finishing requests does not change their shapes.

Although [nightly 12674 passed](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12674#01a07b19-ca8d-499f-a279-e15993ff6da9), the relevant source is identical at both endpoints and both original workloads passed locally, so no introducing PR was established.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Detect NVFP4 in ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoints
author: stecasta
body:
## Purpose

`ModelConfig.is_nvfp4_quantized()` detects ModelOpt NVFP4 by checking that the resolved quantization method is `modelopt_fp4`. A checkpoint that quantizes some layers to NVFP4 and others to FP8 declares `quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION`, so `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.override_quantization_method` claims it and `self.quantization` becomes `modelopt_mixed`. The check returns False even though most of the model is NVFP4.

The consequence is not cosmetic. `enable_act_fusion()` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`) enables `pass_config.fuse_act_quant` for FP4 models precisely because, in its own words, *"FP4 quant is always custom so Inductor cannot fuse it"*. With NVFP4 undetected, `fuse_act_quant` stays False at **every** optimization level, `ActivationQuantFusionPass` never runs, and the fused CUDA op `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` is unreachable for models without manual act+quant fusion (currently everything except Llama and Nemotron-H), since that pass is their only route to it. The model then runs SiLU-and-mul and `scaled_fp4_quant` as two kernels with a bf16 intermediate written to and read back from DRAM.

Affected checkpoints include `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` and `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, both `MIXED_PRECISION` with 208 FP8 layers and 193 NVFP4 layers:

```
config.json -> quantization_config
  quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION
  group_0: W8 A8   (208 targets, attention projections)
  group_1: W4 A4   (193 targets, MLP + lm_head)
```

Passing `--quantization modelopt_fp4` explicitly does not help: `override_quantization_method` overwrites `self.quantization` and breaks out, so the resolved value is `modelopt_mixed` regardless.

## Fix

When the resolved method is `modelopt_mixed`, decide from the per-layer algorithms. `W4A16_NVFP4` is excluded deliberately: it quantizes weights only, so there is no activation quantization for the fusion passes to act on.

## Not a duplicate of #55367

#55367 fixes the same function for **compressed-tensors** mixed-precision checkpoints, where the top-level `format` is `mixed-precision` and NVFP4 has to be read out of `config_groups`. This change fixes the **ModelOpt** branch, where `quant_algo` is `MIXED_PRECISION` and the resolved method is `modelopt_mixed`. That PR's diff does not reference modelopt at all, so the ModelOpt path stays broken after it merges, and this change leaves the compressed-tensors path untouched.

The two touch the same function and will conflict textually. Either order works; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase. Happy to fold this into #55367 instead if maintainers prefer a single change.

## Test

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/model.py tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py
```

All hooks pass, including `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `mypy-3.10`.

New unit test `tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py` covers NVFP4 mixed with another algorithm, a mixed checkpoint with no NVFP4 layer, weight-only `W4A16_NVFP4`, and absent or malformed configs. A separate filename is used so it does not collide with the test file added by #55367.

The predicate was also run against the published `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` `config.json`, which returns True where it previously returned False.

## Measured effect

DGX Spark (GB10, sm121), `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`.

Kernel level, median of 50 CUDA-event timings after 10 warmups, `intermediate_size=17408`, 64 layers:

| M | unfused pair | fused | per forward pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 1.413 ms/layer | 0.755 | 90.4 -> 48.3 ms |
| 8192 | 5.437 ms/layer | 2.920 | 347.9 -> 186.9 ms |

End to end, TTFT at BS1 with `max_tokens=1` and randomised `prompt_token_ids` so prefix caching cannot serve them, median of 15, four arms in one server lifecycle each on one node:

| vs no fusion | M=1024 | M=2048 | M=4096 | M=8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fuse_act_quant` | -6.7% | -30.8% | -4.4% | -6.7% |
| `fuse_norm_quant` | -1.9% | -26.8% | +0.0% | -1.7% |
| both | -4.6% | -29.6% | -4.0% | -5.9% |

No arm is slower than baseline at any prefill length. The M=2048 column overstates: the unfused baseline is bimodal at that shape across server restarts (859.8 ms and 1172.1 ms for identical config in two runs), while M=8192 reproduced within 2%. The other columns are the trustworthy ones.

Decode was checked separately at 32K cached prefix + 2K ISL + 256 OSL with MTP-3, concurrency 1/4/8, both arms as cells of one sweep on one node, prefix cache hit rate 85.3% in both:

| concurrency | ITL | output throughput |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 38.06 -> 37.99 ms | 20.03 -> 20.00 tok/s |
| 4 | 53.44 -> 52.74 ms | 46.39 -> 46.40 tok/s |
| 8 | 82.51 -> 81.46 ms | 60.27 -> 61.50 tok/s |

Inter-token latency is flat to slightly better at every concurrency, so enabling the fusion does not cost decode.

## Accuracy

This change does not introduce or modify a kernel. It only lets an existing, already-default fusion pass apply to a checkpoint class it was being skipped for, and the same pass and fused op already run by default for non-mixed NVFP4 checkpoints. Greedy decoding was smoke-tested on both arms and produced identical output. A full accuracy eval was not run, so if maintainers want one before merging, please say which suite.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line, run the tests and hooks above, and collected the measurements myself.

title: [Bugfix] Support repsonse_format + tool_choice=auto
author: arpera
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39929

In case request has both response_format and tool_choice=auto then we construct structural tags for both constraints and do OR of them.

**IMPORTANT:** to construct structural tag for tools we do a simple trick. Since tool_choice=auto allows by default a tool call or any text, then we cannot use that structural tag. Instead we create a structural tag manually specifying tool_choice to be set as `required`. In that case structural tag would not allow arbitrary text but only valid tool call.

Some time ago there was added support for response_format + tool_choice=required case: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32127

title: [Bugfix][CPU][MoE] Fix out-of-bounds write and segfault when router weights are fp32
author: farzad-elastix
body:
## Purpose

On the CPU backend, serving an MoE model whose router weights are fp32 corrupts the heap on every router GEMM, and the process dies with a SIGSEGV or a glibc abort. Hunyuan-V3 crashes during warmup, before it answers a single request. MiniMax-M2 and Nemotron-H build their routers the same way. Models that set only `out_dtype=torch.float32` keep bf16 weights and are unaffected.

How it happens:

1. `GateLinear` stores MoE router weights in fp32, and decides whether to upcast the bf16 activation by comparing `x.dtype` to `self.weight.dtype`.
2. `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm` builds the GEMM primitive from the real fp32 weight, then with `remove_weight=True` frees the weight by rebinding it to placeholder `torch.empty(0)` without explicitly setting `dtype`. The original weight dtype is forgotten in the process and replaced by the default torch dtype, let's say bf16
3. In forward with a bf16 input, `GateLinear` skips the upcast, and passes a bf16 `x` to `ops.onednn_mm`, which sizes the output buffer from `x.dtype` while the primitive it calls still writes fp32, leading to invalid memory access.

This PR sets `dtype` explicitly at the three removal sites, using the `dtype` already captured above them, so the placeholder keeps the weight's dtype and step 1 compares against the real one.

Related: #27465 fixed a different route to the same corruption, and named the assumption this one breaks — *"I supposed all handler should use same dtype in a inference instance (process)"*.

## Test Plan

New parametrized case in the existing dispatch test, over the three weight dtypes:

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_cpu_unquantized_gemm_dispatch.py -v
pre-commit run -a
```

It forces the zentorch branch through the file's existing `_mock_zentorch_linear_unary` fixture, so it is deterministic on any host and needs no oneDNN dtype support.

Manual check of the real crash, before the fix:

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import cpu_unquantized_gemm, dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm
from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype

layer = torch.nn.Linear(4096, 192, bias=False, dtype=torch.float32)  # an fp32 MoE router
with set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16):  # what base_loader.py does while loading a model
    dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm(layer, remove_weight=True)
print("weight dtype:", layer.weight.dtype, flush=True)  # bfloat16, was float32

x = torch.randn(1, 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
cpu_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, layer.weight, None)  # writes 768 bytes into a 384-byte buffer
```

## Test Result

Before, the three new cases fail and the placeholder's dtype is the ambient default:

```
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype0] FAILED
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype1] FAILED
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype2] FAILED
E       assert torch.float32 is torch.bfloat16
E       assert torch.float32 is torch.float16
E       assert torch.bfloat16 is torch.float32
3 failed, 3 passed
```

After: `6 passed`. The manual script above runs to completion instead of aborting, and a 4-layer Hunyuan-V3 serve that previously died during warmup now completes a request.

AI assistance: root cause, patch and test were produced with Claude Code; I reviewed and ran everything.

title: [Bugfix][Bench] Fix bench mm-processor crash in shared request sampling
author: NickLucche
body:
vllm bench mm-processor` with `--dataset-name random-mm` crashes in the shared request-sampling path, because the mm-processor CLI does not define the legacy flags that `_to_serve_args` in `vllm/benchmarks/throughput.py` reads directly off `args`:

```
File ".../vllm/benchmarks/throughput.py", line 585, in get_requests
    requests = get_samples(serve_args, tokenizer, multimodal_backends=mm_backends)
File ".../vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py", line 1273, in sample
    prefix_token_ids = self.get_prefix(tokenizer, allowed_tokens, prefix_len)
File ".../vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py", line 705, in get_prefix
    if prefix_len <= 0:
TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
```

Two bugs in `_to_serve_args`:

1. It reads `args.input_len`, `args.prefix_len`, `args.backend`, and `args.no_oversample` directly, but `mm_processor.add_cli_args` never defines those flags (`AttributeError` on the first one encountered).
2. `getattr(args, "random_prefix_len", None) or prefix_len` coerces the default `--random-prefix-len 0` to `None`, so a `None` `prefix_len` is passed down to `RandomMultiModalDataset.get_prefix` (the same truthiness-vs-identity issue exists for `random_input_len` / `random_output_len`).

Repro:

```
vllm bench mm-processor --model <mm model> --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral \
    --load-format mistral --dataset-name random-mm --num-prompts 200 --random-input-len 32 \
    --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
    --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
    --random-mm-bucket-config '{(224,224,1):1.0}'
```

check https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56277 for run results (ran with this patch).

Fix in `_to_serve_args`:

- Read the legacy flags via `getattr(args, ..., None)` so the mm-processor CLI (which does not define them) is supported.
- Use identity checks (not truthiness) for the `random_prefix_len`, `random_input_len`, and `random_output_len` fallbacks so an explicit `0` is preserved.
- Default `backend` to `vllm-chat` (mm-processor drives all requests through `llm.chat`, so chat-format requests are required) and `no_oversample` to `False`.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Mistral Vibe). The change has been reviewed and tested end-to-end by the human submitter, who will defend it in review.

Generated by Mistral Vibe.

cc @DarkLight1337

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix flat/scoped mm_processor_kwargs merge and resolution
author: danigarciaoca
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56363.
Fixes #58406.

vLLM accepts `mm_processor_kwargs` from both engine configuration and per-request overrides, and supports both legacy flat kwargs and Hugging Face modality-scoped kwargs such as `images_kwargs` and `videos_kwargs`.

This PR defines consistent semantics across those two dimensions:

* **Generic vLLM handling** defines precedence across engine/request and flat/modality-scoped kwargs, discovers the supported HF processor kwargs per scope, and routes flat kwargs to the HF modality scopes that support them.
* **Model-specific handling** provides processor semantics that cannot be inferred generically.
  * For Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL, for example, `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` correspond to `size.shortest_edge` / `size.longest_edge`.


```text
                           Qwen semantic preparation
                               alias completion
                                      |
                                      ▼
                                 generic vLLM
                                      |
          ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
          │                           │                           │
 source/scope precedence       supported schema            flat → HF scopes
     MultiModalConfig         BaseProcessingInfo        InputProcessingContext
          │                           │                           │
          └───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┘
                                      |
                               resolved kwargs
                                      |
                              Qwen/HF adaptation
                                      |
                               Transformers / HF
```

### Generic `mm_processor_kwargs` handling

`MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs()` now applies source and modality specificity together. For an effective setting within a modality, the precedence is:

```text
engine flat
< engine scoped
< request flat
< request scoped
```

- When both values are mappings, they are merged recursively so a higher-priority partial override does not discard unrelated lower-priority entries.
- For other value combinations, the higher-priority value replaces the lower-priority one.
   - At the modality-scope level, a missing scope, a `None`-valued scope (e.g., ` {"images_kwargs": None}`), and an empty mapping are treated as absent and therefore do not participate in replacement. This applies only to the scope itself; an explicit `None` inside a non-empty scope remains a value.

This is deliberately more specific than a recursive merge of engine and request dictionaries: source precedence alone is not sufficient when the same effective setting can also be represented flat or inside a modality scope.

`BaseProcessingInfo` derives the supported processor kwargs for each HF scope from the processor contract and the modalities supported by the model. This keeps schema discovery generic for HF-compatible processors instead of requiring each model family to reimplement it.

`InputProcessingContext` then resolves flat kwargs using that per-modality processor schema:

```text
0 supported scopes → keep flat
1 supported scope  → route to that scope
N supported scopes → fan out to every supported scope
```

For example, if `size` is supported by both image and video:

```python
{"size": X}
```

is resolved as:

```python
{
    "images_kwargs": {"size": X},
    "videos_kwargs": {"size": X},
}
```

while a video-specific override remains isolated to video:

```python
{
    "size": X,
    "videos_kwargs": {"size": Y},
}
```

becomes:

```python
{
    "images_kwargs": {"size": X},
    "videos_kwargs": {"size": Y},
}
```

When flat and scoped values are both mappings, they are composed recursively with the scoped value taking precedence.

Unknown kwargs are preserved. Without a supported-key schema, vLLM does not guess destinations or create scopes; it only removes redundant flat copies already represented inside recognized HF scopes. This keeps existing callers conservative while preventing lower-priority flat values from being reintroduced alongside an already-resolved scoped representation.

### Qwen-specific handling

The generic layer intentionally does not know that different processor kwargs can represent the same model setting. Qwen therefore prepares its semantic aliases before the generic merge:

```text
size.shortest_edge ↔ min_pixels
size.longest_edge  ↔ max_pixels
```

This is alias completion rather than canonicalization. It makes request precedence visible even when engine configuration and request express the same Qwen setting through different aliases, while preserving explicitly supplied values.

Qwen uses the generic per-scope schema discovery from `BaseProcessingInfo`. Qwen3-VL only extends that schema where vLLM intentionally supports compatibility input that is not part of the native HF video processor contract: `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` are added as video routing targets even though `Qwen3VLVideoProcessor` accepts the equivalent setting through `size`.

Qwen sizing consumers now read the resolved `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` scopes directly rather than requesting a temporary flat view for one modality. Effective vision size remains Qwen-specific:

```text
processor defaults
< size
< non-None min_pixels / max_pixels
```

Qwen3-VL also applies those effective-size semantics at the HF boundary. If an image or video scope contains a `size`, `min_pixels`, or `max_pixels` override, the effective `size` is completed from the corresponding processor defaults before calling HF. This keeps runtime preprocessing consistent with the size used by vLLM's own sizing logic and allows partial scoped `images_kwargs.size` and `videos_kwargs.size` overrides to work correctly.

The final HF representation differs slightly between image and video:

```text
images_kwargs
    processor defaults
        + size
        + min_pixels / max_pixels
            │
            ▼
      complete size
            │
            ▼
     HF image processor
     (min/max remain valid)


videos_kwargs
    processor defaults
        + size
        + min_pixels / max_pixels
            │
            ▼
      complete size
            │
      remove min/max
            │
            ▼
     HF video processor
```

For images, `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` are valid HF kwargs and remain present.

For video, vLLM has historically accepted flat `min_pixels` / `max_pixels`, while `Qwen3VLVideoProcessor` expects the equivalent setting as `size`. Qwen3-VL therefore folds those compatibility aliases into `videos_kwargs.size` and removes the unsupported aliases before any HF call, including text/image-only calls.

For multi-video requests, list-valued `fps` / `num_frames` are converted to the corresponding scalar for each video using independent copies of the resolved kwargs. This preserves the shared merged state and the existing sampling/timestamp behavior.

### Compatibility and related work

- Legacy flat kwargs and HF-style scoped kwargs remain supported.
- Shared flat values continue to apply to every modality whose HF processor schema advertises support for them, while scoped values specialize only their own modality.
- Partial Qwen3-VL image and video size overrides are resolved against the corresponding processor defaults before reaching HF.
- Qwen3-VL keeps its historical flat `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` video compatibility while presenting HF with the native `size` representation.
- Unknown kwargs are retained, and the generic resolver does not attempt to become a universal HF processor validator or model-specific canonicalizer.

This work is broader than #58408: that PR recursively merges nested mappings within the same dictionary path, but explicitly leaves flat/scoped precedence and modality resolution for follow-up. This PR covers that full contract together with the Qwen-specific semantics needed to resolve #56363.

No documentation update is included because this is a bugfix to the existing `mm_processor_kwargs` behavior rather than a new user-facing option.

## 🛠️ Changes since the first review

The first review surfaced three issues in the `mm_processor_kwargs` merge/resolution path. The current implementation was adjusted as follows:

- **Normalize empty modality scopes:** `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs()` now treats a missing scope, a `None`-valued scope, and an empty mapping as absent, so none of them creates a scoped entry.
  - This applies only to the scope itself: an explicit `None` inside a non-empty scope remains a value, while other non-mapping scope values remain explicit and follow normal source precedence.
  - Keeping this normalization in the generic merge avoids duplicating empty-scope handling in model-specific code.

- **Move schema-aware merge/resolution to `BaseProcessingInfo`:** `_merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs()` now lives in `BaseProcessingInfo`, providing the common path for merging configured/request kwargs and resolving flat keys using `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`.
  - Qwen still prepares its `size` / `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` aliases first, then delegates to the base implementation.
  - Mistral3 now uses the same path and reads the resolved `images_kwargs.size` for its internal sizing, keeping vLLM's placeholder/token calculations aligned with the effective size used by Pixtral/HF, including configured-flat / request-scoped precedence.

- **Cache supported processor kwargs per `ProcessingInfo`:** `supported_mm_processor_kwargs` is now a `cached_property`, so the supported kwargs discovered from the HF processor are computed once per processing-info instance.
  - `get_supported_mm_processor_kwargs()` remains overridable, so model-specific additions such as Qwen3-VL's video `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` compatibility support are included in the cached result.
  - Only this processor-derived metadata is cached; request-specific merge/resolution remains dynamic, avoiding repeated processor introspection in sizing/profiling paths.

### AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from ChatGPT. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests reported below, and am responsible for the final implementation.

## Test Plan

<summary>Test commands</summary>

Run the generic `mm_processor_kwargs` merge regression tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_scoped_precedence \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_mapping_vs_replacement \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_empty_scopes_are_absent \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_empty_inference_scope_preserves_config_merge \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_empty_config_scope_allows_inference_merge \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_falsey_non_mapping_scopes_are_not_empty \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_non_mapping_scope_precedence \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_none_leaf_is_explicit \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_merge_mm_processor_kwargs_normalize_and_ownership
```

These cover flat/scoped precedence, recursive mapping merge, empty-scope normalization, non-mapping scope precedence, explicit `None` leaves, and ownership/non-mutation of the input kwargs.

title: [Bugfix] Disable sequence parallelism / async TP under batch invariance and add a TP regression test
author: LioEinaudi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56370.

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not prevent `pass_config.enable_sp` / `fuse_gemm_comms` from being enabled. The `SequenceParallelismPass` rewrites `all_reduce + rms_norm` into `reduce_scatter + rms_norm + all_gather` for compile ranges above `sp_min_token_num`; the reduce-scatter goes through the plain PyNccl path whose reduction order depends on which rank owns a token's chunk, i.e. on the batch composition. Measured on 4x RTX PRO 6000 with Qwen3-1.7B: with SP on, 1522/1536 sampled-token logprobs differ between `bs=1` and `bs=64` and greedy outputs change; with SP off all 1536 match.

This PR:
- forces `enable_sp = fuse_gemm_comms = False` with a `warning_once` when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, next to the existing batch-invariance guards in `vllm/config/vllm.py`;
- adds a multi-GPU regression test (`TP=4`, prompts on both sides of `sp_min_token_num`) under `tests/v1/determinism/` that fails on main without the guard and passes with it;
- documents the limitation in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`.

Making the SP reduce-scatter itself batch-invariant (owner-independent reduction order, as `reduce_scatterv` already does for the MoE combine) is left as a follow-up so that SP can be re-enabled under batch invariance later.

## Test Plan

- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k sp -x -q` on 4 GPUs (new test), before and after the change
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k bs1_vs_bsN` (existing test, unchanged)
- Manual: the repro script from #56370 with `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"sp_min_token_num":64}}'` now logs the warning, keeps SP off, and reports 0 mismatches

## Test Result

Note: with `enable_sp` set, `VllmConfig` currently falls back to the V1 model runner (MRV2 does not support SP yet), so every SP-on measurement above ran on V1; SP-off arms on V2. A forced-V1 SP-off control is bitwise stable (see #56370), so the effect is specific to the SP path. The gate is config-level and runner-agnostic; the SP/batch-invariance interaction should be re-measured once SP lands in MRV2.

Hardware: 4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, PCIe), vLLM main @ 7470082f5 + this patch, torch 2.13.0+cu130, `TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`, attention backend `TRITON_ATTN`.

New regression test (batch invariance with SP requested; the guard forces SP off, bs=1 vs bs=64 logprobs bitwise equal):

```
$ pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k with_sequence_parallelism
WARNING [vllm.py:1562] Disabling sequence parallelism and async TP (pass_config.enable_sp / fuse_gemm_comms) when VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is enabled: the reduce-scatter path is not batch-invariant (see vllm-project/vllm#56370).
PASSED
========== 1 passed, 19 deselected, 14 warnings in 144.62s (0:02:24) ===========
```

Same configuration on main without the guard (from #56370, `enable_sp=True, sp_min_token_num=64`, TP=4): 1522/1536 sampled-token logprobs differ and 17/64 greedy outputs change. With the guard, the standalone repro script from #56370 reports `enable_sp=False`, `logprob_mismatch_tokens=0`, `max_abs_logprob_diff=0.0`.

Existing TP regression (unchanged test):

```
$ VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "bs1_vs_bsN and TRITON_ATTN and 16-16"
PASSED
=========== 1 passed, 19 deselected, 14 warnings in 95.76s (0:01:35) ===========
```

Lint: `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the two Python files.

title: Revert "[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode  (#53664)"
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose

This PR reverts #53664 ("[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode"). That PR added a fallback in `MLAAttentionLayer.build()` that derives `dcp_local_seq_lens` from `seq_lens` whenever `CommonAttentionMetadata` does not carry it, together with an assert and two test-registry entries. The fallback is dead code: in vLLM's in-tree paths, `dcp_local_seq_lens` is always populated before the MLA decode path runs whenever DCP is enabled.

Evidence:

- The monolithic V1 model runner populates `CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens` unconditionally when `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2456-2466`), and this has been in place since before #53664 was authored.
- The modular model runner (MRV2) does the same via `maybe_prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens()` right before attention metadata is built, after PCP batch partitioning (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1728`, helper in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`). The helper returns `None` only when `dcp_size == 1`, in which case the MLA layer's `dcp_world_size` is also 1 and the branch is never taken, so the fallback is unreachable.
- Both runners always set `seq_lens` on `CommonAttentionMetadata`, so the assert added by #53664 is likewise unreachable.

Keeping the fallback would also mask future regressions in runner-side population: if a path ever stopped populating `dcp_local_seq_lens`, the layer would silently derive it instead of failing loudly. Removing it restores a single source of truth for DCP-local sequence lengths (the model runner). The two test-registry entries added by #53664 are removed along with the revert.

title: [bug-fix] Fix KV block leak with fault tolerance enabled in P/D disaggregation
author: tiankaijin
body:
## Purpose

Extend the fault tolerance (FT) framework (#44428) to prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregated deployments. When KV transfer is enabled, a worker failure currently causes two problems:

1. **KV transfer progress loss.** When `_model_forward` raises, the exception path discards the `kv_connector_output`, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` for in-flight transfers are lost. After `retry` recovery, the scheduler's KV transfer bookkeeping no longer matches the actual connector state, and requests can hang or leak KV blocks.

2. **Response queue residue.** In the executor's `get_response`, the first `FAILURE` response raises immediately, without dequeuing the remaining workers' responses. The stale responses left in the MQs are then consumed by the *next* RPC call, corrupting subsequent steps.

Key design:

- **Preserve KV state on failure**: a failed worker's `kv_connector_output` is extracted before the exception is shipped, carried via a new `ExceptionWithKVConnectorOutput` / `ResponseStatus.FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` status, and deferred into the executor's `KVOutputAggregator`
- **Drain-then-raise**: `get_response` always dequeues **all** workers' responses before raising (this covers all collective RPCs, not just `execute_model`), so no residue is left in the response queues
- **Defer-and-replay**: `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` stashes salvaged outputs; they are replayed through the normal `aggregate()` loop at the next successful step, so pending transfers are correctly reported without any special-case merging logic. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped (see Details)
- **Consume, don't drop**: on recovery, `EngineCoreSentinel` drains the batch queue and consumes each future's `kv_connector_output` (worker-side connectors use get-and-clear semantics) instead of clearing the queue wholesale
- **No new control flow**: everything rides the existing response MQ, batch queue, and `KVOutputAggregator` mechanisms

### Details

1. **Async output extraction.** `get_kv_connector_output()` is added to `AsyncModelRunnerOutput` and its implementations (v1 GPU runner, v2 `AsyncOutput` / `AsyncPoolingOutput`). In `WorkerProc.enqueue_output`, when `get_output()` raises, the pending `kv_connector_output` is extracted and shipped to the executor as `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`.

2. **Drain-then-raise in the executor.** In `get_response`, a `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` no longer raises immediately. All workers' responses are dequeued; KV connector outputs (explicit or embedded in successful responses) are stashed via `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs`, and only then is the error raised. Stale exception responses from other ranks are dropped. When FT is disabled or the executor has already failed, the original raise-immediately behavior is preserved.

3. **Defer-and-replay in the aggregator.** Salvaged outputs are stashed by `ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` and replayed through the normal aggregation loop at the next successful `aggregate()` call, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `failed_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` and worker metadata are preserved exactly as if they had arrived late. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped at stash time: a dropped event only costs a cache miss until its blocks are stored again, while replaying them could perturb the surviving workers' event quorum (e.g. overshooting LMCache's `count == num_workers` exact-match threshold). `aggregate()` itself is unchanged.

4. **Batch queue drain on recovery.** `EngineCoreSentinel` now drains the batch queue instead of `clear()`ing it: each pending future's `kv_connector_output` is consumed and applied via `scheduler.update_from_output(SchedulerOutput.make_empty(), ModelRunnerOutput.with_kv_conn_output_only(...))` (KV transfer state only -- the rest of the model output is not applied to avoid corrupting scheduler state mid-recovery).

## Test Plan

Unit tests added in this PR:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py \
    tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_engine_core_sentinel.py -v
```

- `test_output_aggregator.py`: replay of salvaged transfer fields, completion of recv votes, and salvaged event votes never entering the quorum (LMCache exact-match and Mooncake `>=` semantics, including late-live-vote cases)
- `test_executor.py`: drain-then-raise behavior of `get_response` under `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`
- `test_engine_core_sentinel.py`: batch queue drain surfaces `kv_connector_output` and drops failed futures

CI wiring: `.buildkite/test_areas/fault_tolerance.yaml` now runs the sentinel test in the FT pipeline, and `source_file_dependencies` covers `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/` and `vllm/v1/executor/` so aggregator/executor-only changes trigger it.

Manual verification:

**Model**: Qwen3-30B-A3B
**Configuration**: 1 prefill (kv_producer) + 1 decode (kv_consumer), MooncakeConnector, fault tolerance enabled

### Launching the cluster

Each instance runs as a separate `vllm serve` process.

**Prefill instance (producer)** -- GPU 0, port 8010:

```bash
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8010 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Decode instance (consumer)** -- GPU 1, port 8020:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8020 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Proxy** (routes requests between P and D instances):

```bash
python3 examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
    --prefill http://0.0.0.0:8010 8998 \
    --decode http://0.0.0.0:8020 \
    --port 8000
```

### Simulating faults

To simulate a device-side failure on the decode instance, inject a `RuntimeError` in the forward path, raising at a chosen step on the target rank:

```python
# Fault injection: raise at specific steps
if step_count in [250, 5000]:
    raise RuntimeError("FAULT INJECTION: exception in forward path")
```

### Sending inference requests

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "<MODEL>", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 128}'
```

### Querying FT status and issuing recovery

```bash
# Query engine status (one per instance port):
curl -s http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/status
curl -s http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/status

# Issue retry to both instances after both become unhealthy:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
```

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Avoid NaN in the Triton softcap for large attention logits
author: kushaldabbe
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56578 

`apply_softcap` computed `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio becomes `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned.

This is reachable for Gemma-2 style models that set `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`: a pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. Verified on a GTX 1650 Ti with the real helper:

```text
input  : [1.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -1.0, -10000.0, 4400.0]
before : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, NaN, NaN, -0.9999, NaN, inf]
after  : [0.9999, 48.2, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -0.9999, -50.0, 50.0]
```

The fix computes the same value as `1 - 2 / (exp(2 * S / x) + 1)`, which saturates cleanly at `+/-1` for either sign. The helper is shared by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k "50.0 and not fp8 and not q_dtype1"
```

## Test Result

- New test fails on main without the fix: `NaN` for the large scores.
- With the fix: the new test passes.
- 336 softcap tests pass. The `fp8` cases fail only on SM75, where Triton reports `fp8e4nv` is unsupported.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Report a full prefix cache hit as finished
author: jyizheng
body:
Reopens #54714 (accidentally closed by a bad force-push that orphaned the branch history; GitHub would not let it reopen). Same single commit, with @njhill's review addressed: `awaiting_kvs` gating with tests for the abort seed and `num_external_tokens == 0` readback, plus the cosmetic comments (condensed comments, collapsed tuple assignment).

## Purpose

`_read_blocks` returns early when the local block list is empty — D already holds the KV, so only the producer needs telling — and it returns without recording anything. `get_finished` builds `done_recving` from `_recving_transfers` and `_failed_recv_reqs`, so the request is named in neither.

The scheduler has no other way to release it:

```python
if request.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS:
    if request.request_id not in self.finished_recving_kv_req_ids:
        return False
```

There is no timeout. The request stays in `skipped_waiting` — a queue counted in neither `num_running_reqs` nor `num_waiting_reqs` — holding the blocks it was allocated, for the life of the process.

Recording an empty transfer list is enough: `_pop_done_transfers` already treats a request with no outstanding handles as complete. This does it whether or not the notification lands, since the KV is local either way and a failed notification only costs the producer a timeout before it frees its own blocks, which is what the existing message says.

## How it showed up

A 10-prefill/3-decode deployment under saturation. Restarting peers made `send_notif` fail 122 times in half an hour, and each of those requests was abandoned. The three decode workers ended up holding 73–85% of their KV cache with zero running and zero waiting requests and no traffic anywhere on the deployment, until their liveness probes killed them. Only a restart cleared it.

The state is hard to see from outside: with the requests parked in `skipped_waiting`, both queue-depth gauges read zero while most of the cache is spoken for.

## Test Plan

`test_full_prefix_cache_hit_is_reported_finished`, parametrised over the notification succeeding and failing, asserts the request reaches `done_recving`.

## Test Result

Against the unpatched worker the request is reported in neither case; patched, in both.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Normalize single-channel audio to 1D
author: Woolgathererer
body:
## Purpose

Mono audio with an explicit channel dimension can fail in Whisper preprocessing.
For example, passing a `(1, 16000)` waveform at 16 kHz through the offline audio
tuple path raises `ValueError: Failed to apply WhisperProcessor`, while the same
samples in a `(16000,)` array work.

`normalize_audio` returns early when the input channel count already matches
the target, leaving a 2D array for mono input. This also makes
`AudioProcessorItems.get_audio_length()` report 1 instead of 16000.

Return the only channel as a 1D waveform when the target is mono. Extend the
existing NumPy, Torch and parser tests to cover both channel layouts and the
single-sample case.

This reproduces without resampling. #47693 changes the order of normalization
and resampling, #56023 addresses unsupported multi-channel reduction, and
#51022 optimizes downmixing. Their current patches leave this early return

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Bound unanswered P2P lookup waits
author: jacklin78911-collab
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the unanswered-lookup portion of #56823. After a P2P handshake succeeds, a peer that keeps its transport alive but stops answering `LookupMsg` leaves the consumer returning `RETRY` indefinitely. The server's pending-lookup timeout cannot help when its serving loop stops progressing.

Start a 30-second progress deadline when the first unanswered lookup batch is sent for a request. A response that resolves a previously unanswered probe rearms that request's deadline while other probes remain pending. Repeated scheduler polls, additional keys, duplicate responses and unknown keys do not extend it. Completing all probes, fetching the matched prefix, or finishing the request clears the deadline. Unsent probes wait for `ConnectAckMsg` before their response deadline starts.

Each poll drains buffered messages and completed transfers before checking lookup expiry. Deferred store results are drained after transfer finalization, including jobs whose supplied blocks were not fetched. This preserves timely replies read by a delayed scheduler and returns completed load/store results before teardown. The warning identifies the peer, the expired request and elapsed time without progress. This is a progress timeout observed by the scheduler, not a per-key age limit or a transport-arrival timestamp guarantee.

### Session failure policy

An expired lookup sends a best-effort `DisconnectMsg` before marking the **whole peer session** dead, allowing the peer to retire its old session before reconnecting. Existing manager teardown converts unresolved requests to `MISS` for local prefill, retains their failure markers until request completion, and releases session resources. Other outstanding work on that same peer also fails through the existing disconnect path; completed results from the current poll are preserved. Maintainer agreement on retaining this session-wide policy is still requested. A request-local timeout would leave the same stalled peer available for subsequent requests to wait on again.

### Issue scope

This PR does **not** bound the pre-handshake `ConnectAck` wait. #51504 covers that path and is still open as of this revision. #56823 must remain open until both failure paths are addressed; this PR has no automatic issue-closing keyword.

The wire format and model computations are unchanged.

## Duplicate-work checks

The original submission checked #56823 and its comments and searched open PRs for `56823 in:body`, `P2P lookup`, `P2P lookup timeout`, and `P2P connect timeout`.

- #51504 covers handshake deadlines, peer caps and idle eviction; this PR bounds unanswered lookup responses after the handshake. The later PR to land will need to reconcile overlapping edits.
- #55962 advances control traffic while model work is running; it does not bound a missing response.
- #53087 bounds primary-tier `HIT_PENDING` waits, a separate state from remote P2P lookup `RETRY`.
- #53330 guards producer supply versus consumer demand; it does not add lookup response deadlines.

## Validation

### CI follow-up: `b98ec16094c2bfbd81a62bf1a2cef866f356b19e`

The main merge at `fb8ed9c` brought in a Ruff failure in `tools/recipes/sweep/sweep_html_report.py`. This follow-up applies the two-line `datetime.UTC` change requested by CI. The UTC timestamp behavior is unchanged; the current minimum Python version is 3.11.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tools/recipes/sweep/sweep_html_report.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files --hook-stage manual
.venv/bin/python tools/recipes/sweep/sweep_html_report.py --help
git diff --check
```

All passed, including the changed-file mypy hook. The complete two-line diff and the report-generation call path were reviewed again. AI assistance was used for this follow-up.

### Current revision: `9d1f68dff8f43aee265c69a789b6393df9828825`

Based on the merged PR head `5d23150e49e28fa79b46bab7ae502dc311025ef7`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p -q --tb=short
```

**229 passed**. The partial-fetch case supplies two store jobs but fetches only one; both completion results reach the caller in the poll that expires an unrelated lookup, and teardown reports neither as failed. The existing failed-transfer case now checks that its deferred failure also arrives in the same poll and is not repeated.

The reconnect regression uses two managers and real loopback TCP/ZMQ control connections with fake data transports. It checks local MISS fallback, retirement of the peer's old session, a fresh bidirectional handshake, and preservation of the expired request's failure marker. It waits for TCP disconnect events before reconnecting. Three additional consecutive runs passed.

Negative control: restoring only `server.py` and `session.py` to `5d23150` makes both new regressions fail (the unused store result is absent, and the peer retains its old session); the existing full-fetch case still passes. The revised production files were restored afterward.


All applicable pre-commit hooks, explicit mypy-3.12 and the whitespace check passed. The full diff and result-delivery/reaping call chain were reviewed again. This revision's validation is CPU-only; no new GPU generation or NIXL transfer result is claimed. Earlier model smoke results below retain their original commit attribution.

### Earlier revision: `c193c04184e7e04149613066c6c5d9aec200ab39`

Original base: `3f55ad2f073a7d1f573db5a5a3fe3dc9c688ddee`. Validation below is for `c193c04184e7e04149613066c6c5d9aec200ab39`, based on the prior PR head `9cc34f2288da0f83c3f8a6333437f8b13bc1e5c1`.

Coverage includes handshake gating, response progress across overlapping batches, a buffered response consumed at the deadline, duplicate/unknown responses and extra keys not extending the deadline, timer cleanup, completed load/store delivery during expiry, and manager-level `RETRY` to `MISS` fallback. The clock fixture is shared in `conftest.py`; timeout boundaries use `_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_S`.

With the two production files restored to the previous PR head `9cc34f2`, the four targeted regressions fail: partial progress, overlapping batches, buffered responses, and completed-transfer delivery. The revised production files were restored afterward.

Additional CPU-only checks used real loopback TCP/ZMQ control connections and a fake data transport:

- A reply received before the deadline and dispatched at the deadline: lookup returns HIT and the session remains alive.
- Connected peer with no lookup response: session disconnects after 30.010 actual wall-clock seconds and surfaces the failed request.

### Earlier generation/fallback smoke test

These GPU results were measured at the previous PR head **`9cc34f2`**, before the progress/dequeue changes above. They are retained as historical evidence, not a model run of this revision. This revision's validation is CPU-only; the inspected H20 resources were reserved by others, so no GPU workload was started.

A seeded two-layer Qwen2 model generated 32 tokens for each of three 96-token prompts through a real `OffloadingConnector` and ZMQ/NIXL handshake. The helper peer had an empty cache; it either answered MISS or kept polling its connection while withholding lookup responses. GPU and external prefix caches were reset between modes.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Make ExampleHiddenStatesConnector abort-safe
author: ys2025-AI
body:
Fixes `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` abort-path crash.

## Purpose

`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector.request_finished()` crashes `EngineCore` when a
request is aborted while still **waiting** (i.e. before it was ever scheduled) —
the common case when an API client times out and cancels queued requests.

`_request_filenames` is only populated in `build_connector_meta()` for
`SchedulerOutput.scheduled_new_reqs`. A request aborted before its first
schedule never reaches that code, but `Scheduler.finish_requests()` still calls
`request_finished()` for waiting requests, where the unconditional
`self._request_filenames.pop(req_id)` raises:

```
example_hidden_states_connector.py request_finished
    filename = self._request_filenames.pop(req_id)
KeyError: 'cmpl-b98ee80d8ff99a38-0-8e7006c7'
```

The `KeyError` becomes `EngineCore encountered a fatal error`; every API server
process then dies and clients see a storm of `APIConnectionError`.

This is the connector-side counterpart of the scheduler-side stale-completion
crash tracked upstream:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46240
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46304
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53079

### Changes

1. `request_finished` uses `pop(req_id, None)`; when no filename was recorded
   (aborted before scheduling) it drops residual `_pending_saves`/`_lock_fds`
   state and returns `(False, None)` — no hidden states to save, no blocks to
   delay.
2. `request_finished_all_groups` no-ops when the per-group block table is
   missing instead of indexing out of bounds.
3. `get_finished` only reports `finished_sending` for requests it actually
   tracked (a submitted DtoH copy); abort/never-scheduled requests no longer
   trip `assert req_id in self.requests` in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished()`.
4. `get_finished_count()` returns `1`: only TP rank 0 writes hidden states, so
   exactly one completion notification is expected per request; without this,
   `KVOutputAggregator` waits for `world_size` notifications.

(3) and (4) are coupled: (3) alone would never complete a request; (4) alone
would let non-writer ranks report before rank 0's copy finishes, freeing KV
blocks too early.

## Test Plan

New CPU-only unit test
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py`:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py -q --noconftest
```

Covers:

- `request_finished` on a never-scheduled request returns `(False, None)` (no `KeyError`)
- `request_finished_all_groups` handles a missing group table
- `get_finished` does not report an untracked/aborted request
- `get_finished` reports a tracked request once its copy completes
- `get_finished_count() == 1`

## Test Result

```
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py -q --noconftest
5 passed, 15 warnings in 18.92s
```

End-to-end: on vLLM 0.26.0 + vllm-ascend (Ascend NPU) during online DSpark
hidden-state training, aborting queued requests (client timeouts) previously
fataled `EngineCore` with the `KeyError` above; with this change the engine
survives abort storms and training runs to completion. Reproducer: send a batch
of long-prompt requests, let some time out and get aborted while queued.

---

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Add per-tensor FP8 W8A16 kernel to fix Ministral crash on CPU
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Summary

- Add `CPUFp8PerTensorScaledMMLinearKernel`, a per-tensor FP8 W8A16 CPU kernel
  built on the existing AMX block-scaled kernel. `PerTensorTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`
  was the only per-tensor FP8 CPU kernel available and wasn't wired up for
  AMX-capable CPUs, crashing on load of fp8-quantized `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`
  models (e.g. Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512).
- CI: match the wrapped `RuntimeError("Cannot find any model weights with ...")`
  that `default_loader.py` raises for a partial HF cache snapshot, so the CPU
  CI offline→online retry fallback actually triggers for that cache-miss shape.
- CI: mount `~/.cache/vllm` (in addition to the already-mounted `~/.cache/huggingface`)
  so multimodal test fixtures (`VideoAsset`, `ImageAsset`, `AudioAsset`, which
  download into `VLLM_ASSETS_CACHE`) persist across CPU CI container lifetimes
  instead of being re-fetched, and falling back online, on every run.

The two CI fixes were found while chasing recurring CPU CI flakiness during
verification of the kernel fix above (Buildkite builds #89028 and #89045).

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_scaled_mm.py -v`
  → 80 passed (covers both the new per-tensor kernel and the underlying
  block-scaled kernel it reuses, including the N-not-a-multiple-of-32 rejection path).
- CI script changes verified with `bash -n` and against the actual failing
  Buildkite logs they target: #89028 (CPU multi-modal tests re-fetching video
  assets every run) and #89045 (CPU spec-decode failing outright on a partial
  weight-file cache instead of retrying online).

title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect Mamba block allocation estimate that prevents request admission
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose
It is found for Kimi K3, a long request can be rejected admission when loading prefix cache from external KV storage (e.g., Mooncake) and get stuck in the waiting queue forever, causing entire system to stall. Investigation shows the bug is in Mamba's block allocation estimation call `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, which incorrectly calculates the physical blocks needed for such requests, potentially a regression caused by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53614

Stall reproduction on 8 x B300:
```
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0
export MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=mooncake_config.json
export VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=50052
export MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
    --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --prefix-match-unit 128 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --max-cudagraph-capture-size 2048 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":0}' \
    --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
    --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \
    --language-model-only \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"load_async":true,"lookup_async":true,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":false}}'
```

Sending a 1M-length request, clear the GPU local kv cache, and send the same request again causes the entire system to stall as the request fails the admission gate.

## Test Plan
Added unit test that checks equality of estimated blocks vs actual allocated blocks for mamba in `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, existing main fail the tests while the branch passes.
