title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 encoder CUDA graph capture OOM at startup
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61045.

With `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on, Gemma 4 made every encoder CUDA graph capture buffer far bigger than any batch its token budget can hold. Because of this, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` ran out of memory at engine start on a 32 GB GPU. This PR captures one graph per budget and per row width (70, 140 or 280 soft tokens). Each graph gets only as many rows as the budget can fill, so no capture buffer is larger than `budget * 9` patches.

Compared with #61092, this fix:

- Fixes the reported startup OOM. [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) limits the number of rows but keeps every row 2520 patches wide. On the reported setup, [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) still dies in encoder CUDA graph capture (`Tried to allocate 662.00 MiB ... 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`), both with the issue's flags and with images only.
- Makes video graph output match eager output (mean cosine 0.9994). On [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) the graph rows stay 2520 patches wide but the replay gathers at 630, so video output stays wrong.
- Adds 4 CPU test cases. They fail on the old code and also on [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092). [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) adds no test.

## Claims

- With the issue's flags, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` now starts on 1x RTX 5090 32 GB: 21 encoder graphs, 2.61 GiB CUDA graph pool. Before: OOM at startup (`Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB`).
- The images-only variant (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}'`) also ran out of memory at startup before. It now starts and serves images.
- Encoder graph output now matches eager output for video and for batches of 70-token and 140-token images. On the old code these outputs were wrong.
- The change is only in `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` (+49/-10). It uses the existing `capture_axes` support of the encoder CUDA graph manager. The manager and other models do not change.

## Validation

Setup: 1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB). vLLM commit `fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` (0.31.1rc1.dev296), with and without this patch.

Reproducer (the issue's command). No request is needed, because the failure happens at engine start:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --async-scheduling \
  --attention-config '{"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}' --moe-backend marlin \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 1}' \
  --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": 32}}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
```

Before: 4 runs out of 4 failed the same way. 3 ran in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` image and 1 in an editable install of that commit.

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=()
...
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py", line 1992, in encoder_cudagraph_forward
...
    pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.45 GiB of which 4.94 GiB is free.
```

After: 3 runs out of 3 on the final code started:

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=((70, 140, 280),)
Encoder CUDA graph capture complete. Captured 21 graphs across 1 paths.
CUDA graph pool memory: 2.61 GiB (actual), 2.99 GiB (estimated), difference: 0.39 GiB (14.8%).
Application startup complete.
```

The started servers answered every request. One run sent 14 concurrent 448x448 images, each showing a circle in one color, at temperature 0. Another run sent 1 image, 12 concurrent images and 4 videos of 32 frames. Each image answer named the circle's color.

Images only (same command with `{"image": 1, "video": 0}`, 1 run each):

- Old code: OOM in encoder graph capture, `Tried to allocate 644.00 MiB ... with 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`.
- This PR: 21 graphs, 2.61 GiB graph pool, startup complete. 6 concurrent images were each answered with the right color.

Graph output against eager output. A script outside this PR called `cudagraph_manager.execute(...)` and `model.embed_multimodal(...)` on the same inputs. The table gives the mean cosine over the leading tokens that the prompt uses:

| Input | Old code | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 image, 280 tokens | 0.9994 | 0.9995 |
| Batch of 70-token or 140-token images | items after the first: near 0 | 0.9995 or better | | 1 video 480x336, 32 frames | 0.185 | 0.9994 |
| 2 videos 480x336, 16 frames each | 0.191 | 0.9994 |

The old code could not start with the issue's flags. For this comparison it ran with a smaller config: `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets=[2240]`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch=1`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch=32`. The batch-of-images row came from separate runs with images only and 4 items per batch. These comparisons ran on an earlier revision of this patch. The later changes were a rename, test edits, and removing one capture row that no batch fills.

Unit tests (CPU, `device="meta"`):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py
34 passed

# with the old gemma4_mm.py, -k "encoder_cudagraph or encoder_chunk"
E       assert 2520 == (70 * 9)
E       assert 1856 == 14
E       assert 630 == (280 * 9)
E       assert [280, 70] == [280, 280]
4 failed, 5 passed, 25 deselected
```

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: every hook passed or was skipped, including mypy and `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

Root cause: the Gemma 4 encoder graph takes pixels as `(rows, patches_per_row, 768)`, with one image or video frame per row. `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` made this buffer too large in both dimensions:

1. Rows: it used `max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch)` for every budget. With video on, that is `58 * 32 = 1856`. But every row is at least 70 soft tokens, so a batch that fits 4096 tokens has at most 58 rows.
2. Width: every row had the width of the widest image, `min(budget, 280) * 9 = 2520` patches. A video frame, or a 70-token image, needs only 630.

So the 4096-token graph got a `(1856, 2520, 768)` bf16 buffer of 7,184,056,320 bytes: the 6.69 GiB in the issue. The first operation of the patch embedder needs another tensor of the same size. Limiting only the rows is not enough. The 4096 graph then still runs the vision tower on about 4 times the patches its budget can hold and takes 8.57 GiB of graph pool, and the next budget's warm-up runs out of memory. The width problem alone also breaks image-only configs, where every budget of 280 or more gets 58 rows of 2520 patches.

The fix, all in `gemma4_mm.py`:

- `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` declares one capture axis: the row width in soft tokens, `(70, 140, 280)`, up to the configured maximum.
- `select_encoder_cudagraph_items` returns the batch's row width as the axis key: 70 for video frames, and the padded width for images.
- `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` builds rows of exactly that width, and `min(max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch), max(1, budget // width))` rows. The one-row minimum is there only so that capture works when one row is wider than the budget.
- The replay pads list images of mixed widths to the widest one. So `get_encoder_cudagraph_item_specs` sets `path_output_tokens` to that widest width, and the manager never packs more rows into a batch than its graph has. `output_tokens` stays the real count and is still used to slice the output. Note: the docstring of `EncoderItemSpec.path_output_tokens` says single-path models leave it empty. Gemma 4 now sets it on its one path, for this reason.

The graph row width now equals the replay gather width. That is why video and narrow-image graph output, which were wrong before, now match eager.

Trade-offs:

- With the issue's flags, encoder graphs go from 7 to 21, one per budget and width. 3 of them can never be replayed: budget 70 with widths 140 and 280, and budget 140 with width 280. Each is one row. Skipping them would need a change to the manager's capture loop.
- In a config that already worked (images only, budgets `[280, 1120, 2240]`, 4 items per batch), the graph pool grew from 0.93 to 1.12 GiB and the KV cache shrank from 7.71 to 7.46 GiB. This was measured before the final row-count change.
- A list of images of mixed widths is packed at its widest width. It can need a bigger budget, or run eagerly when no budget fits it. The output stays correct.

Not changed here. These are older defects that are the same before and after this PR, and each needs a different change:

- Video frames with padding (for example 320x240, 63 real tokens per frame): the graph path counts the padding slots, so its output is longer than eager output (2240 against 2016 tokens) and later frames are shifted.
- Images with `max_soft_tokens` 560 or 1120 crash when `cudagraph_mm_encoder` is on, because the vision config has no `num_soft_tokens` attribute.
- `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` fails at encoder graph capture.

title: [Bugfix] Require cudnn-frontend >=1.31.0: cuDNN could replay an unloaded kernel from a CUDA graph
author: PeganovAnton
body:
## Purpose

Raise the `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` floor in `requirements/cuda.txt` from
`1.19.1` to `1.31.0`, the first release containing
[NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1195),
"Keep execution plans alive for the CUDA graphs recorded from them".

Before that fix, cuDNN could unload a just-in-time compiled kernel's library
when the last cuDNN owner of it went away, while a CUDA graph still contained
a node that launched that kernel. Replaying the graph then dispatched whatever
had taken over that code address. The upstream fix makes the graph hold a
reference for as long as it can launch the kernel.

The affected `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0-ubuntu2404` stack has both conditions:

- `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` is first in `_POSSIBLE_FP8_KERNELS` for
  CUDA and calls `bmm_fp8(..., backend="auto")`. Because
  `requirements/cuda.txt` declares `nvidia-cudnn-frontend`, the `cudnn` module
  is importable and `auto` admits the cuDNN runner.
- FlashInfer memoises those cuDNN graphs in
  `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=2048)`, keyed per shape, and the cache evicts
  cold entries. The GEMMs themselves are captured into the decode CUDA graphs.

In that stack, an eviction can release the last owner of a kernel that a live decode graph
still launches. The observable outcomes are an illegal-address fault, a CUDA
error reported at synchronisation, or — the case that matters most for a
serving stack — **silently wrong output with no error reported at all**.

FlashInfer 0.7.2, pinned by the tested base, now has a
[capture-retention helper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py#L3761-L3774)
that keeps captured cuDNN GEMM graphs alive for the process lifetime. This
separately mitigates the GEMM eviction path on current `main`. The frontend
floor still ensures that cudnn-frontend's own CUDA-graph lifetime fix is
installed.

## What this fixes

| Issue | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| #52225 | root cause identified directly | The investigation that led here, and the attribution is not statistical. A GPU coredump and CUDA-GDB independently confirmed the faulting kernel as `cudnn_generated_fort_native_sm80_matMul_pointwise_pointwise_knob_0_256x128x128_3_0`, launched with block (384,1,1) against a cubin declaring a 256-thread launch bound and 246 registers — the instruction-issue rejection that reports as Xid 13 `Out Of Range Register`. In the retained fault run, the cuDNN LRU eviction destroying a cold captured graph's plans and runtime kernels was observed directly, 436 µs after a newly compiled graph of a different shape, with the evicted kernel's CUDA graph node still live and no host launch since its capture 66 minutes earlier. A source audit confirmed no graph retention existed in the deployed cuDNN. That is the mechanism this fix removes. |
| #55571 | likely fixed | A third-party report, so the attribution is indirect: no coredump of their fault was analysed and no run on their hardware used the fixed wheel. What makes it strong is that *either* `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` *or* `--enforce-eager` reportedly makes it go away, and those remove exactly the two conditions this defect needs — the cuDNN lane, and CUDA graph capture. |

Deliberately **not** claimed:

- **#61007** (GB10 hang inside a cuDNN FP8 GEMM) is the same lane but a
  different failure: an unbounded host-side hang while cuDNN builds a plan
  lazily per shape in the hot path. This change does not address plan
  construction cost. #57209 is the change aimed at that.
- **#61069, #60119, #59768, #49926** share the Xid 13 or illegal-access
  symptom class but implicate other kernel families, and in #60119's case the
  report itself declines to claim a common root cause. No evidence either way.

## Relationship to #57209

[#57209](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57209) pins `bmm_fp8` to
cuBLAS on sm_12x, avoiding the cuDNN lane. This PR fixes the lane instead, by
taking the upstream fix, and is not an alternative proposal to it: #57209 also
cites host-side plan-construction latency in the serving hot path, which a
frontend bump does not change. If #57209 lands, this bump still matters for
every other cuDNN consumer reached through cudnn-frontend — the
`flashinfer_cudnn` NVFP4 linear backend and the cuDNN ViT and multimodal
encoder attention paths — and for sm_100 and sm_121, which #57209 does not
cover.

## Why the frontend and not the backend

Both upstream fixes work and each is sufficient alone: cuDNN 9.27.0.42 fixes it
for every caller including torch's own, while the frontend fix covers
cudnn-frontend consumers only.

In fairness to upstream, they consider the backend the thorough fix and the
frontend a workaround, and the frontend fix retains the whole `ExecutionPlan`
where the backend retains only the kernel code — so it holds more memory per
plan captured into a live graph. That cost is not quantified here.

The frontend is still the right change *for vLLM*: vLLM already declares a
floor for it and this is one line, whereas pinning `nvidia-cudnn-cu13` would
override the cuDNN version torch resolves transitively. Upstream chose to
write the frontend fix for exactly this reason — so that frameworks could pick
it up without waiting on a backend upgrade — and it is the vehicle they
offered for this report.

The consequence is stated plainly: cuDNN callers that do not go through
cudnn-frontend are unaffected by this PR. In vLLM that means torch
convolutions (`vllm/model_executor/layers/conv.py`) and torch's
`SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION` (`phi4mm_utils.py`). Those are fixed when torch's
transitive cuDNN pin reaches 9.27.0.42, which is the right lever for them; they
are not known to be affected today. If maintainers would rather take the
thorough fix, the backend pin is the alternative and I am happy to switch —
but it should be one or the other, since applying both creates two user
objects for the same kernel.

Upstream has already commented on #52225 pointing at the frontend fix:
<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52225#issuecomment-5900569717>.

## Test plan and results

Hardware: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), driver 580.126.20.

**Frontend fix, either side of the upstream merge commit**, with the backend
wheel as a second axis — 96 cells each side across backends 9.19.0.56 through
9.26.0.51, varying graph construction, workload profile, kernel-cache size and
owner-lifetime arm:

| frontend | reproducing cells |
|---|---|
| `07c939a6cce4` (pre-fix) | 22 of 96 |
| `4d4e428bd747` (PR #1195) | **0 of 96** |

Every reproducing cell is in the arm that releases the owner. The paired
`retain` and `user-object` arms are clean on both sides, which is what makes
this a comparison rather than an absence of failure.

**Backend fix on the public wheel**, with the pre-fix frontend held fixed so
the wheel is the only variable, run control-first within each configuration:

| configuration | 9.20.0.48 | 9.27.0.42 |
|---|---|---|
| populate, cache default/off, release | `SIGSEGV` | clean |
| stream capture, cache default/off, release | CUDA error 718, invalid program counter | clean |
| profile 52225, cache default/off, release | **3,948,544 of 5,275,648 elements wrong, 2,637,824 non-finite, `sync_status=0`** | clean, 0 mismatches |
| all six of the above, retain arm | clean | clean |

The wrong-result rows report no error to the host. The 9.27.0.42 release notes
carry the matching entry: "Runtime-compiled kernel code now stays loaded for
as long as a CUDA graph can launch it."

**The fix is in the binary vLLM actually imports.** vLLM reaches cuDNN through
FlashInfer's `import cudnn`, the compiled module in the wheel, not through
headers:

| wheel | `cuda_graph_retention.h` | retention symbols in `_compiled_module*.so` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.30.0 | absent | 0 |
| 1.31.0 | present | 41 |

**Cost**, measured on the stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0-ubuntu2404` image
with only the frontend wheel swapped, three repetitions per arm, medians:

| measurement | 1.28.0 | 1.31.0 |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph replay | 45.04 µs | 45.04 µs |
| CUDA graph capture | 192.0 µs | 229.1 µs |
| plan build | 7655 µs | 7710 µs |
| max relative error vs cuBLAS | 0.000000 | 0.000000 |

Replay is unchanged, so the steady-state decode path pays nothing. Capture
costs about 37 µs more, once per captured graph at warmup, and the capture
ranges do not overlap across repetitions. The plan-build difference is within
noise at three samples. Numerics are unchanged against the cuBLAS backend.

Eager execution, measured separately because the cost might not be specific to
graphs — per-call host time with GPU work left asynchronous, two repetitions of
seven rounds — shows no regression either: 1.31.0 medians 95.80 and 94.88 µs
against 1.28.0's noisier 112.10 and 95.34 µs, with overlapping ranges.

One nuance for anyone assessing exposure: from backend 9.22 onward the pre-fix
frontend stops reproducing at the default kernel-cache size and still
reproduces with the cache disabled, because the cache was holding a second
reference. Backend version alone therefore does not tell you whether a
deployment is exposed.

Note also that `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` resolves cudnn-frontend **1.28.0**
against the declared floor of 1.19.1, so the effective bump for that image is
1.28.0 → 1.31.0.

## Not measured

- **No end-to-end serving before-and-after with the released wheel.** The
  mechanism is directly established and the fix is verified on the
  deterministic reproducer, but the remaining step — serving the affected
  model at full exposure on the released wheel and showing the fault rate go
  to zero — is a multi-hour stochastic measurement and is not included. An
  earlier run with both fixes built from source did not reproduce the bug on
  Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4.
- **Read the lane ablation carefully if you cite it.** Disabling the
  FlashInfer FP8 class gave 7 of 12 against 0 of 12 at p≈0.0023 on the
  *family* endpoint (any `0x0d`/`0x0e`/`0x0f` fault in a cuDNN matMul); on the
  exact `0x0d` subtype alone it is 1 of 12 against 0 of 12, p=0.5 and
  uninformative. It corroborates that the lane is necessary; it is not the
  basis for the root-cause attribution, which is the coredump evidence above.
- **A Python-level reproduction was attempted and failed to fault its own
  control**, so it proves nothing in either direction and is not offered as
  evidence. The deterministic reproducer pins the engine and kernel config for
  both the target and the reoccupying donor, and FlashInfer's Python API
  exposes no way to select either.
- **The memory retained by the frontend fix is not quantified.** It keeps the
  whole execution plan alive per plan captured into a live graph, where the
  backend fix keeps only the kernel code.
- **No specific models are claimed as fixed.** There are internal reports that
  the backend upgrade resolved corruption for some FP8 Nemotron checkpoints,
  but they are soak observations without a paired control, so they are not
  offered here as evidence.
- The plan-build cost difference and cuDNN 9.28's expected opt-out are
  unresolved here.

## Duplicate check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cudnn-frontend in:body OR cudnn frontend in:title"` — no open PR changes this floor.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52225 in:body"` — one unrelated MoE PR.
- #57209 is the nearest open work; it avoids the lane rather than fixing it, and the difference is described above.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance. Every line of the diff and every
number above was reviewed by the submitter, the measurements were run on
first-party hardware, and the cells that were not measured are labelled as
such rather than inferred.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][KV Connector] Fix DecodeBenchConnector crash on bounded KV cache groups
author: grYe99
body:
## Overview

`HiSparse` + `DecodeBenchConnector` **crashes** on `GLM-5.3` when `ISL > device_buffer_size(4096)`.

```
AssertionError: DecodeBenchConnector block range exceeds allocated blocks: request=chatcmpl-bd27629bd71bb94d-9ff77f54, group=22, range=[0, 87), allocated=64
```

The assertion fires in the scheduler on the first qualifying request, EngineCore goes fatal, and the whole serve instance dies. ISL ≤ 4096 passes only coincidentally (see Root Cause).

## Reproduction

Single 8xH200 node, TP8, vllm 0.32.0:

```
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 256000 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{}},{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}]}}'
```

The assert above comes from this exact setup, on the first request with ~5.5k tokens.

## Root Cause

HiSparse (in-tree since v0.32.0, #60072) adds per-request hot-cache groups via `HiSparseHotSpec` — a direct `KVCacheSpec` subclass with a bounded allocation of `blocks_per_request = cdiv(device_buffer_size, block_size)` blocks. These groups opt out of external KV transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`, `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`): they are ephemeral per-request replicas rebuilt from their transferable source group after a connector load. `DecodeBenchConnector.update_state_after_alloc` assumes every non-`CircularBufferSpec` group is token-paged and asserts the computed token range fits the allocation.

The numbers in the assert, decoded:

- `allocated=64`: the hot group's per-request cap — `cdiv(device_buffer_size=4096, block_size=64) = 64`, unrelated to sequence length.
- `range=[0, 87)`: the token-paged formula `cdiv(total_computed_tokens, 64)` for the request's ~5.5k tokens.
- Hence the crash is deterministic for any request with ISL > 4096, and ISL ≤ 4096 passes only because `cdiv(ISL, 64) ≤ 64` by coincidence.
- `group=22` is one of the 78 `hisparse_hot` groups of GLM-5.3.

## Fix

Skip groups that opted out of external KV transfer (i.e. groups missing from `KVCacheConfig.transfer_group_ids`): select no blocks for them at fill-scheduling time, the same way startup-fill groups are already handled. NIXL/Mooncake already key off `transfer_group_ids`; no new spec-shape heuristic is introduced.

This also aligns the fill side with the connector's load-side declaration: `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids()` defaults to `prefix_cacheable_group_ids`, which already excludes these groups. Skipping them additionally avoids selecting the 78 `hisparse_hot` layers that are absent from the connector's `kv_caches` (previously warned about on every request).

Groups with `enable_kv_transfer=True` (circular buffers, Mamba, sliding-window attention included) take exactly the same paths as on main — token-range math and the in-range assert are unchanged — so no currently working configuration changes behavior.

## Validation

- New regression test `test_decode_bench_connector_skips_non_transfer_groups`: builds a group from the real in-tree `HiSparseHotSpec` with `enable_kv_transfer=False` and asserts its entry in `reqs_to_fill` is empty; no checkpoint needed, runs in the existing kv_connector CI job. **Fails on main's `decode_bench_connector.py`, passes on this branch** (verified by checking out main's connector and re-running).
- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py -q` → 30/30 pass.
- E2E on the Reproduction setup (single node, TP8 + MultiConnector): on v0.32.0 as released, the first request with ISL > 4096 asserts as above; with the fill-side fix in this branch, the same serving setup handles such requests normally.

AI assistance was used (analysis, fix, tests, validation); every changed line reviewed and tested by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix renderers tests broken by tool name removal from warn logs
author: ganeshr10
body:
## Overview

[#59294](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59294) removed the tool name from the two malformed-`arguments` warnings in `vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`, but did not update `tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py`, which still asserts the name appears in the emitted record. Seven tests have failed on `main` since it merged.

That PR's own `:computer: (CPU) Reasoning + Renderers` job failed for this reason ([build 94769](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94769)) and it was merged red, so the breakage landed on `main` and now fails for every PR that touches a `cpu-async-engine-deps` path.

## Fix

Drop the four tool-name assertions and keep each test asserting the part of the message that still exists. The tool name was the only thing distinguishing `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large` from the small-payload case, so it asserts on the logged length instead, which is what actually covers the point of having a large case: an 18 KB payload is summarised by length rather than logged.

The source change in #59294 is left alone: not logging the tool name is the intended behavior.

## Validation

```
$ pytest -q tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py -k tool_call_arguments
12 passed
```

Failing tests before this change, all with the same shape:

```
FAILED renderers/test_chat_utils.py::test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small
  assert 'exec' in 'Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (54 chars);
  coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.'
```

- `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[[]]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[42]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object[true]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object["hello"]`
- `test_tool_call_arguments_multiple_independent`

title: [CI] Fix B200 FusedMoE Layer Kernels hang on NVSHMEM IB setup
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

`(B200) FusedMoE Layer Kernels` is failing ~24% of main runs (59/247 over the last two weeks), almost all of them by hanging until the 90 minute job timeout. The hang is in `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]`, where NVSHMEM's InfiniBand transport setup fails and the spawned workers never exit. This PR keeps these single-node DeepEP tests on NVLink and off the NICs, and makes any future hang fail fast.

Alternative to the stalled draft #53332, which retries the launch instead of avoiding IB; details below.

## Claims

- The CUDA DeepEP cases of `test_moe_layer` no longer use NVSHMEM's IB transports. That is where every B200 hang starts. Both GPUs in each test are on the same node, connected by NVLink, so the IB path carries no test traffic anyway.
- `parallel_launch_with_config` kills its workers and raises `TimeoutError` after 15 minutes. `test_moe_layer` already turns that into a normal test failure, so a future hang costs one test instead of the whole job.
- The B200 job timeout drops from 90 to 45 minutes. Passing runs take 15–18 minutes, and the slowest passing run in the last two weeks took 36 minutes.

## Validation

**CI history (job logs from builds 94300–94498, 56 runs: 47 passed, 8 timed out, 1 failed fast).** All 8 timeouts show the same signature and then no further output until the job is cancelled:

```
ibrc.cpp:427:  non-zero status: 22 ibv_modify_qp failed
ibrc.cpp:1526: non-zero status: 7 ep_connect failed
init.cu:1047:  non-zero status: 7 nvshmem setup connections failed
```

**Local repro (2x B300 on one node).** IB is unusable on this box for an unprivileged user (8 MB memlock), which makes it a stand-in for a broken IB setup. Command:

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k deepep
```

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]` | fails in NVSHMEM init (`ibrc.cpp:314: cq creation failed`) | passes (48/48 subcases) |
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_high_throughput-2-1-True]` | n/a | 191/192 subcases pass |

The one high-throughput miss is a local DeepGEMM JIT failure (`nvcc fatal: Failed to preprocess host compiler properties`), unrelated to this change. DeepEP high-throughput mode with 2 ranks allocates no RDMA buffer and does not initialise NVSHMEM.

**Launcher timeout.** Tested with a worker that sleeps forever and the timeout set to 30 s: it raised `TimeoutError` after 31 s, and no child processes were left behind. A normal launch still returns.

## Details

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- **It is the first NVSHMEM init that fails, not re-initialisation.** The test creates a new DeepEP low-latency buffer for each subtest, so a passing run initialises NVSHMEM 48 times. Each init logs 32 `cudaHostRegister` fallback warnings (1536 per passing run). All 8 hung runs stop after exactly 32, before the first subtest finishes. So the hang always happens on the first init of the job, never on a later one.
- **IBGDA is unavailable in these pods, so NVSHMEM falls back to IBRC.** The `cudaHostRegister ... error=800` / `ibgda_*` fallback warnings appear in passing runs too. The fallback IBRC queue-pair connect is what intermittently fails, and the worker group then hangs instead of exiting.
- **It looks host- or contention-related.** Timeouts hit dgxB200-09/12/14 (8 of 32 runs) and none of 01/11/16 (0 of 23). 5 of the 8 timeouts started within 2–5 minutes of another run of this job on the same host. Every B200 pod sees all of the node's NICs (the job's `nvidia-smi topo -m` lists 12), so concurrent pods share them. This is suggestive, not proven.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why these settings</summary>

- `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` disables IBRC.
- `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` hides the NICs from IBGDA. DeepEP's low-latency buffer sets `NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=1` unconditionally, and `REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` alone still tried IBGDA locally and failed.
- With no remote transport, NVSHMEM uses its P2P transport. DeepEP's low-latency kernels take the NVLink store path whenever `nvshmemi_get_p2p_ptr` returns a peer pointer, which is the case for every peer in a single-node test.
- The settings are applied through the existing `env_dict` hook, only for CUDA DeepEP backends. ROCm/MoRI paths are untouched.
- The CI pods for both jobs that run this file have their GPU pair on NVLink (`NV18` in the `nvidia-smi topo -m` of the B200 job and the H100 job). If a future runner had a GPU pair without peer access, the low-latency case would fail clearly rather than hang.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Relation to #53332</summary>

#53332 (draft, idle since Sep 14) adds an opt-in join timeout plus a single retry with NVSHMEM debug logging. It is framed around NVSHMEM re-initialisation. The B200 data above shows the failure is on the first init and in the IB transport, so this PR removes the IB dependency rather than retrying it. The timeout here applies to every `parallel_launch_with_config` caller: the longest single launch seen in a passing B200 run is ~195 s, against the 900 s limit.

The H100 SIGSEGV that #53332 also describes happened after `init failed for transport: IBGDA`. This change should avoid that too, but I have not reproduced it.

</details>

**Limitations.** This drops IB transport coverage from `test_moe_layer`. That coverage was never meaningful here: the tests are single-node, and IB setup on the CI pods only works via fallback. Multi-node DeepEP coverage belongs in a multi-node test.

title: [Bugfix] Fix NaN output of the Mamba2 chunk scan kernel on sm90
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview Fixes #61603. On Hopper (sm90), the Mamba2 SSD kernel `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` writes NaN/Inf into whole output rows from finite inputs with some of its autotune configs (8 of 23 in the reproducer). The autotuner picks configs by speed only, so it can pick one of them. This PR drops these configs on CUDA sm90 only. It uses one rule taken from the compiled code: drop a config when `num_warps % 4 == 0`, `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0` and `num_stages > 1`. Compared with #61664, this fix: - also drops three configs (M/N/K, warps, stages) that compile to the same racy code on Triton 3.7.1: 64/32/32 8w 2s, 128/256/64 8w 3s and 128/32/32 4w 4s. On the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree the reproducer still prints `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 1 of 15` (128/32/32 4w 4s gave NaN in 81 of 100 calls), and 128/256/64 8w 3s gave NaN in 50 of 50 calls at dstate 256. - adds a test that runs the real kernel with every config in the list. It fails on the old code and on the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree. The tests in [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) are mock-only and never run the kernel; on the old code they fail only with an `ImportError` that comes from that PR's own refactor. ## Claims - On sm90, no config left in the autotune list gives NaN on the reproducer: `0 of 12`, against `8 of 23` before. - Other platforms keep all 23 configs. The filter returns the list unchanged unless the device is CUDA with capability 9.0. - No speed cost at the shapes measured on an H20-3e: the fastest config of the old list is kept. - The new test `test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches` fails on the old code and passes with the fix. ## Validation Setup: 1 x NVIDIA H20-3e (sm90), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, vLLM at commit `77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`, then the same commit plus this PR. Reproducer: the issue's script, changed to force each config of `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` in turn and run it 100 times on finite inputs (seed 0, 181 tokens, 2 chunks). Run it with `python sweep.py`. I swept the whole list because the issue's `GOOD` config is not in the list at this commit.
sweep.py (the issue's unused BAD/GOOD/force_old lines left out) ```python import torch, triton from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssd_chunk_scan import ( _chunk_scan_fwd, _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel) print("triton", triton.__version__, "torch", torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)) seqlen, nchunks = 181, 2 dev, g = "cuda", torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) rn = lambda *s, dt=torch.bfloat16, sc=0.5: (torch.randn(*s, generator=g, device=dev)*sc).to(dt) x, C = rn(seqlen,64,64), rn(seqlen,8,128) cb = rn(nchunks,8,128,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=1.0) dt_ = (torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev)*0.1).float() dA = (-torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev).cumsum(-1)*0.05).float() states = rn(nchunks,64,64,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1) cu = torch.tensor([0,128,181], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) sidx = torch.zeros(nchunks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) ALL = list(_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs) print("inputs finite:", all(bool(torch.isfinite(t.float()).all()) for t in (x,C,cb,dt_,dA,states))) nbad = 0 for i, c in enumerate(ALL): _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs = [c] hits = 0 try: for _ in range(100): out = torch.empty(seqlen,64,64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) _chunk_scan_fwd(cb, x, dt_, dA, C, states, cu, out, sidx, D=rn(64,64, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1)) hits += int((~torch.isfinite(out.float())).any().item()) except Exception as e: print(i, c.kwargs, c.num_warps, c.num_stages, "ERR", type(e).__name__); continue nbad += hits > 0 print(i, c.kwargs, "warps", c.num_warps, "stages", c.num_stages, "-> NaN in", hits, "/100 calls") print("configs producing NaN from finite inputs:", nbad, "of", len(ALL)) ```
| Tree | Runs | Last line, every run | |---|---|---| | `77154ca6116a` | 3 (1 in a source checkout, 2 in the nightly image for that commit) | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 8 of 23` | | this PR | 3 | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 0 of 12` | Before the fix, the NaN configs were 64/64/64 with 4 warps and 2 stages (NaN in 22 to 31 of 100 calls) and the seven configs with 4 warps and 4 stages (53 to 100 of 100). 128/256/64 with 8 warps and 3 stages raises `OutOfResources` at this shape. After the fix, each of the 12 configs left gave NaN in 0 of 100 calls. Tests: ``` python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py -k test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches -v ``` - With this PR: passed, 2 of 2 runs. - With the old config list: failed at 64/64/64, 4 warps, 2 stages, 2 of 2 runs. One run failed the finite check. The other failed the closeness check with `Greatest absolute difference: 1.7147041145625415e+38`, so the test compares outputs and does not only check `isfinite`. - Whole file `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` with this PR: `95 passed`. - `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files passes. I used `--noconftest` because the test environment did not have `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports. The new test uses only `monkeypatch`. In CI, the Buildkite step `kernels-mamba-test` runs `pytest -v -s kernels/mamba` on an H200 (sm90), so the new test runs on the affected architecture. Speed: `triton.testing.do_bench` on every config of the old list, NemotronH-like prefill shape (128 heads, headdim 64, 8 groups, dstate 128, chunk 128, bf16), on the H20-3e: | seqlen | Best of old list | Best of new list | Best config | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 | 62.2 us | 62.2 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | | 8192 | 425.4 us | 425.4 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | At seqlen 8192 the dropped configs took 481.7 to 1818.1 us. Not run: an end-to-end NemotronH server run (the issue's empty responses and `not JSON compliant: nan`). Only the kernel reproducer and the tests above were run. ## Details Root cause. In the K loop, `acc += tl.dot(cb, x)` uses `cb` built in registers (decay `exp`, `dt`, causal mask, cast to bf16). With whole warpgroups (`num_warps % 4 == 0`) and `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0`, Triton lowers this dot to wgmma with the A operand in registers. With `num_stages > 1`, Triton's `TritonGPUPipeline` pass splits the dot into async wgmmas and waits with `pendings = 1`. So the last wgmma of an iteration is still running when the loop jumps back. The next iteration loads the next `cb` tile into the same registers before it waits for that wgmma. The PTX ISA does not allow changes to the A registers of `wgmma.mma_async` before `wgmma.wait_group`. The running wgmma reads raw fp32 bits as bf16, which gives NaN, Inf and values near 3.4e38 in whole output rows. The race depends on timing, so the NaN rate changes by config and by run. The bug is in Triton's pipeliner, which vLLM cannot change. The vLLM part is that the autotune list offers configs that Triton compiles this way.
SASS of the K loop, 128/128/32 with 4 warps and 4 stages ``` /*58f0*/ LDS.128 R160, [R234] ; <- overwrites R160..R163 /*5b90*/ LDS.128 R156, [R234+0x1000] ; <- overwrites R156..R159 ... /*70a0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R88, R160, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R88 ; <- A = R160..R163 /*70b0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, R156, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R24, gsb0 ; <- A = R156..R159 /*71d0*/ WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1 ; <- leaves the 0x70a0/0x70b0 group running ... /*7720*/ @!P5 BRA 0x5750 ; ```
The fix. `_drop_racy_wgmma_configs` wraps the existing list. On CUDA sm90 it drops 11 of the 23 configs (old indices 2, 9, 10, 12, 13 to 19). - It keeps the 1-stage wgmma configs: Triton waits on them with `pendings = 0` right after the dot. It keeps the 2-warp and `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 32` configs: they use `mma.sync`, which is synchronous. - Only sm90 has wgmma, so other GPUs keep the full list. `is_cuda()` is needed because ROCm gfx90a also reports capability (9, 0). - The filter is a rule, not a list of configs that failed once. Configs 2, 10 and 12 have the same racy code but gave little or no NaN at the reproducer's shape (12 does not fit there). At dstate 256, config 10 gave NaN in 1 of 20 calls and config 12 in 20 of 20. A TTGIR check of all 23 old configs at dstate 128 and 256 found 0 mismatches between the rule and the racy pattern. - The filter runs when the list is built, not as `early_config_prune`. Triton skips pruning when the list has one config, and `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG` walks `self.configs` without pruning, so pruned configs could still run. - A TTGIR scan of the other Mamba2 SSD kernels (`_bmm_chunk_fwd`, `_chunk_state_fwd`, `_state_passing_fwd`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd`) found no register-A async wgmma, so only this kernel changes. Reading the diff: `ruff format` re-indents the config list because it is now a function argument. With whitespace hidden (`git diff -w`), the change in `ssd_chunk_scan.py` is about 25 lines. No config is added, removed or edited by hand. Limitations: this works around a Triton bug seen with Triton 3.6.0 (in the issue) and 3.7.1 (here). The new test does not check that non-sm90 platforms keep the full list. ---

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Require exact strides for moe_forward custom ops
author: ldkhang1201
body:
## Overview

Fixes #52308: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` outputs garbage under `torch.compile` with the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE backend. `--enforce-eager` works. The fix changes the tag on `vllm.moe_forward` and `vllm.moe_forward_shared` from `needs_fixed_stride_order` to `needs_exact_strides`.

This supersedes #52383, which I closed: it moved the pad inside the op based on a wrong diagnosis (CUDA-graph replay), and that approach would break the ROCm RMSNorm+pad fusion (#34636). #49092 (`.contiguous()` in `scaled_fp4_quant`) would be a complementary kernel-side safeguard.

## Claims

- GSM8K accuracy for Nemotron-3-Nano NVFP4 on TRTLLM MoE with default compile goes from ~0.01 back to eager parity.
- A new unit test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The change is two lines and touches no other code path.

## Validation

1x GB300, torch 2.14.0+cu132, default `vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, which selects the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM MoE backend. Evaluated with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` on all 1319 questions. Every compiled run used fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` and `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` directories (see the cache note in Details).

| Config | Completions, 5-shot, 256 tokens | Chat, thinking off, 1024 tokens, temp 0 |
|---|---|---|
| `--enforce-eager` | 0.303 | 0.882 |
| compile, main | 0.006 (46% invalid) | 0.008 (47% invalid) |
| compile, this PR | 0.299 | 0.890 |

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
    --max-tokens 1024 --temperature 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

Unit test: `pytest tests/quantization/test_trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_dim_padding.py -v` gives 5 passed. With the old tag, the new test fails with `[(2816, 1)] == [(2688, 1)]`.

The GPU runs used base commit 8a8e2baa02 with this exact patch. Between that commit and this branch's base, the only change under `fused_moe/` is `oracle/fp8.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Nemotron-3-Nano has hidden size 2688. The TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE pads it to 2816, and `MoERunner._maybe_pad_hidden_states` applies `F.pad` inside the compiled graph. Inductor fuses the preceding RMSNorm into the padded buffer. Because `needs_fixed_stride_order` only pins stride *order*, Inductor then passes `shared_experts_input` (the unpadded 2688-wide activations) to `moe_forward_shared` as a view into that buffer: `reinterpret_tensor(buf, (s, 2688), (2816, 1), 0)`. The shared expert's NVFP4 linear calls `scaled_fp4_quant`, whose kernel assumes packed rows. Row 0 is read correctly; every later row is read at the wrong offset. Eager mode never creates the alias. With this PR, the generated code passes a separate packed buffer.

**Why this tag.** `needs_fixed_stride_order` was a torch 2.6 workaround. It was already removed from the other MoE custom ops in #19346, #28974 and #33209; these two ops were missed. Since torch 2.8, `needs_exact_strides` has been the default for custom ops (pytorch/pytorch#148063, #150511), so this restores the default behavior.

**Tradeoff.** Inductor may now insert a copy when its preferred layout differs from eager, which in practice means one `(tokens, hidden)` copy per MoE layer when the hidden dim is padded. When no padding happens, inputs are already contiguous and nothing changes. The change adds no host sync. On ROCm, gpt-oss with the AITER RMSNorm+pad fusion uses `moe_forward` with the padded buffer itself, which is contiguous, so it is unaffected.

**Compile cache note.** Changing the op tag does not invalidate the Inductor FX graph cache or the vLLM AOT compile cache. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` does not bypass the Inductor cache either. A dev install at the same vLLM version may keep loading the old aliased graph until those caches are cleared. Release upgrades are unaffected because the vLLM version is part of the cache key.

**Scope and CI.**
- `needs_fixed_stride_order` still appears in `model_executor/layers/transformers/moe.py`, `models/utils.py` and `qwen3_dflash2.py`. I did not analyze those call sites and left them unchanged.
- The new test runs in the H200 Quantization job. It mocks the MoE layer with `Mock(spec=MoERunnerInterface)` because `get_layer_from_name` asserts that type, and checks only the stride the op receives, so the result is deterministic.
- No existing GSM8K CI config covers TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE with compile: the Nemotron NVFP4 configs in `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor/` use `--enforce-eager` or CUTLASS. I can add one as a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR uses `needs_exact_strides` or addresses this stride alias. #52383 (mine, now closed) and #49092 are discussed above. Open PRs #61179 and #61367 touch the same op registration for a different bug.

**AI assistance.** I used Claude Code to investigate, write the patch and test, and run the evaluations. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evals above.

title: [revert] [Build] Fix QuTLASS compilation with PyTorch 2.13
author: cleonard530
body:
## Overview This PR is to revert the changes in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58173, and to add a check to make sure this doesn't happen again. I believe what happened was that a local old version of QuTLASS, before it was migrated to the stable ABI, was being built against the new flags that help ensure QuTLASS stays stable. So I also added a check in here to make sure that a version of QuTLASS after this update is being used. This checks for the file `qutlass/csrc/include/registration.h` which was only added after the migration. cc @Harry-Chen @janeyx99 ## Validation **main branch:** [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/) vllm: **this branch** build succeeds and `[STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _qutlass_C.abi3.so (stable_shim=60, unstable=0) min-torch=2.11.0` Note: the drop in the number of stable_shim comes from internal implementation differences in torch/stable. Particularly the inclusions of `torch_exception_get_what`, `torch_exception_get_what_without_backtrace`, and `torch_new_stable_ivalue` in 2.13. ---

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix garbage/NaN lora_expand output on SM90 with fp32 i…
author: BeichenHuang
body:
## Overview Fixes #48590. On SM90, single-slice `lora_expand` with fp32 inputs (the real `add_lora_linear` path) returns garbage or NaN for rank ≥ 64. This PR forces `num_stages=1` for that path on SM90, which works around triton-lang/triton#9433. It also adds the missing fp32-input regression test. This is an alternative to #48638. ## Claims - Correct output for fp32-input `lora_expand` on SM90 at every rank and batch size we tested. End to end, Qwen3-8B with an r=64 LoRA goes from 2047/2047 NaN prompt logprobs to 0. - Expand kernel cost on single-slice layers is at most +8% (`add_inputs=False`) or +21% (`add_inputs=True`) on the worst shape (R=128, T=8192). Multi-slice layers are unchanged. For comparison, #48638 costs +106% on the same shape. - The workaround is applied after config selection, so it also covers configs from `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER`. - New test `test_lora_expand_fp32_inputs` covers the `CAST_TYPE` path, which no existing test exercises. ## Validation All runs on an H20-3e (SM90), torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0. ```bash pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k fp32_inputs # main: 8 failed / 28 passed -> this PR: 36 passed pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py # this PR: 4309 passed ``` The 8 failures on main are exactly `nslices=1 × rank∈{64,128} × {fp16,bf16} × 2 batch shapes`. They show up to 43% mismatched elements and a max abs diff of 3006. In CI, `tests/lora` runs on H200 MIG (SM90), so the new test exercises the fixed path there.
Minimal reproducer (kernel level) ```python import torch from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops import LoRAKernelMeta, lora_expand T, H, R = 1029, 4096, 64 x = torch.randn(1, T, R, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) # fp32, as in add_lora_linear B = (torch.randn(1, H, R, device="cuda") * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16) out = torch.zeros(T, H, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) meta = LoRAKernelMeta.make(max_loras=1, max_num_tokens=T, device="cuda") meta.prepare_tensors(torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")) lora_expand(x, [B], out, *meta.meta_args(T, False), offset_start=0, add_inputs=False) ref = x[0] @ B[0].float().T print("NaN:", out.isnan().sum().item(), "wrong:", ((out.float() - ref).abs() > 0.05).sum().item()) # H20, main: NaN: ~6000-9000, wrong: ~30k-450k (varies run to run). With bf16 x: 0 / 0. ```
End to end: Qwen3-8B with a random r=64 LoRA on all 7 projections, comparing 2048-token prompt logprobs against HF transformers + PEFT. | | NaN logprobs | mean \|Δ\| vs HF+PEFT | |---|---|---| | main | 2047 / 2047 | NaN | | #48638 (`block_n=32`) | 0 | 0.0185 | | this PR | 0 | 0.0177 | **Kernel latency vs #48638.** Single-slice expand, H=4096, fp32 input, median µs on H20, `add_inputs=True`: | R | T | main (wrong for R≥64) | #48638 | this PR | |---|---|---|---|---| | 16 | 2048 / 8192 | 26.2 / 82.7 | 35.0 / 141.0 | 26.3 / 82.6 | | 64 | 2048 / 8192 | 27.0 / 79.1 | 39.3 / 161.0 | 29.1 / 86.7 | | 128 | 2048 / 8192 | 34.7 / 101.8 | 52.7 / 210.1 | 39.5 / 122.9 | | 64 | 1 / 16 / 128 | 10.2 / 9.0 / 9.8 | 12.0 / 8.8 / 9.9 | 10.3 / 9.3 / 10.2 | At T=8192, #48638 is 1.7–2.1× slower than main, including R=16, which was never affected. This PR stays within 1.00–1.21×.
Multi-slice and add_inputs=False: before → after this PR `add_inputs=False`, before → after this PR, with 1/2/3 slices. Rows not shown are within ±3% for T≥512 and within 0.99–1.06× for T=16: ``` S R T | st2 us | st1 us | ratio 1 128 2048 | 31.8 | 34.4 | 1.08x 1 128 8192 | 97.9 | 106.1 | 1.08x 1 64 8192 | 69.6 | 69.1 | 0.99x 2 128 8192 | 439.5 | 438.6 | 1.00x 3 128 8192 | 653.2 | 655.4 | 1.00x ```
## Details **Root cause.** The fp32 → bf16 cast in-kernel (`CAST_TYPE`) makes the wgmma read its A operand from registers. With `num_stages=2`, Triton leaves the second wgmma of each iteration in flight across the loop back-edge. ptxas older than 13.3 then reuses that wgmma's A registers for the next iteration's shared-memory loads (triton-lang/triton#9433). Triton 3.5.0–3.8.0 all assemble SM90 kernels with an affected ptxas. To confirm, the unfixed kernel passes the new test when `TRITON_PTXAS_PATH` points at the ptxas 13.3 bundled with triton 3.8.0 (`ptxas-blackwell`). **Why `num_stages=1`.** With one stage, Triton waits for every wgmma within its own iteration, so no register-A wgmma stays in flight across iterations. That removes the hazard structurally, whatever the tile shape. `block_n=32` (#48638) only hides the hazard because ptxas happens to serialize the wgmmas for that shape. `block_n=64` with the same stages and warps still fails at R=128. **Scope.** The workaround applies only to CUDA SM90 with `CAST_TYPE`. Other GPUs (including ROCm, where `is_cuda()` is false) and bf16/fp16-input callers are unchanged. It covers all slice counts. The multi-slice default measured correct, but it runs the same pipelined register-A loop, and `num_stages=1` costs nothing there. **Removal.** This can be dropped once vLLM's Triton assembles SM90 kernels with ptxas ≥ 13.3. Triton main does that via triton-lang/triton#12035, expected in 3.9.0. **Not covered here.** `fused_moe_lora_op.py` does `tl.dot(a.to(tl.bfloat16), ...)` with `num_stages=3`. For fp16 MoE models, that cast is a real conversion and could hit the same bug. We haven't verified it, so it is left for a follow-up. ---

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix speculative warmup deadlock with pipeline parallelism
author: chenjr97
body:
## Overview

Fix a pipeline-parallel startup deadlock in MRV2 speculative decoding introduced by [#59260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59260).

## Claims

- Ensure all PP stages participate in the additional greedy warmup pass.
- Add regression coverage for matching warmup rounds across PP stages, with speculative decoding enabled and disabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```

- **34 passed** in 9.64 seconds. These suites are covered by the existing `V1 Executor + Worker` CI job.
- **GLM-4.7-Flash smoke test passed**: MRV2, TP=2, PP=2, BF16, MTP with one speculative token, JIT warmup and CUDA graphs enabled.
- Warmup completed and generation produced exactly **1,024 tokens** using `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=True`. Recorded 532 draft tokens and 492 accepted tokens; process exited successfully.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The model run validates startup and generation; no accuracy benchmark was performed.

## Details

Only the last PP stage owns a rejection sampler. Previously, the additional greedy warmup pass was gated on its presence, so earlier stages skipped the pass while the last stage waited for their activations.

Gate this pass on `speculative_config` instead, ensuring every PP stage executes matching forwards. The change is limited to the warmup condition and regression tests.

title: [MyPy][5/N] Fix mypy errors in hard tests/ dirs and enforce follow-imports=silent
author: adarshxs
body:
## Overview

Part 5 of enabling mypy on `tests/` (#49569). Fixes the mypy errors in the PR 5 directories and moves them from `SEPARATE_GROUPS` to `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so they are now checked with `--follow-imports silent` and cannot regress: `tests/entrypoints/llm`, `tests/entrypoints/openai`, `tests/kernels` (absorbing the previously listed `tests/kernels/{attention,core,helion,mamba,quantization}` and the separate `tests/kernels/moe`), `tests/lora`, `tests/tool_parsers`, `tests/v1/attention`, `tests/v1/e2e`, `tests/v1/ec_connector`.

Builds on #49570 (PR 0/1) and #51043 (PR 2). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these directories for mypy (checked `gh pr list --search "49569 in:body"` and `"mypy tests"`; the open `[MyPy]` PRs are #55485 (PR 4), #55542 (kv-A) and #55901 (kv-B)).

Partial #26533.

## Claims

- 533 mypy errors across the eight directories → 0, with `--warn-unused-ignores` also clean. (The issue's ~650 estimate predates #59428, which disabled `arg-type` and `assignment` under `tests/`.)
- Type-only: no `vllm/` changes, no `cast()`, no bare `# type: ignore`; the 29 ignores added are scoped to an error code and carry a reason (inline when the line fits in 88 columns, on the preceding line otherwise); 12 ignores that no longer suppressed anything are removed.
- 49 mock method assignments replaced with `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- Pre-existing test defects surfaced by the stricter check are fixed where safe, and flagged in a comment where fixing would change what the test exercises (list in Details).

## Validation

Environment: the pre-commit hook env (mypy 1.20.2, no torch/transformers so they resolve to `Any`), Python 3.11 like the hook.

```bash
# 1. the directories are clean at the strictness being enforced
.venv/bin/mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores \
    tests/entrypoints/llm tests/entrypoints/openai tests/kernels tests/lora \
    tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/attention tests/v1/e2e tests/v1/ec_connector
# Success: no issues found in 632 source files   (before: 533 errors in 111 files)

# 2. the hook as CI runs it, with the new grouping in effect
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
# passes; the only output is 3 darwin-only errors in vllm/ (posix_fadvise, MADV_HUGEPAGE)
# that exist on macOS before this change and do not appear on Linux CI

# 3. routing proof: each PR 5 directory now lands in the "" (silent) group
.venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/pre_commit'); import mypy; \
  print([k for k,v in mypy.group_files(['tests/lora/utils.py']).items() if v])"
# ['']   (same for a file in each of the other seven directories; tests/v1/core still prints ['tests/v1/core'])

# 4. all other hooks on the changed files
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main)
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, ... all pass
```

Test runs (macOS CPU build of vLLM, so only CPU-runnable suites; everything else collected only):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest --collect-only` on all 116 changed test files | 8316 tests collected; 6 collection errors, all missing optional deps on macOS (triton-cpu, tilelang, datasets), none from this change |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/{chat_completion/test_chat_error,completion/test_completion_error,completion/test_completion_text_offset,responses/test_function_call_parsing,responses/test_response_input_to_harmony,responses/test_responses_utils,responses/test_serving_responses,test_render_parity,test_tool_choice_content_none}.py` | 243 passed, 1 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_*.py` (14 changed files) | 528 passed, 1 skipped, 19 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit tests/v1/attention` (3 pre-existing non-collecting files ignored) | 984 passed, 1150 skipped, 214 failed + 16 errors; the identical set of 230 ids fails on unchanged `main` in the same environment (CUDA/ROCm-only tests, `/dev/shm`, NIXL), so none is from this change |

No model evaluation: the change does not touch `vllm/` and cannot affect output, accuracy or serving.

## Details

Most fixes follow the issue's recipe: `assert x is not None` before an `X | None` access, `assert isinstance(...)` to narrow a union or an abstract base to the concrete class the test builds, annotations on fixtures and helpers, and `monkeypatch.setattr` instead of assigning to a method. Scoped ignores remain only where a test stub intentionally does not satisfy the real interface (`misc` for `None` fallbacks of optional kernel classes and a `Final` attribute, `attr-defined` for `SimpleNamespace` stubs, `type-abstract` where a test instantiates an abstract class through a factory).

Pre-existing defects the stricter check surfaced (all in tests; none changes what a test exercises):

- `tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py`: `StructuredOutputsParams(backend=...)` has no such init field (`_backend` is `init=False`), so the call raised `TypeError`; the kwarg is removed and the helper no longer takes a backend.
- `tests/lora/utils.py`: `DummyLoRAManager.init_lora` passed `embeddings_tensor=` to `LoRALayerWeights(...)`, which no longer accepts it.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_{internlm2,longcat,phi4mini}_tool_parser.py`: `tokenizer.get_vocab = MagicMock()` permanently mutated the module-scoped tokenizer fixture and leaked into later tests; now `monkeypatch.setattr`, undone per test.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`: assignments to a non-existent `FusedMoEParallelConfig.use_dp` removed; the no-DP state already comes from `make_no_parallel()`.
- `tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/{mk_objects,common,cli_args}.py`: registries and `Config` fields were annotated as holding instances although they hold classes; now `type[...]` of the Modular subclasses that are actually registered.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py`: the mock prefill backends' `run_prefill_new_tokens` / `run_prefill_context_chunk` did not match the ABC (`chunk_idx` vs `chunk`, missing `out` / `output_scale`).
- `tests/v1/attention/utils.py`: `try_get_attention_backend` was annotated `type[AttentionImpl]` but `get_impl_cls()` returns `type[AttentionImplBase]`; and the `add_mock_model_methods` block is removed: its `get_num_layers` mock shadowed the real method with the wrong arity, the three `*_for_layer` hooks no longer exist on `ModelConfig`, nothing reads any of them, and no caller passed the flag.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py`: `query_len_support` is a `ClassVar` and was assigned through an instance; the assignment is removed (the inherited default is the value it set).
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`: `get_fake_sample_fn` was annotated `-> SamplerOutput` although it returns a callable.
- `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_metadata.py`: asserted load entries as `(transfer_id, block_ids)` pairs; the metadata carries `(transfer_id, block_ids, shape)` and the worker unpacks three values, so the test is updated to the real contract.

Deliberately not changed, flagged with a comment and a scoped ignore:

- `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`: the int8 non-block branch of `moe_quantize_weights_2d` calls `ops.scaled_int8_quant(w, w_s, use_per_token_if_dynamic=...)`, but the signature is now `(input, scale, azp, symmetric) -> (q, scale, azp)`, so it would raise if reached. No test reaches it (every int8 caller uses block quant and the modular-kernel CLI only accepts fp8); a replacement needs a GPU to validate, so it is left for a follow-up.

Typing gaps in `vllm/` that the per-test fixes keep running into, left for follow-ups:

- four identical `type-abstract` ignores: `select_common_block_size` / `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` take `type[AttentionBackend]`, but the indexer backends leave `get_impl_cls` abstract;

`MockMLAAttentionLayer.forward_impl` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` keeps a scoped `override` ignore because the replica deliberately takes only the arguments the test passes; the prefill-registry mocks above were aligned to their ABC instead because they are registered as real backends.

The hook change is routing only: the absorbed `tests/kernels/*` entries become redundant under the `tests/kernels` parent entry and are removed, mirroring what #51043 did for `tests/plugins_tests`.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align speculator hidden norm in GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE and GLM-OCR MTP with GLM5Next to recycle post-final-hidden.
author: spandantiwari
body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimal change; mirrors the existing #47448 / `glm5next` pattern exactly.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real-object drafter test and an e2e test on both model runners (GLM-OCR) in CI; acceptance validated out-of-CI on GLM-4.5-Air (checkpoint too large for CI).
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wrong output of the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion on ROCM_ATTN
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Purpose

On `ROCM_ATTN`, the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion (`fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache`) stores V in an interleaved layout, and the layer's attention kernels must read it that way. Two places break that contract, so the fusion produces wrong output on `main`:

1. **Qwen3 models decode garbage** (Qwen3-8B GSM8K 0.87 → 0.005). `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` calls `set_interleaved_v_cache()` on each eligible layer, but with `layer_name` hoisted (`_USE_LAYERNAME`, torch >= 2.11) one layer's patterns cover the model, so the loop `break`s after the first eligible layer and skips the call for every other one. Those layers keep `_use_interleaved_v_cache=False`: the fused kernel then writes the NHD layout into a cache their kernels read as the paged layout. Prefill looks right because it attends over the fused kernel's `k_out`; every decode step after it reads the cache. The existing fusion tests use a single attention layer, so they never reached the second layer.
2. **With `fuse_rope_kvcache` also on, models without QK-norm get a corrupted V cache** (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.766 → 0.71). The pass switches layers to the interleaved V cache before any pattern matches. On a layer the QK-norm pattern does not match, the RoPE + KV-cache fusion writes the KV cache instead, through `RocmAttentionImpl.do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, whose Triton writer (`rocm_aiter_ops.triton_rope_and_cache`) only stores the regular V layout. A per-layer check at pattern registration cannot keep such layers out, because with `layer_name` hoisted one pattern serves every layer and graphs loaded from the compile cache skip the passes.

Fixing the first alone makes the second hit every layer instead of one (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.012), so both are fixed here, one commit each:

1. `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` switches every eligible layer and only skips the duplicate pattern registration.
2. `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` applies RoPE in place (`ops.rotary_embedding`) and takes the unfused `do_kv_cache_update`, which already writes the interleaved layout, on layers that use the interleaved V cache. Layers with the regular V cache keep the fused Triton writer.

Only `ROCM_ATTN` is affected; `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` is off by default.

## Test Plan

Single MI300-series GPU (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `ROCM_ATTN`, TP1. The change is on `main` @ `6af1e0ae27`; it was exercised on a source build of `main` @ `5be4266f5c` with the touched files replaced (they and the pass manager are unchanged between the two).

- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`
- `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0` against `vllm serve <model> -cc.pass_config.fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache=true [-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=true] -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=true`
- Speed: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(16, 4*C)`, median TPOT, two rounds per arm in the order PR, base, PR, base.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** 1497 and 50 passed (24 skipped). Two new cases fail on `main` and pass here:

- `test_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion_interleaves_every_layer` builds three `ROCM_ATTN` layers and checks that all of them switch.
- `test_rope_kvcache_fusion` gains an `interleaved_v` case that compares the fused and unfused caches of an interleaved-V `ROCM_ATTN` layer; its bf16 variants fail on `main`. (With an fp8 cache and `block_size=16` the two V layouts coincide, so those pass either way.)

**Root cause of the first bug, confirmed at runtime** on Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers): on `main`, `set_interleaved_v_cache()` ran for one layer; that layer's fused writes used `use_shuffle_layout=True` and the other 27 layers' used `False`. The fused writer and the unfused interleaved writer produce byte-identical caches, and the decode and prefill kernels read the interleaved layout correctly, so only the flag was missing.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions unless noted):

| Model | Fusions on | `main` | This PR | Fusions off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm | 0.005 (200 questions) | 0.871 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm + RoPE | — | 0.876 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | QK-norm + RoPE | 0.718 / 0.706 | 0.757 | 0.766 / 0.763 |

The QK-norm pass replaces all 36 patterns of Qwen3-8B in both arms. With only the first commit, the Llama row drops to 0.012.

**Speed, Qwen3-8B.** QK-norm fusion on with this PR, versus stock `main` without the fusion. On the fusion arm `splitting_ops` is limited to the attention ops and the `rotary_embedding` CustomOp is dispatched, which keeps the request from being dropped without turning on Inductor graph partition; the RoPE + KV-cache fusion is also on there but does not match Qwen3. Mean of two rounds:

| Concurrency | `main` (ms) | With fusion (ms) | TPOT | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.886 | 4.650 | **−4.8%** | +5.2% |
| 8 | 6.552 | 6.275 | **−4.2%** | +4.4% |
| 32 | 8.983 | 8.715 | −3.0% | +2.6% |
| 64 | 11.576 | 11.368 | −1.8% | +2.5% |
| 128 | 17.554 | 17.206 | −2.0% | +4.2% |

GSM8K in that setup: 0.876 / 0.876.

On interleaved-V layers the RoPE + KV-cache fusion now runs as two kernels instead of one. A fused write of the interleaved layout needs the Triton RoPE + cache kernel to support it, which is an AITER change.

---
