title: [Bugfix][Parser] DeepSeek V4.1: don't leak a `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` opener into content
author: YaashuDave
body:
## Overview

The `deepseek_v41` parser now accepts `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` (V4's wrapper name, V4.1's spacing) as a tool-call opener, so it no longer leaks into `content`. Part of #62051 (the "V4 spelling" row); the other rows are not changed here.

## Claims

- For V4.1 output whose tool block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the opener no longer appears in `content`, in both streaming and non-streaming. The tool calls are parsed as before.
- Like the canonical `<｜DSML｜ calls>`, this opener also ends an open reasoning block.
- No change for the canonical spelling, the unspaced V4 spelling, or truncated calls.

## Validation

The table uses the inputs from #62051, run through `DeepSeekV41EngineToolParser` on CPU (non-streaming, and streaming one character at a time followed by `finish_streaming()`):

| Model output | main @ `bde4d00113` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n<｜DSML｜ invoke name="WebFetch">…</｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` | call `WebFetch {"url": "https://x.com"}`, but `content` = `"\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n"` | same call; the opener is not in `content` |
| Well-formed `<｜DSML｜ calls>` block | call parsed, `content` = `"Hi\n\n"` | unchanged |
| Unspaced V4 block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>…`) | returned as text, no call | unchanged |
| Truncated value / truncated name / block without an invoke | as described in #62051 | unchanged (rows 2-3 are #62259) |

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py
```

- New `test_v4_wrapper_name_opens_tool_block` (streaming at chunk sizes 1/7/10000, plus non-streaming, thinking on and off) and `test_v4_wrapper_name_ends_reasoning`. All 7 cases fail on main and pass with this change.
- All 147 tests in the three DeepSeek parser test files pass.
- `tests/parser` and `tests/tool_parsers`: 8064 passed vs. 8057 on main (the 7 new tests). Both have the same 15 errors, all in `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py`, which needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Validated with parser-level tests on CPU only; I did not serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The change is limited to the parser config, and these tests run in CI under the existing `parser` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

**Root cause:** `deepseek_v41_config` replaces V4's `TOOL_START` (canonical spelling plus `DSML_TOOL_START_VARIANTS`) with the single string `<｜DSML｜ calls>`. When the block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the V4.1 invoke that follows still matches through the existing `(CONTENT, INVOKE_PREFIX)` transition, so the call is parsed. The opener before it, however, stays in `CONTENT` and is emitted as text.

**Fix:** add it as a `TOOL_START` variant in `deepseek_v41.py`, the same way #56141 added misspelled wrappers to the V4 config. `token_id_terminals` is unchanged: in the V4.1 tokenizer only `｜DSML｜` is an added token (non-special), so the tags reach the parser as text.

**Notes for reviewers:**

- A prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` now behaves like a prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ calls>`: it opens a tool block. This matches what #56141 accepted for the V4 variants.
- **Open question (the "unspaced V4 spelling" row of #62051):** a fully V4-spelled block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`, `<｜DSML｜invoke …>`) is still returned as text. That matches the Rust frontend, which keeps V4 tags as text in the V4.1 dialect on purpose (`v4_tags_remain_text_in_v41_dialect`, #56208). If V4.1 should accept V4 spellings, I can do that in both frontends in a follow-up.
- **Rust frontend:** it parses invokes only inside a recognised block, so it returns this whole block as text, and this PR doesn't change that. I can align it in a follow-up if you'd like.
- Related: #62259 (truncation rows of #62051) touches other parts of the same file. #61142 (another V4.1 opener drift) edits the same config; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Kimi-K2.6 int4 MoE prefill regression on Triton 3.8 (gfx950 tuned config)
author: afriedri
body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K2.6 (int4 W4A16, TP8) prefill regressed between v0.29 and v0.31 on MI350/MI355: c32 TTFT went up ~150%. The cause is a Triton 3.7.1 → 3.8.0 codegen regression in `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` for one tile, which the tuned config uses for its `"8192"` entry (every batch from ~6k tokens up): BLOCK 256×256×32, 8 warps, 2 stages, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=32`. On Triton 3.8 that tile is 3–8x slower; the same tile with 1 stage, or with BLOCK_N 128, is fine.

This PR changes that entry to BLOCK_N 128 and `num_stages=1` in the four identical `E=384,N=256,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI35*,dtype=int4_w4a16.json` files. Nothing else changes: only Kimi-K2-family int4 checkpoints at TP8 on MI350/MI355 load these files, and only batches of ~6k+ tokens use this entry.

## Test Result

Kernel (Kimi-K2.6 TP8 shapes, w13 + w2 summed over M=8192 and 16384, Triton 3.8.0):

| `"8192"` entry | µs |
| --- | ---: |
| current (256×256×32, 8 warps, 2 stages) | 44180 |
| 256×256×32, 8 warps, **1 stage** | 7677 |
| 256×**128**×32, 8 warps, 2 stages | 7631 |
| **this PR** (256×128×32, 8 warps, 1 stage) | 6129 |

Serving (change vs. current table):

| conc | TTFT (before → after) | TPOT | E2EL | tok/s |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 118 → 117 ms (−0.9%) | +1.8% | +1.8% | −1.7% |
| 32 | 1981 → 829 ms (−58%) | −1.5% | −5.8% | +6.2% |

c1 doesn't reach the `"8192"` entry; its TPOT difference comes from one restart (20.93 vs 21.92 ms) and is run-to-run noise.

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the analysis, the config search and drafting. All changes reviewed.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for structurally-corrupted PNG images
author: reda-maizate
body:
## Overview

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` now catches Pillow's `SyntaxError` ("broken PNG file"), so a request containing a structurally-corrupted PNG fails with HTTP 400 instead of an unhandled HTTP 500.

Fixes #62703. Related: #60303 / #60308 cover the sibling `DecompressionBombError` case in the same except clause; this change covers the `SyntaxError` case, which that PR does not address.

## Claims

- A chat completion containing a corrupt PNG returns **HTTP 400** `BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk ...)` instead of **HTTP 500** `InternalServerError` with the raw Pillow message.
- No behavior change for valid images, or for corrupt inputs already handled by the `OSError` / `UnidentifiedImageError` branches (they keep returning the same 400s).

## Validation

**Unit test** (real-world reproducer bytes — a 79-byte PNG whose stray bytes between the IDAT CRC and IEND shift the chunk stream):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -v
# => 20 passed (incl. new test_image_broken_png_rejected)
```

**End-to-end A/B on a real deployment** — `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`df3bd094a`), single H100, `google/gemma-4-26b-A4B-it`; "patched" = same container with this branch's `image.py` overlayed (byte-identical base verified before overlay):

| Request | Nightly (before) | This branch (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Corrupt PNG (reproducer above) | `500 InternalServerError: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` |
| Valid 64×64 PNG | `200` (answers "Red") | `200` (answers "Red") |
| Random non-image bytes | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: cannot identify image file` | `400` (unchanged) |

CI coverage: `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` runs in the premerge CPU job (`pytest -m cpu_test multimodal` in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), which is triggered by both changed paths (`vllm/multimodal/`, `tests/multimodal`).

## Details

**Root cause:** `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` wraps decode failures in a client-facing `ValueError` (`"Failed to load image: ..."`), but its except clause only catches `(OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)`. Pillow raises a plain `SyntaxError` for corrupted chunk structures — it is neither of those — so it escaped unwrapped. The request-level error mapper (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`) promotes `ValueError` to `BadRequestError` (400) but maps unmapped exceptions to `InternalServerError` (500), which is exactly what clients observed.

**Fix:** add `SyntaxError` to the existing except tuple. The wrapping pattern — and therefore the 400 path — already existed and is proven by the A/B table above. A genuine Python `SyntaxError` cannot occur inside this try block (it only calls Pillow and plain attribute reads), so the widened catch cannot mask unrelated failures.

**Not a duplicate:** #60308 (open) adds `DecompressionBombError` to the same clause but does not handle `SyntaxError`; searches of open issues/PRs for "broken PNG" return no results. The two changes compose trivially if both merge.

**Model evaluations:** not applicable — the change only affects how invalid client input is surfaced (HTTP status/message of the error path); it cannot alter model output for accepted requests.

**AI assistance:** this change was prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3 via OpenCode) under the direction of, and fully reviewed line-by-line by, the human submitter, who ran all tests and end-to-end validations above.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DP NUMA affinity regression
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Overview

Fix CPU data-parallel ranks all binding to the same NUMA node, a regression from #45026. Fixes #47328.

## Claims

- With `--data-parallel-size N` on a multi-NUMA CPU host, each `EngineCore_DP*` now binds the cores and memory of its own NUMA node instead of every rank binding the same cores.
- Manual pinning with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES` without DP is unchanged.
- No change to shared engine code; the fix is CPU-only (26 lines added, 10 removed, excluding tests).

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, on a 6-NUMA-node host:

```bash
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --data-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 256
```

OpenMP binding chosen by each EngineCore at startup (from the `OpenMP thread binding info` log):

| | `EngineCore_DP0` | `EngineCore_DP1` |
|---|---|---|
| main | cores 192-222, reserved 223 | cores 192-222, reserved 223 (same) |
| this PR | cores 192-222 (node 0), reserved 223 | cores 224-254 (node 1), reserved 255 |

With this PR the two workers also bind memory to distinct NUMA nodes (`NUMA binding: Using MEMBIND policy ... nodes (0)` and `(1)`), and a completion request returns a correct response end to end.

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py   # 21 passed
```

`test_omp_manager_binds_each_dp_rank_to_its_assigned_node` builds `OMPProcessManager` on a fake 2-node topology and checks that two DP ranks get disjoint cores. It fails (both ranks pick node 0 cores) if the assigned ids are ignored.

## Details

**Root cause.** #45026 moved the per-DP-rank device list from the device-control env var into `parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`. `CoreEngineProcManager` still computes each rank's shard and stores it there, and GPU/XPU consume it. The CPU code still read only `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, which nothing sets per rank anymore. `OMPProcessManager`, which runs in the EngineCore process, then saw the full node list and picked `allowed_numa_nodes[local_rank]`, the same node for every DP rank.

**Fix.** `get_visible_memory_node()` takes an optional `assigned_node_ids`. Precedence is assigned ids, then `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, then all nodes. `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA` still overrides everything. Three call sites pass the ids:

- `OMPProcessManager` reads the config. The in-process `get_assigned_physical_gpu_ids()` global is only set inside worker processes, so it is not available in the EngineCore process where this runs.
- `CPUWorker` reads `vllm_config.parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`.
- `CpuPlatform.get_current_memory_usage` runs in the worker and uses the global.

**Limitations.** `--device-ids` also fills `assigned_physical_gpu_ids`, so on CPU it now selects NUMA nodes (composed with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`), consistent with GPU. This path is not covered by the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization][Spec Decode] Load ModelOpt mixed-precision DFlash and DSpark drafts
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix loading of nested ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints, quantization
settings for DFlash/DSpark drafts, and per-tensor FP8 normalization on FNUZ GPUs.
This incorporates the parser fix from the
earlier closed, unmerged [PR #36312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36312)
and adds draft-layer name mapping, regression tests, CI coverage and documentation.

## Claims

- Nested `MIXED_PRECISION` metadata selects the existing `modelopt_mixed` backend.
- ModelOpt draft settings match the weight aliases, runtime module prefix and
  decoder layer offset before quantized layers are constructed.
- Per-tensor FP8 weights and static input scales are normalized for FNUZ GPUs
  such as AMD MI300, using the existing conversion helper.
- Other quantization backends retain their existing quantization-config handling.
  No FP8 kernel changes are needed.

## Validation

The current source passes 24 focused CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit,
including mypy and CI selection. CPU checks used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and
Transformers 5.17.0; current main pins Torch 2.14.0.

AMD CI exposed an existing per-tensor FP8 loader omission: both checkpoint
regressions failed during engine initialization at `input.dtype == weight.dtype`
in [MI300 quantization CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96958#01a16a9a-8a0e-4f38-8027-3356b1307ef8).
The loader retained FN weights while the activation quantizer selected FNUZ.
The fix applies the existing FN-to-FNUZ normalization before requantization,
including both weight and static input scales. The existing regressions now
require the exact platform dtype and input scale. Fresh AMD validation is
pending CI. A CPU check confirmed the conversion preserves dequantized weights, including
negative zero, while doubling both scales.

GPU validation below used vLLM 0.32.0 with the source fixes backported. The
checkpoint-loading regressions are retained, with shared fixture setup and
the existing speculative-metric reader. GPU tests were not rerun for this
cleanup; the full current-main environment and full suites remain untested.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native/legacy mixed config, uppercase/lowercase | Four mixed-config failures; NVFP4 control passes | All five cases pass |
| Draft mapping, aliases, offsets and Quark preservation | Missing runtime-name mapping | 17 CPU cases pass against real quantization configurations |
| Small mixed Llama checkpoint through `LLM` | Config conversion fails | Loads actual FP8/BF16 layers; nested/flat metadata produce identical completions |
| Small mixed DSpark checkpoint through `LLM` | Missing `fc.weight_scale` parameter | Mixed FP8 `fc`, Markov and offset decoder projections; positive proposals and exact OFF/ON token equality |

Observed errors before the respective fixes:

```text
Value error, Unknown ModelOpt quant algo: MIXED_PRECISION

ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in Qwen3DSparkModel. The available parameters belonging to fc (ReplicatedLinear) are: {'fc.weight'}
```

The small GPU regressions create random checkpoints and integer token prompts
locally. Exact comparisons use batch invariance. CI dependencies and the
rendered ModelOpt documentation are updated. Changed-file pre-commit checks
pass, including mypy and CI test selection.

Additional GPT-OSS-20B mixed-FP8 DSpark smoke on B200, TP=1, fixed K=2:

- All 1,120 output tokens across 35 prompts match SpecDec OFF.
- 2,140 tokens were proposed and 16 accepted with normal verification.
- Runtime inspection confirms per-channel weight and per-token activation FP8
  for `fc`, and per-tensor FP8 for the Markov output projection.
- Export files are unchanged.

The GPT-OSS draft was trained for eight optimizer updates and quantized with
synthetic calibration inputs. These are functional smoke results, not a held-out
quality evaluation or a speedup measurement. Other hardware, tensor-parallel
sizes and quantization formats were not tested.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands</summary>

Repository test entrypoints:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k modelopt -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'draft_quant_config or draft_weight_aliases' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'nested_mixed_checkpoint or mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -v
```

Earlier GPU execution used the vLLM 0.32 compatibility setup described above.
The regression bodies at that point ran with the real stock test fixture:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
  -v -s test_gpu_regression.py
```

Each GPU regression passes after its fix and fails before it with the error
shown above. Current-main GPU execution remains pending.

</details>

## Details

There are two failures. Config conversion rejects nested `MIXED_PRECISION`
metadata before the existing backend can load it. After that is fixed, the
draft loader looks up per-layer settings using runtime names such as `model.fc`,
while the checkpoint names the layer `fc`. It builds an unquantized projection
and then fails to load `fc.weight_scale`.

The shared `map_draft_quant_config` helper in `models/utils.py` maps ModelOpt's
draft settings through the existing weight aliases, module prefix and decoder
layer offset before constructing the layers. Apply this
only to ModelOpt: other backends can use semantic configuration keys or suffix
rules that must not receive a module prefix.

Related work has different scope: [#49900](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49900)
handles `draft_model.` prefixes in another proposer path;
[#53122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53122) configures draft
quantization aliases and context-KV projection, without this runtime-root and
teacher-layer remapping. No equivalent open PR was found.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix cooperative_topk illegal memory access on NaN scores
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

Since #59645, `cooperative_topk` crashes with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` when a row of 64K columns or more contains more NaNs than `top_k` (e.g. 1% of a 256K row, or a fully-NaN row). NaN scores can reach decode top-k during warmup and CUDA-graph capture, where the indexer reads uninitialized KV blocks (see the note in `candidate_blocks.py`). Before #59645 such rows produced garbage indices; now they take down the process.

**Root cause.** nvcc compiles the integer expression `bits | 0x80000000u` in `convert_to_uint32_v2` as the FP operation `-|x|`:

```
ISETP.GE.AND P0, PT, R2, RZ        // bits >= 0 ?
FADD R10, -|R2|, -RZ               // "bits | 0x80000000u" emitted as -|x|
@P0 IMAD.MOV.U32 R9, RZ, RZ, R10
```

That is bit-exact for finite values and ±inf, but FADD canonicalizes NaN to `0x7FFFFFFF`, which is the ordered key of -0.0. The FP16 coarse bins put NaN above +inf (bin 1023), so the two orderings disagree. When NaNs overflow the threshold bin, the exact recovery takes the single-key path with a -0.0 pivot. Every positive score then counts as "above" it, and the unchecked append in `collect_exact_candidates` writes past `s_topk` (compute-sanitizer: invalid `__shared__` write in `unbounded_round0_single_key`).

**Fix.** Read the bits through an opaque `mov.b32`, so the key stays bit-exact and NaN orders above +inf in both the coarse and exact keys, matching `torch.topk`.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix the test_qwen.py failure when AITER is on
author: qli88
body:
## Overview

models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py fails when AITER is on. The cause is AITER's RMSNorm has different implementation compared with HF version, and the inductor generates different fused kernels when AITER is on. More important, the results are so sensitive to those small diffs is because the ppl calculation is not accurate. Those prompt tokens outside the reference answer --- the system prompt, the question and the chat-template markup --- those tokens are nearly unpredictable, so their log-probs sit in the softmax tail, where tiny numerical differences move them a lot. They made up 20%+ of the scored tokens but about two-thirds of the total loss, and those are just numerical noises. As a fix, I updated the PPL calculation based on only answer tokens, and reference PPL is also updated accordingly.

Also, the other file, test_glm.py, is also updated with the new calculation.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-request draft retention for structured output under PP

body:

Revert https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442, which introduces a performance regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs, and re-fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54437 by addressing the root cause in `DraftTokensHandler`.

```
140 passed, 3 skipped, 19 warnings
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on H100 80GB.

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- 95% confidence intervals in brackets

No regression on PP=1

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 673.6 [668.3, 678.9] | 675.7 [666.5, 684.9] | +0.32%
broad / c96 | 9,835.7 [9,749.2, 9,922.2] | 9,785.8 [9,690.9, 9,880.7] | −0.51%
tight / c1 | 1,057.8 [1,047.7, 1,067.9] | 1,062.4 [1,051.7, 1,073.1] | +0.43%
tight / c96 | 18,582.1 [18,469.9, 18,694.3] | 18,565.3 [18,389.4, 18,741.2] | −0.09%

</body></html>

Recover performance regression on PP=2

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 661.45 [660.82, 662.08] | 662.79 [662.39, 663.19] | +0.20%
broad / c96 | 3,951.12 [3,822.93, 4,079.30] | 12,038.09 [11,768.25, 12,307.93] | +204.68%
tight / c1 | 1,021.45 [1,020.70, 1,022.19] | 1,024.63 [1,023.00, 1,026.26] | +0.31%
tight / c96 | 3,865.53 [3,771.94, 3,959.13] | 21,029.32 [20,574.89, 21,483.75] | +444.02%

</body></html>

## Details

### Background

`DraftTokensHandler` allows workers to asynchronously send draft tokens back to the scheduler / structured output manager for processing.

With async scheduling, it works roughly like:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
--------------------------------------------------
schedule step N
sample step N
                                        execute step N
schedule step N+1
wait for step N
                                        sample step N
                                        DraftTokensHandler.set_draft_tokens
                                        execute step N+1
DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens
generate sampling bitmasks
sample step N+1
                                        sample step N+1
...
```

On main, `DraftTokensHandler` holds the latest batch set by the worker. This works fine for PP=1, but when PP>=2, this can occur:
```
Scheduler-side          Worker-side
----------------------------------
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch A)
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch B)
get_draft_tokens
```

Micro-batch B replaces micro-batch A in the handler. Scheduler-side cannot recover A's drafts and generates incorrect grammar bitmasks, leading to #54437.

#54442 fixes this by effectively truncating the worker-side draft sequence, reducing acceptance length.

This PR fixes this by making `DraftTokensHandler` track draft tokens by request ID. So micro-batch B cannot override micro-batch A.

Final notes:
- Suggest reviewing commits independently
  - `e3595db629d88881e74eafc357e471924b4d9c1f`: revert #54442, could be a separate PR
  - `c67afdec130ca06c6beb5e286a5b83b91fdae3a2`: track draft tokens by request ID.
  - `bb3694db86066ea2d272051b0495bad3ae09d026`: E2E repro
- Alternative #61348 includes adding a debug flag to catch the handoff race, this is not included in this PR in favor of the E2E repro.

title: [Bugfix][NVFP4] Fix NaN logits and garbage output from uninitialized fused act+quant scales
author: nv-nikitaj
body:
## Overview

Make the fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel initialize the padded entries of the swizzled NVFP4 block-scale buffer, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` kernel already does. Fixes a regression from #53568, which switched the scale allocator to `torch.empty` (previously `torch.zeros`, restored in #45739).

## Claims

- Fixes NaN logits and garbage output (`other other other ...`) on NVFP4 checkpoints, e.g. `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`.
- Fixes HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan` on `/v1/chat/completions` with `logprobs`.
- Covers both users of the kernel (the `ActivationQuantFusionPass` and the manual fusion in `fused_act_quant.py`) with no allocator memset.

## Validation

Setup: 8x RTX PRO 4500 (sm120), TP=8, `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`, FlashInfer-Cutlass NVFP4 linear backend, `fuse_act_quant: True`, built from source with CUDA 13.2.

Repro:

```bash
# 1. Serve (TP=8)
vllm serve nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --served-model-name nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 --port 8000

# 2. Once the server is up, send 100 chat+logprobs and 100 completions requests
NAME=nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5
echo -n "chat:  "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_chat_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"logprobs\":true,\"top_logprobs\":1,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful assistant.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello!\"}],\"max_tokens\":100}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo -n "compl: "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_compl_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"prompt\":\"What is the test plan?\",\"logprobs\":2,\"max_tokens\":50,\"temperature\":0}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo "nan-errors: $(grep -l 'Out of range float' /tmp/r_*.json | wc -l)"
```

Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`, 20 passed (12 existing, 8 new).

## Details

The fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel only wrote valid rows of the swizzled block-scale buffer, but the NVFP4 GEMM reads the padded entries, so since #53568 switched the allocator to `torch.empty` it consumed stale memory as scales and produced NaN logits. This PR makes the kernel zero the padded scale rows and columns itself (as `scaled_fp4_quant` does) and keeps the allocators as `torch.empty`, so there is no extra memset.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for corrupt AVIF and BLP images
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Inspired by #62703. A chat request with a corrupt AVIF image gets HTTP 500, and one with bad BLP data gets HTTP 501, instead of 400. `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` turns only `OSError`, `UnidentifiedImageError` and `SyntaxError` into the `ValueError("Failed to load image: ...")` that becomes a 400. Pillow's AVIF decoder raises `RuntimeError`, and the BLP plugin raises `BLPFormatError`, a `NotImplementedError`, so both get past that `except`. This PR adds `RuntimeError` to it, which covers both.

#62704 fixed the case from #62703, a PNG with a broken chunk (`SyntaxError`), by adding one class to the same tuple. This PR follows the same approach for the decoder errors that it does not cover. An image over Pillow's pixel limit (`DecompressionBombError`) has the same cause, but #60308 fixes it, so this PR does not touch it.

## Claims

- A corrupt AVIF (`RuntimeError: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item`) now gives HTTP 400 `Failed to load image: ...`, not 500.
- A BLP file with an unknown compression (`BLPFormatError: Unknown BLP compression 0`) now gives HTTP 400, not 501.
- Any `NotImplementedError` or `RecursionError` raised while decoding (both subclass `RuntimeError`) now also gives 400 instead of 501/500. These come from the input image, so 400 is intended.
- Valid PNG, JPEG, WEBP and AVIF images load as before. vLLM's own `ValueError`s in this block (pixel limit, decoded-size budget) are not affected.
- A new parametrized test in `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` covers both cases and checks the wrapped cause.

## Validation

Setup: CPU only. vLLM at upstream `main` `debcf2284`, Pillow 13.0.0, Python 3.12.

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py
```

With the patch, 22 passed. With the old `image.py`, the two new cases fail with `RuntimeError: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item` and `BLPFormatError: Unknown BLP compression 0`, and the 20 other tests pass.

HTTP status: I passed each input to `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` and gave the escaping exception to the real `create_error_response`:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| AVIF with no primary item | `RuntimeError` -> 500 | 400 `Failed to load image: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item` |
| BLP2 with compression 0 | `BLPFormatError` -> 501 | 400 `Failed to load image: Unknown BLP compression 0` |
| PNG with a broken chunk (#62703) | 400 | 400 |
| PNG with a 20000x10000 header | `DecompressionBombError` -> 500 | 500, fixed by #60308 |
| Valid PNG, JPEG, WEBP, AVIF | loads | loads |
| Garbage bytes, truncated PNG | 400 | 400 |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`: all hooks passed or were skipped.

No model evaluation was run. The change only affects images that fail to decode.

## Details

Pillow has no single base class for bad image data, so `load_bytes` lists the classes. The one added here covers what a fuzz run over the allowed formats found escaping that list, apart from `DecompressionBombError`:

- `RuntimeError` comes from the C AVIF decoder (`_avif.AvifDecoder`) in `Image.open()`.
- It also covers `NotImplementedError`, which Pillow plugins raise for format features they do not support (`BLPFormatError` is one), and `RecursionError` from deeply nested input.
- Every call in this block only decodes client-supplied bytes, so all of these are client errors and map to 400. A 501 in vLLM means the model does not support the API, which does not fit a bad image.

`MemoryError` is still not caught and still gives 500.

This PR and #60308 both extend the same tuple, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

title: [CI][ROCm] Skip the AITER MoE garbage-rows test for fp8 per-tensor until the AITER fix
author: AndreasKaratzas
body: - `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: skip `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows` for fp8 per-tensor configs until the AITER fix is in the pinned `AITER_BRANCH` `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows[single_inf-fp8_tensor_tensor]` and `[single_nan-fp8_tensor_token]` failed on MI300 in [amd-ci 15340](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15340) with `mean |mk_out| = 0`. The bug is in AITER, not vLLM: `fused_moe_2stages` allocates `a2` with `torch.empty`, stage 1 never writes the slots of `topk_ids == -1` rows, and the dynamic per-tensor a2 quant then takes its scale over that stale memory, which can push every real row to fp8 zero. Per-token and block schemes scale row by row and are unaffected, so only configs with fp8 per-tensor weights (which the test runs with no static a2 scale) are skipped. The AITER fix is ROCm/aiter#6568; this guard should be removed when `AITER_BRANCH` includes it. #62927 targets the same failure from the vLLM side but does not fix it (details in that PR). On MI350X with AITER v0.1.26, poisoning the caching allocator with 1e30 makes exactly the four skipped params fail (3/3 runs) while the other nine pass; nothing was run on MI300, where CI failed (1 failing nightly of ~10 since 2026-10-08). With the guard, the group runs 9 passed, 7 skipped. This adds a skip, which tests/AGENTS.md discourages; it is a temporary ROCm-only guard until the AITER bump, alongside the existing ROCm/aiter#6275 skip in the same test. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Guard NaN scores in gfx942 mono routing
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Overview

On gfx942, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--monokernel` and adaptive DSpark verification dies with `Memory access fault` during CUDA graph capture. The profile replays a context over KV blocks no request has written. The draft FFN then sees NaN router scores. `stage_route` ranks with `fx.max`, which keeps the NaN, so the same expert is picked twice and a later gather indexes off the slot table.

A NaN score now ranks last, and the winner ballot ignores lanes past the expert count. Both edits are in this patch. The KV fill is gone.

## Claims

- Without this patch, the serve command faults during the real capture and the server does not start.
- With both router edits and no KV zero, the real capture finishes and the server starts.
- Finite scores pick the same experts. TPOT on the shapes below stays with stock.
- No config or API change.

## Validation

MI325X, 4 GPUs, gfx942. The fault is on current main. The runs below are nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56` with main's Python over it, including this `stage_route`. The binaries were not rebuilt from this tree.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --monokernel --max-model-len 266240 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5],"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

| | without this patch | with this patch |
|---|---|---|
| real capture | `Memory access fault` on all four ranks after the DSpark graphs | finished in 60 s, 14.30 GiB |
| startup | engine core failed | `Application startup complete` |
| one completion | n/a | `Paris. The final answer is 123` |

Accuracy is a separate serve: monokernel, no speculative decoding. lm-eval `niah_single_1` at 4096, the first 8 of the 500 repeat-haystack samples. Stock and this patch both scored 1.0, and the 8 completions were identical.

Perf is that same serve, temperature 0, seed 0, 4 warmups. Mean / median TPOT:

| ISL / OSL / concurrency | prompts | stock | this patch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 / 128 / 4 | 64 | 5.43 / 5.23 ms | 5.42 / 5.23 ms |
| 1024 / 256 / 8 | 48 | 6.95 / 6.91 ms | 6.92 / 6.87 ms |
| 512 / 512 / 16 | 32 | 9.26 / 9.32 ms | 9.20 / 9.26 ms |

`stage_route` runs once per decode token. A longer prompt adds attention on every step, so these short prompts are where that cost can show up in TPOT. The output lengths are how many decode steps were averaged.

## Details

`batches_to_profile` is the only caller that passes a nonzero `context_len` into `_dummy_run`. `set_dummy_context` fills block tables with ids nobody has written, and the draft reads them. Two requests replay 10 tokens, the gfx942 monokernel's multi-tile draft FFN, and that launch faults.

`fx.max` keeps a NaN, and the NaN then compares equal to itself, so the draft shape emits the same expert id twice. The route counts winners with a bitmap, the count comes up short, and the gather reads off the slot table. Ranking the NaN as `-inf` after the max, and masking the ballot with `cursor < ept`, removes the duplicate. Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3 already drop NaN scores before ranking. The ballot mask is particular to this router, which holds 2 experts per lane and picks 3.

A local ranking check matches that. Unguarded draft NaN rows pick `[[0, 64, 0], [0, 64, 0]]`, bitmap 28 against 30 slots. With both edits the bitmap is 30 and there are no duplicates. Finite draft scores, and the target 384/6 shape, match with and without the guard. That check is the ranking logic, not the GPU kernel.

`stage_route` runs on every monokernel FFN launch, including target-only decode with adaptive verification off. The TPOT rows are that path.

Warmup and `profile_run` leave `context_len` at 0. `set_dcp_capture_context` is the other fabrication, only when `cp_size > 1`, and this PR does not change it.

`test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range` launches that draft shape with NaN logits. With this patch it finishes, and each token's ids are unique:

```text
.                                                                        [100%]
1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 7.91s
```

The same test against main's `moe.py`:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x44a297b0) on address 0x7ece472b5000. Reason: Unknown.
Fatal Python error: Aborted
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/accelerator/__init__.py", line 270 in synchronize
  File "/root/vllm/tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py", line 732 in test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range
EXIT:134
```

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Let decodes reuse divergent local hybrid prefix hits
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` does not opt into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` (#50344), so a hybrid-model decode (attention plus Mamba, GDN or KDA) drops its local attention hit and pulls the whole prompt from P every turn. This opts the `kv_consumer` role in, as MoRIIO READ and NIXL already do.

## Claims

- On a hybrid model, a Mooncake decode keeps its local attention prefix and pulls only the uncached suffix plus the recurrent state.
- `kv_producer` and `kv_both` keep the current lookup.

## Validation

- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, Mooncake RDMA, multi-turn agentic replay at concurrency 48: decode local prefix hit rate 0.0% to 93.9%; draft acceptance 58.78% to 58.79% (MoRIIO READ 58.79%).
- The new scheduler test fails on main and passes here. Mooncake unit tests: 164 passed. pre-commit clean.

<details><summary>Request flow, test output and serving numbers</summary>

Turn k of a session whose prompt extends turn k-1:

1. The router sends the request to P with `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and pushes KV.
2. On D, the attention blocks pulled in turn k-1 are still cached. Mamba has no state at any block boundary, since D never computes those positions.
3. Before: `get_computed_blocks` returns the hit every group shares, 0 tokens. Mooncake asks for N-1 tokens and pulls every attention block plus the state slot.
4. After: `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` returns the attention hit H. Mooncake asks for N-1-H tokens and pulls the suffix blocks plus the state slot; P pairs the last blocks of each group.
5. D decodes from the recurrent state P computed at N-1.

Unit test, on main and on this branch:

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py -k keeps_local_attention_prefix
# main
E       assert 6 == 2
E        +  where 6 = len([9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14])
FAILED ...::test_hybrid_gdn_remote_prefill_keeps_local_attention_prefix[kv_consumer-2]
1 failed, 1 passed, 11 deselected
# this branch
2 passed, 11 deselected

$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
164 passed
```

Serving, Kimi-K3 1P1D, decode flags `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'`, aiperf multi-turn agentic trace replay at concurrency 48. One run per column.

| Decode metric | Mooncake before | Mooncake after | MoRIIO READ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local prefix cache hit rate (log) | 0.0% | 93.9% | 91.2% |
| Prompt tokens, `local_cache_hit` / `external_kv_transfer` | 0 / 801.7M | not recorded | 731.3M / 70.9M |
| Draft acceptance | 58.78% | 58.79% | 58.79% |
| TTFT mean / p50, same request window | 2984 / 1727 ms | 3137 / 1730 ms | 2611 / 1365 ms |

The "after" run was cancelled by the cluster after 4598 requests, so it has no end-of-run Prometheus snapshot; its hit rate is the decode's periodic log line. MoRIIO's hit rate is `local_cache_hit` over all prompt tokens.

</details>

## Details

A decode never computes the block boundaries of a pulled prompt, so it caches attention blocks but no recurrent state. With the opt-in, the scheduler keeps the attention hit, and `update_state_after_alloc` already pulls every transfer group's unhashed blocks, the state slot included. With nothing to pull, the scheduler falls back to the reconciled lookup (#50344).

Only `kv_consumer` opts in: the per-group lookup reports a shared-prefix boundary of 0, which would disable junction checkpoints on roles that prefill locally.

Limitations:
- Serving runs used vLLM 81198e97 with this property forced to True on the decode, matching this PR; not re-run on main.
- Under `MultiConnector` every child must opt in until #63041.
- TTFT did not change on this workload.

Not a duplicate: the open Mooncake PRs (#53730, #63420, #63425) do not touch this property. AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used to write the change, the test and this description.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 vision crash with online FP8 quantization
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63732. With `--quantization fp8`, an image request to Gemma 4 returns HTTP 500 and kills the engine core. The transformers patch embedder casts the pixel values to `input_proj.weight.dtype`. Once vLLM quantizes that layer, this dtype is `float8_e4m3fn`, so the FP8 linear gets an FP8 input. This PR runs the patch embedder steps in `gemma4_mm.py` with the pixel values cast to `self.model_dtype`. It makes the same change for the pooled states before `embedding_projection` in the encoder CUDA graph path.

Compared with #63911, this fix:

- Also fixes `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model`. They borrow Gemma 4's `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` and build their own FP8-quantized tower. [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) swaps the embedder only in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.__init__`, so their image and video paths still crash with the reported error (checked with a probe that loads E4B with FP8 and builds each model's own tower, since no checkpoint of either model was at hand).
- Adds tests that fail on the old code for video and for the encoder CUDA graph path, including the `embedding_projection` cast. The compiled and encoder-graph cases in [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) pass on the old code, so they guard neither path.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image requests with online FP8 no longer crash the engine. `input_proj` stays FP8 and still uses the same FP8 kernel.
- The same fix covers video inputs. On the old code, `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` with video enabled crashed at engine start, because the encoder profile run sends dummy video through the same patch embedder.
- The same fix covers the encoder CUDA graph path (the patch embedder call and the `embedding_projection` cast).
- Online `fp8_per_block`, `fp8_per_channel` and `mxfp8` (eager, custom ops off) crashed at engine start on the old code. With this fix, all three answer `The sign in the image is a **STOP** sign.`
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model` get the same fix through the borrowed methods.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 1 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 16 GB (SM 12.0), vLLM `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`) with and without this patch, transformers 5.20.2.

Reproducer. Server:

```bash
vllm serve --port 18000 --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}'
```

Once it logs `Application startup complete`, send a 64x64 white PNG:

```bash
BODY='{"model":"google/gemma-4-E4B-it","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAAABACAIAAAAlC+aJAAAAS0lEQVR42u3PMQ0AAAwDoPo33UrYvQQckD4XAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAYHLAMpT0sIcNbcEAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"}},{"type":"text","text":"What color is this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":16}'
OUT=$(curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}' localhost:18000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY")
echo "$OUT"
echo "IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
```

Before (3 of 3 runs, each on a fresh server): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=500`. The server log shows:

```
RuntimeError: ... "dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant_kernel_scalar_type" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

After (6 of 6 runs, each on a fresh server: 3 by me and 3 in a separate re-check): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=200`, answer `"The image is **white**."`. No `not implemented`, `Traceback` or `EngineDeadError` line in any log. The server still selects `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod`. The old code gives the same answer only when `input_proj` is left out of FP8 with `--quantization-config '{"ignore":["vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj"]}'`.

New tests, on the old `gemma4_mm.py` and on this patch:

 | Test | Old code | This PR |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py -k gemma4` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k gemma4_fp8` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |

On the old code, the CUDA graph row fails earlier, in the eager video profile run. So I also checked each CUDA graph change on its own: with only the `encoder_cudagraph_forward` patch-embedder call reverted, or only the old `embedding_projection.weight.dtype` cast restored, the row fails with the same error.

Borrowing models: a script builds a vision tower with random weights from the E4B config (unquantized) and calls `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` on all three classes. Image and video outputs for all three match the old code exactly (same shapes and sums).

`pre-commit run` on the four changed files passes.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM builds the Gemma 4 vision tower with `AutoModel.from_config`. It then replaces each `nn.Linear` with a `ReplicatedLinear` that carries the tower quant config. With online FP8, `input_proj.weight` becomes `float8_e4m3fn` after loading. The transformers `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.forward` does:

```python
pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
if (target_dtype := self.input_proj.weight.dtype).is_floating_point:
    pixel_values = pixel_values.to(target_dtype)
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values)
```

This is right for a plain `nn.Linear`. For a quantized layer, though, the weight dtype is the storage dtype. FP8 is a floating type, so the guard lets the cast through. The bf16 pixel values are rounded to FP8 without a scale, and the FP8 linear's activation quant gets an FP8 input. `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` only accepts fp16, bf16 or fp32. A debug run confirmed the chain: the pixel values enter the patch embedder as bf16, and only `vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj` receives an FP8 input. `encoder_cudagraph_forward` had the same mistake in vLLM code: it cast the pooled states to `embedding_projection.weight.dtype`, which is also FP8 under the tower quant config.

The CUDA kernel runs when the `quant_fp8` custom op is on: with `--enforce-eager`, with `+quant_fp8`, and by vLLM's default for block-scaled FP8 checkpoints and ROCm AITER FP8 linear. With the op off, eager `forward_native` also fails (`"abs_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'`). Only the default compile mode passes without an error, and there the pixel values are still rounded to FP8 without a scale.

Fix: a module-level `_embed_patches(patch_embedder, pixel_values, pixel_position_ids, padding_positions, dtype)` repeats the steps of the transformers forward (`2 * (x - 0.5)`, `input_proj`, `_position_embeddings`, sum), but casts to the given dtype. The image, video and encoder CUDA graph paths call it with `self.model_dtype`. The CUDA graph path also casts the pooled states to `self.model_dtype`, as the eager paths already do before `embed_vision`. The quant config is not touched, so the layers stay FP8. For an unquantized layer nothing changes, because then the weight dtype is the model dtype. The helper is a module-level function, not a method, because the two borrowing models copy `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` without inheriting from Gemma 4. A method would be missing on those classes.

Alternatives not taken:

- Building `input_proj` without quantization: this changes which layers the user's quantization covers. It can also break loading of pre-quantized checkpoints that quantize this layer, and it leaves the `embedding_projection` cast as it is.
- Making the FP8 linear accept an FP8 input: this treats the crash site, and by then the input has already been rounded to FP8.

Tradeoffs and limitations:

- `_embed_patches` uses the private `_position_embeddings` of the transformers embedder. This file already splits `Gemma4VisionModel.forward` into its parts, so this goes one level deeper in the same style.
- With online FP8 in the default compile mode, which did not crash before, image outputs may change a little because the pixel values are no longer rounded to FP8 first. On `input_proj` against the bf16 weight, the relative error went from 4.50% to 3.68%. I did not run a vision eval.
- The tests use `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, which CI already uses. E2B has the same vision tower and would be cheaper, but I could not confirm the answer checks (`stop`, `book`) on E2B.
- CI: `gemma4_mm.py` is added to `source_file_dependencies` of `quantized-models-test` and its AMD mirror, so the eager test runs when this file changes. This adds an estimated 14% more runs of that step. The `gemma4_fp8` row (`core_model`) runs in the existing multimodal step.
- Not run on AMD.
- Out of scope: online `mxfp4` on SM 12.x fails at engine start in `input_proj` with `ValueError: SM12x cute-dsl requires NVFP4 with 128x4 scales`, the same before and after this patch, with a bf16 input.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix compact KV row regression tests
author: khluu
body:
## Summary

Fix the compact HiSparse KV-row tests added by #58305:

- stop patching `_create_side_stream` / `_create_event`, helpers removed by the platform-backend refactor before #58305 merged;
- construct the gather-prefill runtime with the parameterized KV dtype so FP8 `uint8` caches are bound to a `uint8` runtime instead of the default `float32` runtime;
- exercise staged-prefill backing through a real initialized runtime instead of calling the instance method with `self=None` after the gather path began using runtime cache ops.

## Failure evidence

Nightly main build #97886 and subsequent main builds through #98096 fail the exact H100 and B200 V1 Attention shards:

- `test_hisparse_index_group_preserves_row_width`: `AttributeError` for removed `_create_side_stream`;
- `test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows`: runtime expects `torch.float32` but receives the parameterized `torch.uint8` cache;
- `test_hisparse_staged_prefill_cache_backs_min_attention_rows`: `self=None` reaches `self.cache_ops` after the gather implementation changed.

The failures are deterministic test defects introduced by #58305, not failures in the unrelated later main commits.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- full file-scoped pre-commit suite for `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`
- first exact build #97912 proves the original two failure families pass; it exposed the third stale test call above
- updated exact H100 and B200 V1 Attention CI required before merge

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Fix KV-cache corruption under whole-graph compile (revert #42129)
author: ericschreiber
body:
## Overview

Implements solution 2 as outlined in issue #62865.
In more detail: fixes #62865 by reverting #42129 and, under torch < 2.13, keeps its intended hang protection by not formatting the slow log message for vLLM ops.
Currently using compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []` on Transformers-backend models corrupts the KV cache because Inductor passes tensors in a different layout than the kernels assume. As discussed with maintainers and @okorzh-amd (author of #42129) in Slack, this is the revert-based alternative to #62924.

## Claims

- Fixes degenerate output for Transformers-backend models (e.g. Qwen3, Kolibri-1, likely others) under compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []`.
- It does so by restoring PyTorch's default handling for all `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` custom ops.
- Keeps the compile-hang protection from #42129 through: (1) from torch 2.13 the slow log message is only built with INFO logging; (2) below 2.13 (currently only the gfx1250 preview image) the message is never built for `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` ops, the same ops #42129 covered.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, torch 2.13.0+cu130, precompiled kernels. All runs with vLLM and Inductor compile caches disabled.

### Correctness
**1. Regression test** 
Added a new test `test_whole_graph_compile` which uses Qwen3-0.6B on the Transformers backend on compile mode 2 vs eager with `check_logprobs_close`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_whole_graph_compile -v
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | failed: `Matched tokens: []`, ref `'LLM is a large language model, ...'`, test `'>>1\n\n\n\n...'` |
| this PR | passed 2 runs|

**2. GSM8K** 
With this PR, mode 2 matches eager and the native implementation on GSM8K (Qwen3-0.6B, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`); while on main there is a clear regression.

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| Transformers backend, eager | 0.391 | 0.3% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, `main` | 0.011 | 10.8% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, this PR | 0.401 | 0.2% |
| native vLLM implementation, default mode 3 | 0.400 | 0.2% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 2, "backend": "inductor", "cudagraph_mode": 2}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

**3. Bounded log message for vLLM ops under torch < 2.13**
Introduced a test `tests/compile/test_inductor_operator_str_patch.py` which checks that a `vllm::` op's message is only its name. Running on torch 2.12 (CPU, a small compiled graph with a `vllm::` op and a custom op from another namespace), unpatched torch builds the full message for both ops; with the patch it is never built for the `vllm::` op. 
I could not test on gfx1250 itself.

### Compile time
On CUDA, cold-cache compile time is unchanged within noise (`main` vs this PR): Kolibri-1 mode 3 28.3 vs 28.1 s, Kolibri-1 TP=2 61.1 vs 62.1 s, Qwen3-4B mode 3 19.4 vs 19.5 s.

On ROCm, @djramic reported on Slack that without the #42129 allow-list the Kimi-K2 arch (dummy weights, torch 2.13) compiles about as fast as before. I had no ROCm access to verify this myself.

## Details

**Root cause:** #42129 added every `vllm::*` and `vllm_aiter::*` op to Inductor's `FALLBACK_ALLOW_LIST`. Inductor creates fallbacks for allow-listed ops without PyTorch's default layout constraint for custom ops. Without it, Inductor passes `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` a head-major key, strides `(128, 128*S, 1)` instead of eager's `(1024, 128, 1)`. `reshape_and_cache_flash` only reads `key.stride(0)` and assumes packed heads, so every cached key is scrambled and the output is garbage. Default mode 3 is unaffected because it splits the graph at the attention and KV-cache ops.

**Why revert:** The allow-list only existed to skip an implicit-fallback INFO message that torch <= 2.12 builds eagerly, which hung compilation on deep MoE/TP graphs. pytorch/pytorch#185951 makes it lazy from torch 2.13, and CUDA, CPU, XPU and the default ROCm images are on >= 2.13. Reverting restores PyTorch's behavior for all vLLM ops. #62924's own control row (allow-list disabled) already gives token-identical output to its patched run. The allow-list cannot stay for torch < 2.13 either, because the layout bug is in that code path on every torch version; those versions only need the hang protection, which skipping the message for vLLM ops provides.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- The torch < 2.13 patch can be removed once every platform pins torch >= 2.13. Until then, Inductor messages for vLLM ops (including lowering errors) show only the op name on those versions, as with #42129.
- On torch >= 2.13 with Inductor's graph logger at INFO, the full message is still built and can be slow on very deep graphs (`IRNode.__str__` has no depth limit, as #43111 found). This is opt-in debug logging.
- Overlaps with #57310, whose allow-list change should become unnecessary.
- A follow-up PR could make the KV-cache writers (reshape_and_cache, reshape_and_cache_flash and their Triton versions) reject keys whose heads are not packed, so a future layout change raises an error instead of silently corrupting the cache.

title: [Bugfix] Flashinfer attention warmup deadlock under PP>1
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Overview

Fix a deadlock during Flashinfer attention warmup under PP>1.

## Claims

Fix a deadlock that occurs when one PP rank contains only Flashinfer attention groups while another PP rank contains a mix of Flashinfer and non-Flashinfer attention groups.

Most commonly affects models with dflash / dspark drafters on Blackwell, where Flashsinfer is often the default attention backend for the target model.

## Validation

Ran on B200:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":2,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

On this PR, we get
```
INFO:     Started server process [771742]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

On main, we get stuck after
```
EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:46:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
(EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:47:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
```

`--enforce-eager` doesn't resolve this because Flashinfer attention warmup is run regardless of enforce eager and compilation mode.

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` doesn't resolve this because it controls Flashinfer autotuning, not Flashinfer attention warmup.

```
pytest -v -s \
  tests/model_executor/test_attention_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py

99 passed, 2 warnings
```

## Details

During `kernel_warmup`, we may call `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` to run "a mixed prefill+decode batch to warm up both attention paths".

This is currently gated under "all attention groups use the Flashinfer backend" because hybrid attention backends may not support the dummy run.

With spec decode, the drafter may choose a different attention backend than the target model. Since the drafter is present on the last PP rank only, different ranks will disagree on whether they should participate in the Flashinfer warmup, causing deadlock.

The current fix synchronizes across PP ranks and only runs the Flashinfer attention warmup if all ranks agree. In effect, warmup behavior is consistent between PP=1 and PP>1.

Related:
- #60791 tracks issues with MiniMax-M3. Item 8 lists "PP where stages differ in running the M3 attention warmup". M3 warmup also uses `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` but it's separate from Flashinfer warmup.

---

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Preserve KV cache zeroing when mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups are reduced for the scheduler. Resolve the zeroing decision across workers so pipeline stages agree even when only one stage has mixed precision. Split out of #63232 (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash); this change remains independent of the other split PRs.

## Claims

- Scheduler projection preserves the decision to zero newly allocated attention blocks.
- All PP workers initialize zeroing when any worker requires it. This prevents MRV2 from receiving zeroing work on a stage without a zeroer.
- Uniform-precision attention-only configurations continue to skip zeroing.

## Validation

The same regression tests were run on original PR head `998f165a2ab0ce47f63ff280b96a600901c7d914` and this revision.

| Check | Original PR head | This revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config matrix: uniform, mixed first stage, mixed second stage | 1 passed, 2 failed (`False is True` on a uniform worker) | 3 passed |
| Related scheduler, Mamba, and PP config tests | Not rerun | 7 passed |
| Qwen3-0.6B, MRV2, PP=2, FP8 KV, BF16 layer 0 | Worker_PP1 asserted that `kv_block_zeroer` is not None; first completion returned HTTP 500 | 1 passed; PP=2 and PP=1 first-token top-5 logprobs match at the helper's precision |
| Pre-commit on the seven changed files | Not rerun | Passed |

CPU commands (with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config_keeps_zeroing -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  -k 'test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config or test_wrapped_mamba_group_requires_block_zeroing or test_get_kv_cache_configs_pp_sharding' -q
```

GPU command, run through Slurm with two visible GB200 GPUs and cached real weights (before: job 40854, 1 failed; after: job 40859, 1 passed in 171.17 s):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py \
  -k test_pp_mixed_precision_kv_cache -v -s --tb=short
```

The regression compares PP=2 against PP=1 using the existing `generate_close` helper: greedy first-token top-5 logprobs rounded to two decimal places. Both revisions use the same existing native build. This validates the Python configuration/zeroing path with Qwen, not MiniMax native operators or model accuracy on a benchmark. No performance claim is made.

The E2E test is included in the existing pipeline/context parallelism CI steps, with dependencies added for the changed core files. NVIDIA coverage is in the existing optional nightly step; AMD coverage uses its existing PR step. AMD was not run locally.

## Details

`generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` reduces each `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` to one layer spec. Recomputing mixed precision after that reduction loses information. Saving only worker 0's mixed-precision result also leaves PP workers inconsistent: a uniform stage skips zeroer initialization although it receives the scheduler's `new_block_ids_to_zero`.

`has_mixed_precision_kv_cache` remains a local fact. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` becomes a stored execution decision, initialized from each worker's full configuration. The planner ORs that decision across workers after final replanning, and scheduler projection preserves it through deepcopy. The tradeoff is that uniform stages also zero new attention blocks when another stage requires zeroing.

This extends the metadata-preservation fix in #49623 to intra-group precision and PP worker agreement. It is not a duplicate of the open fixes for transfer destinations/tails (#62313, #55085), backend-specific block reuse (#58716), or initial allocation zero fill (#59432).

AI assistance was used: Claude for the original split, and OpenAI Codex for this follow-up implementation, regression tests, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pin FlashKDA and FlashMLA with NaN fixes
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64758: under load, some Kimi-K3 requests turn into streams of token 0 (`!!!!`) until `max_tokens`. This PR moves the FlashKDA and FlashMLA pins to commits with two kernel fixes: https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/16 and https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/pull/41.

Both kernel PRs are merged, and the pins point to their upstream merge commits.

## Claims

- FlashKDA prefill no longer copies a NaN from one request into other requests of the same batch. On Kimi-K3 with one injected NaN request, other decodes made bad drop from 96/240 to 0/240.
- FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel now waits for the previous kernel (PDL) before it reads the query. A forced race gives NaN in 49/50 calls on stock and 0/50 with the fix.
- On the natural burst reproducer from the issue, bad requests went from 14 on stock to 0 with both fixes.
- No measurable end-to-end performance cost on Kimi-K3.

## Validation

All runs: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` @ `f831ab66`, 2 x 8 H200, TP8 x PP2 over InfiniBand, V2 model runner, stock flags from the issue, vLLM `063c0c6` (PR #61867 head). The fixes were applied by swapping only `_flashkda_C` and `_flashmla_C`.

Burst reproducer (`repro_natural_burst.py` in the issue), fresh server per arm, same seed:

| | Stock | FlashKDA fix | FlashKDA fix + FlashMLA fix (no-PDL variant) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run length | 12.5 min | 10.8 min | 25.0 min |
| First-NaN events | 2 | 1 | 0 (about 2.6 expected, P about 0.08) |
| Bad requests | 14 (groups of 2 and 13) | 1 | 0 |

The last arm used the FlashMLA variant that launches without PDL. The `griddepcontrol.wait` variant pinned here was checked with the forced kernel race (49/50 to 0/50, bit-identical outputs) and in the performance A/B below, but not on the burst reproducer.

With one NaN injected into one request by a debug hook, stock made 96 of 240 other decodes bad and the FlashKDA fix made 0. GSM8K was 0.945 on stock and 0.947 with the fix.

Performance, stock against both fixes, one server start per arm:

| Metric | Stock | Both fixes | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| TPOT, batch 1 (ms) | 15.51 | 15.50 | -0.1% |
| TPOT, batch 8 (ms) | 26.38 | 26.31 | -0.2% |
| TPOT, batch 32 (ms) | 44.20 (0.86) | 45.00 (1.3) | +1.8%, within noise |
| TPOT, batch 64 (ms) | 58.17 (3.4) | 59.38 (4.6) | +2.1%, within noise |
| TTFT, 1k-token prompt (ms) | 225.9 | 222.4 | -1.6% |
| TTFT, 8k-token prompt (ms) | 858.2 | 858.7 | +0.1% |
| TTFT, 64k-token prompt (ms) | 5046 | 5054 | +0.2% |
| GSM8K (5-shot) | 0.947 | 0.948 | +0.1% |

Each value is the median of 3 repetitions; brackets give the max-min spread where it matters. Both arms use `-O3 -DNDEBUG` builds whose SASS is identical to the wheel's; the only difference is the two patches. Three repetitions can neither show nor rule out a 1-2% cost at batch 32-64.

Decode: random 32-token prompts, 1,024 output tokens with `ignore_eos`, greedy, 4/16/64/128 prompts at concurrency 1/8/32/64. Prefill: `vllm bench serve` with random 1k/8k/64k-token prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, median TTFT. GSM8K: 5-shot, greedy, 1,319 questions, once per arm.

Kernel-level reproducers and tests are in the two kernel PRs.

## Details

**Spread (confirmed): FlashKDA.** Prefill works in chunks of 16 rows. For a sequence's last, partial chunk, it read `beta` and `v` from the rows after the sequence end (the next request in the batch, or the next head) and cancelled them by multiplying by zero. `0 * NaN` is NaN. vLLM runs the decode rows of a mixed step through this kernel together with the prefills, so one NaN request could hit up to 15 decodes and one prefill per step. The fix selects 0 for those rows.

**First NaN (strong suspect, not proven): FlashMLA.** K3's decode path runs `fused_kimi_k3_mla_decode_q_concat_kv_cache_insert`, which writes the query and triggers PDL completion, then FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel. That kernel is launched with PDL but never called `griddepcontrol.wait`, so it could read a query buffer (`torch.empty`) that was not written yet. The fix adds the wait after the prologue. We have not shown that this race causes the natural events; one natural event appeared after the attention output, which it does not explain.

Pin contents:

- FlashKDA: `47fc9fe` (current pin, on upstream `dev`) to `9d9e928`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#16. No other upstream change comes in.
- FlashMLA: `d1a1c92` (current pin) to `847ef30` on upstream `main`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashMLA#41. It also brings vllm-project/FlashMLA#39, a one-line fix per kernel in the SM100 sparse decode head64 kernels.

Scope and limits:

- The FlashMLA change affects every model that uses the SM90 dense decode kernel, not only Kimi-K3. It adds one wait per CTA and leaves outputs bit-identical. We only measured Kimi-K3.
- CI cannot run Kimi-K3 (two 8 x H200 nodes). The validation above was done outside CI.
- vLLM code is unchanged; only the two pins in `cmake/external_projects/` move.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix KV-sharing fast prefill hang from unsynchronized host offsets
author: hojuna
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64985. Under async scheduling, `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` can hand the attention metadata builders a `query_start_loc_cpu` whose device-to-host copy has not finished yet. The trtllm-gen decode kernel then receives a garbage query length and hangs.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: `query_start_loc_cpu` from `make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata` now always holds final values.
- No new sync on the common path. With one logit per request (no speculative decoding), the host offsets are built with `torch.arange` instead of being copied.
- Adds a regression test that fails on `main` and passes with this change.

## Validation

**Unit test** `tests/v1/attention/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_metadata.py`. The CUDA case keeps the stream busy and reads the host offsets without a sync, the way the builders do.

```
# base
E       assert [0, 4, 7, 8, 10] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
E       assert [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] == [0, 2, 3, 6, 7]
2 failed, 6 passed
# this PR
8 passed
```

**End-to-end.** Setup: B200, Gemma 4 E4B fine-tune (bf16), `vllm serve --kv-sharing-fast-prefill --enable-prefix-caching -cc '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, MRV2, async scheduling on. The workload replays `/v1/completions` requests (`max_tokens=1`, 96 concurrent).

| run | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4,649-request slice | hangs (4/4 runs) | completes, 20 s |
| full 31,649 requests | hangs | completes, 105 s |

Pre-commit (ruff check/format) passes locally.

**Review follow-up (9c5b0d7, rebased on main).** `arange` now uses `device="cpu"`. Added `[1, 1, 1, 0]` (a request with no logits) and `[2, 1, 1, 0]` (`num_logits_indices == num_reqs` with `max_logits_per_req > 1`) so each branch condition is tested on its own, plus a CUDA test under `torch.device("cuda")`. CPU run: `5 passed, 3 skipped (CUDA)`. Removing either branch condition makes exactly one of the new cases fail. The CUDA cases were not re-run in this round (no GPU available right now); the earlier CUDA results above are unchanged code paths. Only `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` were run locally, not the full official pre-commit.

## Details

`decode_query_start_loc` is computed on the GPU, and its host copy was made with `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`. The builders read it on the host right away:

- `split_decodes_and_prefills`
- FlashInfer `_compute_decode_query_lens`

With async scheduling the copy sits behind in-flight GPU work, so the host reads unfinished memory. Instrumentation is in the issue. The bug reproduces on MRV1 and MRV2 and with both PIECEWISE and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE.

The change:

- **One logit per request** (`max_logits_per_req == 1` and `num_logits_indices == num_reqs`): the offsets are `[0, 1, ..., num_reqs]`, built on the host directly.
- **Otherwise** (speculative decoding with fast prefill, e.g. #63553): use a blocking copy. Correctness requires the values now. A sync-free alternative would pass the host-side per-request logits counts from the model runner (MRV2 already has `cu_num_logits_np` in `FastPrefillHelper.prepare`). I kept that out of this fix to avoid touching `CommonAttentionMetadata` and the runners, and I'm happy to follow up.

Relation to #60445: it builds the same one-logit host offsets with `arange`, so that path overlaps. Its multi-logit fallback still uses `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`, which has the same race. This PR makes the fallback safe to read immediately and adds regression tests for both paths, so it is worth merging on its own; whichever lands second can drop the duplicate one-logit branch.
