title: [Bugfix] Fix startup illegal memory access from unaligned extensible KV cache segments
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview Fix a startup illegal memory access in FlashMLA sparse prefill with the extensible KV cache (#56492), reproduced with DeepSeek-V3.2 on B300. FlashInfer autotuning runs FlashMLA before warmup expands the cache. When a sparse gather includes an invalid (padding) index, FlashMLA reads past the selected rows. With only the null block committed, those reads can reach unmapped memory inside the layer's reserved KV view. This PR extends the segment alignment introduced in #65225 to caches without an RDMA connector, and commits a second block at allocation for block-outermost layouts (follow-up commit by Nick Hill). ## Claims - Prevents the reproduced startup crash by keeping memory mapped beyond each layer's initial KV rows. - Covers block-compact, layer-outermost layouts and block-outermost layouts. - Preserves logical KV capacity and block strides. ## Validation ### End-to-end The segment-alignment fix was validated with DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8) on 8×B300, using EP + TP2 + DP2 + PP2, eager execution, and prefix caching disabled. Settings: `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=64`, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`. Each startup test used an empty `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` to exercise autotuning. | Check | main | With segment alignment | Extensible KV cache disabled | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Startup | Illegal memory access in 3/3 runs | Pass | Pass | | GSM8K accuracy, 250 questions | — | 0.884 | 0.880 | | 32 requests with 4096-token prompts | — | 32/32 succeed | 32/32 succeed | ### Regression coverage - Engine initialization without a KV connector verifies that per-layer segments are granule-aligned. - Block-outermost allocation tests verify mapped memory beyond the last layer's view start. - A FlashMLA kernel regression test exercises the newly allocated cache with both `LBNHC` and `BLNHC` layouts, using offsets that would otherwise expose unmapped memory. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \ "tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py::test_sparse_flashmla_prefill_on_the_kv_cache_at_allocation" ``` All 70 tests pass on B300; with only the test changes applied on main, 6 fail. The FlashMLA test needs SM100 and is skipped on the H100 CI runner; it was run on B300 and, by Nick Hill, on GB300.
Kernel reproduction On one GPU, place a bf16 KV view near a granule boundary and commit only block 0 (73,728 bytes). The minimum mapped size depends on the indices: | Inputs | Faults when mapped bytes from the view's start are below | |---|---| | Valid indices inside block 0, padded with `-1`, as in the failing startup | Up to about 130 KiB, depending on the query row | | All indices `-1`, `topk_length=0` | Approximately 100 KiB | | All indices valid | No over-read detected | Views fully contained in committed memory do not fault in these tests. The rows above combine our B300 measurements with Nick Hill's on GB300. The following reproduces the all-invalid-indices case: ```python import torch from vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface import flash_mla_sparse_fwd from vllm.utils.extensible_tensor import ExtensibleTensor BLOCK, D, HQ, TOPK, SQ, G = 64, 576, 64, 2048, 128, 2 << 20 room = 81408 # Mapped bytes from the KV view's start to the granule boundary. dev = torch.device("cuda") q = torch.randn(SQ, HQ, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) indices = torch.full((SQ, 1, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) topk_length = torch.zeros(SQ, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) offset, view_bytes = 4 * G - room, 1024 * BLOCK * D * 2 buf = ExtensibleTensor( offset + view_bytes, device=dev, segment_capacities=[offset, view_bytes], ) buf.resize_segments_([0, BLOCK * D * 2], zero_new=True) kv = buf.full_view()[offset:].view(torch.bfloat16).view(-1, 1, D) flash_mla_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, D**-0.5, topk_length=topk_length) torch.cuda.synchronize() # Illegal memory access: only 81,408 bytes are mapped. ```
## Details The allocator previously committed only block 0 while exposing each layer's full reserved KV view. FlashMLA's SM100 sparse prefill kernel reads past the rows selected by the sparse indices when a TMA gather includes an invalid index: about 100 KiB from the view start when every index is invalid, and up to about 130 KiB when only some are. In the failing startup, `model.layers.17` had a 72 KiB null block and only 80,128 mapped bytes from its view start, less than the roughly 128 KiB the kernel read there. The fix handles the two layouts differently: - **Block-compact, layer-outermost:** align each layer's segment to a memory granule, so committing the null block maps the full first granule. This reuses the existing RDMA padding path. Padding increases reserved address space without adding physical memory, since each segment's commits already map whole granules. - **Block-outermost:** layers share one segment, and their views start at different offsets within block 0. Committing two blocks keeps at least half a granule (1 MiB on the tested device) mapped beyond each layer's view start, well above the roughly 130 KiB FlashMLA reads. This can increase the initial physical mapping; logical KV capacity is unchanged. Layouts that are neither, such as `LHBNC`, keep the current allocation; forcing `LHBNC` with sparse MLA can still fault. This keeps the allocation policy independent of a hard-coded FlashMLA access size. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the crash, write the change and tests, and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations listed above. ---

title: [Bugfix] Fix DP ViT all-gather dtype mismatch when the first parameter is fp32
author: micah-wil
body:
## Summary

With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, ranks that get no images all-gather placeholder embeddings whose dtype comes from `next(vision_model.parameters())`. Since #64111, MiniMax-M3 keeps its patch embedding in fp32 while the tower outputs bf16. Ranks with images then gather bf16 and ranks without gather fp32, so the all-gather mismatches and startup hangs.

This uses the vision model's `dtype` attribute when it has one, and falls back to the first parameter's dtype otherwise. Other models are unchanged: their `dtype` either matches the first parameter or isn't defined.

## Test plan

- `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` with `-tp 4 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data` now starts and serves image requests. Before the fix, it hung after the encoder profile run.
- Ongoing coverage comes from the nightly MiniMax-M3 evals, which run with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

title: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. The rest then has to be rescued one site at a time: buffers by name, and everything held some other way is lost. With this change `sleep(level=2)` states what the caller rewrites and keeps the rest, at the same address. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F11).

This replaces this PR's earlier site-by-site fixes (MXFP4 permute cache, DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load`, GEMM-RS/AR), which are reverted here because the rule covers them.

## Failures this addresses

All come from non-parameter state in the weights pool. Measured on GB200 without any fix:

| State | How it is held | Failure after a level-2 wake |
|---|---|---|
| GEMM-RS/AR peer pointer table from `symm_mem.rendezvous` | Inside the torch handle | Table reads all zeros, then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` on the first forward. Kimi-K3 placeholder weights, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with GEMM-RS |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load` indices | Weight loader closure | GSM8K 0.90 → 0.0, and later reloads don't repair it |
| MXFP4 TRT-LLM permute cache | Quant method attribute | gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.375 → 0.0 |

The same pattern is in code but not measured: Inkling and Beam peer tables, DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram handles (#64922), plain attributes (#60009), attention impl state (#62634).

## Change

- `CuMemAllocator.sleep` and `XpuMemAllocator.sleep` take `discardable`: a weights allocation is discarded only if every live block in it starts at an address in `discardable`. An address that doesn't match keeps the allocation, so a wrong match costs host memory, not state.
- `Worker.sleep(level=2)` passes the storage addresses of the parameters the update rewrites, through `SleepModeBackend.suspend(discardable)`. That replaces `level`, which said the same thing: nothing discardable is level 1. It changes a plugin interface, so an out-of-tree backend must follow.

Kept tensors stay in `weights` and return on `wake_up(["weights"])`, so tags keep their meaning. Level 1 is unchanged.

## Removed

These existed to survive level 2, which now keeps them:

- Model state in the runtime pool (#63548), LoRA state in the runtime pool (#62358), and the MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill workspace in the runtime pool (#64856). All three are built during `load_model`; none is a parameter.
- The CPU copies of `named_buffers()`, on every platform.
- The separate CPU save and restore of `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`. Preserved parameters are now just not discardable, so their backup goes through the allocator: pinned where `PIN_MEMORY` is on, instead of pageable, and kept across wake for reuse.

Left in place: buffers registered for this reason (they are still correct as buffers), and the KV-init and CUDA graph runtime pools, which are outside `load_model`.

## Not covered

- Parameters the update doesn't write, such as those absent from the checkpoint: still discarded, as today. `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` is for those.
- `discard(tags)`: unchanged. Its only caller passes `kv_cache`.
- Weight-derived tensors that post-load processing doesn't refresh now keep old values instead of garbage. That is a separate bug class.


## Validation

Every run is the RL cycle: `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`. Nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions unless noted. Code at 33056538ad and e82bcb85c4; later commits change only docs and comments and merge main.

**Weights over NCCL, through the state-transition verifier.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, TP4, 2 updates, every tensor sent except the Engram embedding tables. The fixed-token oracle compares logprobs before and after.

| Code | GSM8K before → after | Oracle | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9007 → **0.0** | Differs | 28331 |
| Earlier site-by-site fixes | 0.9045 → 0.9037 | Same | 28323 |
| | 0.9030 → 0.9067 | Same | 28329 |
| This PR | 0.9067 → 0.8923 | Same | 28322 |
| | 0.9022 → 0.9098 | Same | 28327 |
| | 0.9007 → 0.8984 | Same | 28328 |

Across the three runs of this PR GSM8K moves -1.44, +0.76 and -0.23 points. The noise between identical runs here is about 1.5 points.

**Reload from disk**, GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 3 cycles. "Differing" compares tensors per rank with a real cold start.

| Model | Code | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | This PR, real start | 0.9052 → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| | This PR, dummy start | — → 0.9030 → 0.9014 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | main | 0.9022 → **0.0** → **0.0** | 160 / 160 experts | 46346 |
| | This PR | 0.9083 → 0.8976 → 0.8931 | 0 / 160 experts | 46345 |
| Beam NVFP4 | main | 0.9431, then **hangs**: `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` | — | 46339 |
| | This PR | 0.9447 → 0.9439 → 0.9454 | 0 / 1224 all parameters | 46338 |
| MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 | main | 0.166 → 0.166 → 0.190 | 0 / 2150 all parameters | 46337 |
| | This PR | 0.175 → 0.187 → 0.178 | 0 / 2150 all parameters | 46336 |
| Kimi-K3 8-layer placeholder, GEMM-AR on | main | Illegal address on the first forward | — | 46016 |
| | This PR | Values are fake, so not meaningful | 0 / 358 all parameters | 46268 |

The dummy start is also an update between different weights: state derived from random weights would stay stale and lower GSM8K. MiniMax-M3 scores low on main too, so its run only shows no regression from removing the MSA runtime pool. The Beam hang is one run per arm, and its cause isn't diagnosed.

**LoRA with no reload, the flows #62358 fixed.** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with a real adapter, GB300, TP 1 and 2, waking all at once or weights before KV cache, 2 cycles. Output compared token by token with before sleep, with and without the adapter. `inplace` preserves nothing and has user code write every parameter back.

| Code | `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]` | `inplace` | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | Same | Same | 28336 |
| This PR | Same | Same | 28334 |
| Negative control: this PR, discarding the whole weights pool | Same | **Differs**, 4 of 4 | 28335 |

**ROCm,** MI355X, reload from disk, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, 3 cycles: this PR 0.9469 → 0.9477 → 0.9500 (34144), main 0.9500 → 0.9492 → 0.9500 (34145). That path doesn't hit the failures above on main, so this shows no regression and that the pool snapshot works on ROCm. `test_cumem.py` 22 passed, and `test_sleep_mode.py -k deep_sleep` 9 passed (34143).

**What level 2 backs up to host memory,** per rank:

| Model | GPU memory freed | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 80.35 GiB | 0.97 GiB | 2.35 GiB |
| Beam NVFP4 | 70.15 GiB | 0.39 GiB | 1.55 GiB |
| Kimi-K3 placeholder | 34.94 GiB | 0.30 GiB | 1.14 GiB |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MI355X | 40.81 GiB | 0.10 GiB | 1.87 GiB |

**Tests,** GB200 and GB300, 2 GPUs: `test_cumem.py` 22 passed; `test_sleep_mode.py` and `test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py` 20 passed, 1 skipped, including LoRA and the multimodal models; `tests/lora` manager, worker and layers 263 passed, 168 skipped; `tests/v1/worker` and the MiniMax-M3 MSA kernel tests 115 passed, 3 skipped. `test_level2_keeps_what_the_update_does_not_rewrite` and `test_deep_sleep_keeps_preserved_parameters` are new. The backup check in `test_cumem.py` is updated for what level 2 now keeps.

**Not run:** XPU, full Kimi-K3, Inkling and MiniMax-M3 at the verifier level. AMD CI is blocked waiting for approval. The `sleep_mode.md` section was read cold by an agent twice and corrected from what it couldn't answer.

title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by unresolved autorefs
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Overview

The strict MkDocs build (Read the Docs, `fail_on_warning: true`) has been failing on `main` since 2026-11-05 with `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`. Every PR's docs check fails with the same warnings, e.g. builds [35688234](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688234/) (`main` at `e336407a3d`) and [35688313](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688313/). This PR fixes the docstrings behind those warnings. No code behavior changes.

## Claims

- The strict docs build passes again. All 12 `mkdocs_autorefs: Could not find cross-reference target` warnings are gone.
- The only changes are docstrings. No code changes.

## Validation

Ran the same command as Read the Docs, with `requirements/docs.txt` installed in a clean venv:

```bash
uv venv -p 3.12 /tmp/docs-venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/docs-venv uv pip install -r requirements/docs.txt
/tmp/docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --site-dir /tmp/docs-site --config-file mkdocs.yaml --strict
```

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`e336407a3d`) | Exit 1, `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`, the same 12 warnings as Read the Docs build 35688234 |
| This PR | Exit 0, `Documentation built in 178.18 seconds`, no warnings |

## Details

There are two root causes.

**1. MiniMax-M3.1 drafter docstrings (11 warnings), from #65386.**
- Some docstrings write array shapes as consecutive brackets, such as `red[8 t + wave][row][token]`, `x [16][K]`, `x_in [rows][6144]`, `x8[t][16 tid ..]`, `xs8[t][tid / 2]` and `o [112][128]`.
- Markdown parses `[a][b]` as a reference-style link, so autorefs tries to resolve `b` (`row`, `K`, `6144`, `16 tid ..`, `tid / 2`, `128`) and fails.
- Fix: wrap these shapes in code spans in `drafter/device.py` (`red_store`, `xq_chunk`, `row_x`, `quant_store`) and `drafter/attention.py` (`store_partial`). Single brackets such as `[1, rank, site]` are not affected, so they are left as is.

**2. `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` lost its docstring (1 warning), from #54109.**
- #54109 renamed the documented class to `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModularBase`, then added new `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular` subclasses without docstrings.
- mkdocstrings skips objects without a docstring by default, so the API page has no anchor for `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. The link in `docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md` then cannot resolve.
- Fix: give both subclasses a one-line docstring that names their activation quantization, so both get API anchors. The docs link stays as it is, because it names the concrete experts class.

title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by subclassing mocked torch classes
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

The strict docs build on main has failed since #65235 with `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand` and `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'PydanticMagicMock'` ([main build at #65235](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35689810/)). Every main build since then fails the same way. PRs that change docs fail too, while PRs without docs changes skip the build.

## Claims

- Fixes the strict docs build. The argparse docs generator imports every CLI subcommand again, including `vllm preload`.
- Generated CLI and engine-args pages are unchanged.

## Validation

`mkdocs build --strict` in a docs-only environment, as on Read the Docs (`requirements/docs.txt`, Python 3.12, no torch):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .docs-venv
uv pip install --python .docs-venv/bin/python -r requirements/docs.txt
.docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --strict --config-file mkdocs.yaml --site-dir /tmp/site
```

| `generate_argparse.py` | Result |
|---|---|
| main | exit 1, `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand`, same `TypeError` as the Read the Docs log |
| this PR | exit 0, all CLI pages built, including `cli/preload` |

## Details

- Root cause: `TraceTensor` subclasses `torch.Tensor`, which is mocked in the docs build. Subclassing a mock produced a mock instance rather than a class, and `@dataclass` then failed on the `Copy.src: TraceTensor` annotation in `reload/bake.py`.
- Fix: `PydanticMagicMock.__mro_entries__` gives any class inheriting from a mock a real `MockBase` base, so it is a real type. `MockBase` supports pydantic schemas and subscripting (for `cachetools.LRUCache[_K, _V]`). `torch.nn` now uses `PydanticMagicMock`, so `nn.*` subclasses are covered too.
- Validated with `mkdocs build --strict` on current main without torch: exit 0, no warnings. Compared with the previous fix, the page set is identical. `cli/bench/serve` differs only in its random `--result-filename` default and the order of a `set` of choices.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `generate_argparse.py` or this failure. #66044 fixed unrelated cross-reference warnings.
